3.20.2.a.m: [He touches] his limbs according to the characteristic marks [in the mantra] with “Speech in my mouth…”;

3.20.4.a.s: prakṣālya pātraṃ pūrayitvā diśo jinveti parācinaṃ ninayati
3.20.4.a.d: प्रक्षाल्य पात्रं पूरयित्वा दिशो जिन्वेति पराचिनं निनयति
3.20.4.a.m: Having washed the vessel and filled it, he pours it away from himself with “Invigorate the quarters!”;

3.20.6.a.s: yatrāsmai brahmabhāgamāharati taṃ pratigṛhya nāsaṃsthite bhakṣayati
3.20.6.a.d: यत्रास्मै ब्रह्मभागमाहरति तं प्रतिगृह्य नासंस्थिते भक्षयति
3.20.6.a.m: When he brings the brahman's portion to him, having received it, he does not partake of it until [the ritual] is concluded.

3.20.7.a.s: brahmanbrahmāsi brahmaṇe tvāhutādya mā mā hiṃsīrahuto mahyaṃ śivo bhavetyantarvedyanvāhāryamāsannamabhimṛśati
3.20.7.a.d: ब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मासि ब्रह्मणे त्वाहुताद्य मा मा हिंसीरहुतो मह्यं शिवो भवेत्यन्तर्वेद्यन्वाहार्यमासन्नमभिमृशति
3.20.7.a.m: With “O brahman, you are Brahman; for Brahman to you, the consumer of the oblation; do not injure me! Free from injury, be propitious to me!” he touches the anvāhārya cooked rice set down inside the altar ground.

3.20.8.a.s: brahmanprasthāsyāma ity ucyamāne deva savitaretatte prāha tatpra ca suva pra ca yaja bṛhaspatir brahmā sa yajñaṃ pāhi sa yajñapatiṃ pāhi sa māṃ pāhy oṃ pratiṣṭeti prasauti
3.20.8.a.d: ब्रह्मन्प्रस्थास्याम इत्य् उच्यमाने देव सवितरेतत्ते प्राह तत्प्र च सुव प्र च यज बृहस्पतिर् ब्रह्मा स यज्ञं पाहि स यज्ञपतिं पाहि स मां पाह्य् ओं प्रतिष्टेति प्रसौति
3.20.8.a.m: When it is said: “O brahman, we shall set forth,” he gives the impulse with: “O divine Savitṛ, this he has proclaimed to you; impel it and sacrifice it! Bṛhaspati is the brahman; may he protect the sacrifice, may he protect the lord of the sacrifice, may he protect me! Om, stand firm!”

3.20.9.a.m: “Earth has gone to earth, the mother has gone to the mother.

3.20.9.b.s: bhūyāsma putraiḥ paśubhir yo no dveṣṭi sa bhidyatām iti yatdiṃca yajñe mṛnmayaṃ bhidyeta tadabhimantrayeta
3.20.9.b.d: भूयास्म पुत्रैः पशुभिर् यो नो द्वेष्टि स भिद्यताम् इति यत्दिंच यज्ञे मृन्मयं भिद्येत तदभिमन्त्रयेत
3.20.9.b.m: May we abound in sons and cattle! He who hates us, let him be broken!”—if whatever earthenware vessel should break in the sacrifice, he should consecrate it with this [mantra].

3.20.10.a.s: brahmabhāgaṃ prāśyāyāḍagnirjātavedāḥ pra ṇo yakṣyabhivasyo asmān saṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā vājavatyetyāhavanīyamupasthāya yathetaṃ pratiniṣkrāmati
3.20.10.a.d: ब्रह्मभागं प्राश्यायाडग्निर्जातवेदाः प्र णो यक्ष्यभिवस्यो अस्मान् सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्येत्याहवनीयमुपस्थाय यथेतं प्रतिनिष्क्रामति
3.20.10.a.m: Having partaken of the brahman's portion, having worshipped the āhavanīya with “Agni Jātavedas has sacrificed; sacrifice for us, give us more wealth, unite us with benevolence rich in vigour!” he walks out the way he entered.

3.20.11.a.m: Thus the function of the brahman for the iṣṭis and animal sacrifices is prescribed—the function of the brahman.

4.1.1.a.m: We shall explain the duties of the sacrificer.

4.1.2.a.s: yajamānasya brahmacaryaṃ dakṣiṇādānaṃ dravyaprakalpanaṃ kāmānāṃ kāmanam
4.1.2.a.d: यजमानस्य ब्रह्मचर्यं दक्षिणादानं द्रव्यप्रकल्पनं कामानां कामनम्
4.1.2.a.m: [The duties] of the sacrificer are: celibacy, giving the sacrificial gifts, arranging the materials, and wishing of desires.

4.1.3.a.m: He mutters the mantras that contain blessings for himself, attends upon [the fires] without ritual implements, and follows [the rites] with consecratory mutterings.

4.1.4.a.m: And on the new- or full-moon day he has his hair and beard shaved.

4.1.5.a.m: “He also has the body hair shaved in part,” so says the Vājasaneyaka.

4.1.6.a.s: vidyudasi vidya me pāpmānamṛtātsatyamupaimīti yakṣyamāṇo 'pa upaspṛśati
4.1.6.a.d: विद्युदसि विद्य मे पाप्मानमृतात्सत्यमुपैमीति यक्ष्यमाणो ऽप उपस्पृशति
4.1.6.a.m: About to sacrifice, he touches water with: “You are lightning; sever my sin! From untruth I approach truth.”

4.1.7.a.m: This touching [of water] takes place in all sacrifices.

4.1.8.a.s: agniṃ gṛhṇāmi surathaṃ yo mayobhūrya udyantamārohati sūryamahne /
4.1.8.a.d: अग्निं गृह्णामि सुरथं यो मयोभूर्य उद्यन्तमारोहति सूर्यमह्ने ।
4.1.8.a.m: “I take Agni of good chariot, who is delightful, who climbs up to the rising sun for the day;

4.1.8.b.s: ādityaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotiruttamaṃ śvoyajñāya ramatāṃ devatābhyaḥ //
4.1.8.b.d: आदित्यं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरुत्तमं श्वोयज्ञाय रमतां देवताभ्यः ॥
4.1.8.b.m: may the Āditya, highest light of lights, stay for tomorrow's sacrifice for the deities!

4.1.8.c.m: The Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas, the deities along with Indra:

4.1.8.d.s: tāḥ pūrvaḥ parigṛhṇāmi sva āyatane manīṣayā //
4.1.8.d.d: ताः पूर्वः परिगृह्णामि स्व आयतने मनीषया ॥
4.1.8.d.m: them I, beforehand, lay hold of in their own abode with my thought.

4.1.8.e.m: Those gods who have entered into this fifteenth nourishment, them I, beforehand, lay hold of;

4.1.8.f.s: agnirhavyavāḍiha tānāvahatu paurnamāsaṃ haviridameṣāṃ mayyāmāvāsyaṃ haviridameṣāṃ mayīti yathāliṅgamāhavanīye 'nvādhīyamāne japati
4.1.8.f.d: अग्निर्हव्यवाडिह तानावहतु पौर्नमासं हविरिदमेषां मय्यामावास्यं हविरिदमेषां मयीति यथालिङ्गमाहवनीये ऽन्वाधीयमाने जपति
4.1.8.f.m: may Agni the bearer of oblations bring them here! May this full-moon oblation of theirs be in me! May this new-moon oblation of theirs be in me!”—according to the characteristic mark, he mutters while fuel is being added to the āhavanīya.

4.1.9.a.m: “Between the fires the cattle have come to the assembly of the gods;

4.1.9.b.m: them I, beforehand, lay hold of in their own abode with my thought,” he mutters standing between the fires.

4.1.10.a.s: iha prajā viśvarūpā ramantām agniṃ gṛhapatimabhisaṃvasānāḥ /
4.1.10.a.d: इह प्रजा विश्वरूपा रमन्ताम् अग्निं गृहपतिमभिसंवसानाः ।
4.1.10.a.m: “Here may manifold offspring delight, dwelling together facing Agni the lord of the house;

4.1.10.b.s: tāḥ pūrvaḥ parigṛhṇāmi sva āyatane manīṣayā //
4.1.10.b.d: ताः पूर्वः परिगृह्णामि स्व आयतने मनीषया ॥
4.1.10.b.m: them I, beforehand, lay hold of in their own abode with my thought.

4.1.10.c.m: Here may manifold cattle delight, dwelling together facing Agni the lord of the house;

4.1.10.d.s: tānpūrvaḥ parigṛhṇāmi sva āyatane manīṣayeti gārhapatyam
4.1.10.d.d: तान्पूर्वः परिगृह्णामि स्व आयतने मनीषयेति गार्हपत्यम्
4.1.10.d.m: them I, beforehand, lay hold of in their own abode with my thought,” [he mutters facing] the gārhapatya.

4.2.1.a.m: “This Agni of the fathers has conveyed the oblations to the fathers;

4.2.1.b.s: taṃ pūrvaḥ parigṛhṇāmyaviṣaṃ naḥ pituṃ karaditi dakṣiṇāgnim //
4.2.1.b.d: तं पूर्वः परिगृह्णाम्यविषं नः पितुं करदिति दक्षिणाग्निम् ॥
4.2.1.b.m: him I, beforehand, lay hold of; may he make our nourishment free from poison,” [he mutters facing] the dakṣiṇāgni.

4.2.1.c.m: “May the guardians of the assembly kindle you incessantly as the share of victory;

4.2.1.d.s: agne dīdāya me sabhya vijityai śaradaḥ śatamiti sabhyam //
4.2.1.d.d: अग्ने दीदाय मे सभ्य विजित्यै शरदः शतमिति सभ्यम् ॥
4.2.1.d.m: O Agni, shine for my assembly, for victory for a hundred autumns,” [he mutters facing] the sabhya fire.

4.2.1.e.m: “May I bring food fit for the dwelling for a hundred autumns;

4.2.1.f.s: āvasathe śriyaṃ mantramahirbudhniyo niyacchatv ity āvasathyam
4.2.1.f.d: आवसथे श्रियं मन्त्रमहिर्बुध्नियो नियच्छत्व् इत्य् आवसथ्यम्
4.2.1.f.m: in the dwelling may Ahirbudhnya bestow fortune and sacred counsel,” [he mutters facing] the āvasathya fire.

4.2.2.a.m: “Here I proclaim the sacrifice to the Vasus, whose eldest is Agni;

4.2.2.b.m: here I proclaim the sacrifice to the Rudras, whose eldest is Indra;

4.2.2.c.s: idamahaṃ varuṇajyeṣṭhebhya ādityebhyo yajñaṃ prabravīmītyanvāhiteṣu japati
4.2.2.c.d: इदमहं वरुणज्येष्ठेभ्य आदित्येभ्यो यज्ञं प्रब्रवीमीत्यन्वाहितेषु जपति
4.2.2.c.m: here I proclaim the sacrifice to the Ādityas, whose eldest is Varuṇa,” he mutters when the fires have had fuel added to them.

4.2.3.a.s: pasavatīroṣadhaya iti purā barhiṣa āhartorjāyāpatī aśnītaḥ /
4.2.3.a.d: पसवतीरोषधय इति पुरा बर्हिष आहर्तोर्जायापती अश्नीतः ।
4.2.3.a.m: With “May the plants be rich in cattle,” the husband and wife eat before the sacrificial grass is brought;

4.2.3.b.m: before the separation of the calves on the new-moon day.

4.2.4.a.m: About to observe the fast for the Full Moon sacrifice, they do not become overly sated.

4.2.5.a.m: They should eat food free of beans and meat with clarified butter, or in its absence, with curd or milk.

4.2.6.a.m: At the Full Moon [sacrifice], he enters upon the vow [when the adhvaryu sets out to cut] the sacrificial grass

4.2.6.b.m: or at the New Moon, when the calves have been driven away.

4.2.7.a.s: praṇītāsu praṇīyamānāsvāsanneṣu vā haviḥṣu vratamupaitītyubhayatra sādhāraṇam
4.2.7.a.d: प्रणीतासु प्रणीयमानास्वासन्नेषु वा हविःषु व्रतमुपैतीत्युभयत्र साधारणम्
4.2.7.a.m: Or, common to both [occasions], he enters upon the vow while the praṇītā waters are being brought forward, or when the oblations have been placed [near the fires].

4.2.8.a.m: Some [say that the order is]: eating, adding fuel to the fires, entering upon the vow;

4.2.8.b.m: some [say]: entering upon the vow, eating, adding fuel to the fires;

4.2.8.c.m: some [say]: adding fuel to the fires, entering upon the vow, eating.

4.2.9.a.m: With [the mantra]: 'May the plants be full of milk,' he sips or touches water.

4.2.10.a.m: He crosses behind the āhavanīya towards the south.

4.2.11.a.s: eṣa evāta ūrdhvaṃ yajamānasya saṃcaro bhavati
4.2.11.a.d: एष एवात ऊर्ध्वं यजमानस्य संचरो भवति
4.2.11.a.m: From this point on, this alone is the sacrificer's path of movement.

4.3.1.a.m: Standing south of the āhavanīya, about to enter upon the vow, he meditates upon the ocean with his mind.

4.3.2.a.s: atha japaty agne vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmīti brāhmaṇaḥ /
4.3.2.a.d: अथ जपत्य् अग्ने व्रतपते व्रतं चरिष्यामीति ब्राह्मणः ।
4.3.2.a.m: Then a brāhmaṇa mutters: 'O Agni, lord of vows, I will observe the vow.'

4.3.2.b.s: vāyo vratapata āditya vratapate vratānāṃ vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmīti rājanyavaiśyau
4.3.2.b.d: वायो व्रतपत आदित्य व्रतपते व्रतानां व्रतपते व्रतं चरिष्यामीति राजन्यवैश्यौ
4.3.2.b.m: A rājanya and a vaiśya [mutter]: 'O Vāyu, lord of vows! O Āditya, lord of vows! O lord of the vows of vows, I will observe the vow!'

4.3.4.a.s: athādityamupatiṣṭhate samrāḍ asi vratapā asi vratapatir asi tatte prabravīmi tacchakeyaṃ tena śakeyaṃ tena rādhyāsam iti
4.3.4.a.d: अथादित्यमुपतिष्ठते सम्राड् असि व्रतपा असि व्रतपतिर् असि तत्ते प्रब्रवीमि तच्छकेयं तेन शकेयं तेन राध्यासम् इति
4.3.4.a.m: Then he pays reverence to the sun [with the mantra]: 'You are sovereign, you are the guardian of vows, you are the lord of vows; I proclaim that to you; may I be able to do that; with that may I succeed; with that may I prosper.'

4.3.5.a.m: If he should enter upon the vow after sunset, paying reverence to the āhavanīya, he should mutter this yajus-formula:

4.3.6.a.m: 'They strew grass around both fires; may the deities dwell near me.

4.3.6.b.s: ahaṃ grāmyānupavasāmi mahyaṃ gopataye paśuniti sāyaṃ paristīryamāṇeṣu japati
4.3.6.b.d: अहं ग्राम्यानुपवसामि मह्यं गोपतये पशुनिति सायं परिस्तीर्यमाणेषु जपति
4.3.6.b.m: I dwell near the domestic animals; [dwell near] the animals for me, the lord of cattle,' he mutters while [the fires] are being surrounded with grass in the evening.

4.3.7.a.m: At the evening meal, he eats wild food, free of beans and meat;

4.3.8.a.s: api vā kāmamā mārgādā madhuna ā prāśātikāt
4.3.8.a.d: अपि वा काममा मार्गादा मधुन आ प्राशातिकात्
4.3.8.a.m: or indeed as he pleases, up to venison, up to honey, up to millet;

4.3.10.a.m: He should not eat in the evening of that with which he is to sacrifice in the morning.

4.3.11.a.m: About to fast for wild food, he drinks water or does not.

4.3.12.a.m: Yawning, he should say: 'May skill and insight be in me.'

4.3.13.a.m: On the night of the New Moon, he remains awake.

4.3.14.a.s: api vā supyādupari tveva na śayīta
4.3.14.a.d: अपि वा सुप्यादुपरि त्वेव न शयीत
4.3.14.a.m: Or he may sleep, but he should not sleep on a raised bed.

4.3.15.a.s: api vopari śayīta brahmacārī tveva syāt
4.3.15.a.d: अपि वोपरि शयीत ब्रह्मचारी त्वेव स्यात्
4.3.15.a.m: Or he may even sleep on a raised bed, but he must remain celibate.

4.3.16.a.m: Some teach staying awake on both [nights].

4.3.17.a.m: He sleeps in the shed of the āhavanīya or in the shed of the gārhapatya.

4.4.1.a.s: devā deveṣu parākramdhvaṃ prathamā dvitīyeṣu dvitīyāstṛtīyeṣu trirekādaśā iha māvata idaṃ śakeyaṃ yadidaṃ karomy ātmā karotvātmane /
4.4.1.a.d: देवा देवेषु पराक्रम्ध्वं प्रथमा द्वितीयेषु द्वितीयास्तृतीयेषु त्रिरेकादशा इह मावत इदं शकेयं यदिदं करोम्य् आत्मा करोत्वात्मने ।
4.4.1.a.m: 'O gods, display your prowess among the gods, the first among the second, the second among the third; thirty-three [gods], protect me here; may I be able to do this which I do; let the self act for itself.

4.4.1.b.s: idaṃ kariṣye bheṣajam idaṃ me viśvabheṣajā aśvinā prāvataṃ yuvam iti japitvā śvobhūte brahmāṇaṃ vṛṇīte
4.4.1.b.d: इदं करिष्ये भेषजम् इदं मे विश्वभेषजा अश्विना प्रावतं युवम् इति जपित्वा श्वोभूते ब्रह्माणं वृणीते
4.4.1.b.m: I will make this healing; O Aśvins, possessing all healings, protect this of mine'—having muttered this, when the morrow comes, he chooses the brahman priest.

4.4.2.a.s: bhūpate bhuvanapate mahato bhūtasya pate brahmāṇaṃ tvā vṛṇīmaha ity uktvāpareṇāhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśati
4.4.2.a.d: भूपते भुवनपते महतो भूतस्य पते ब्रह्माणं त्वा वृणीमह इत्य् उक्त्वापरेणाहवनीयं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविशति
4.4.2.a.m: Having said: 'O lord of the earth, lord of the world, lord of the great being, we choose you as brahman,' and having crossed behind the āhavanīya towards the south, he sits down.

4.4.3.a.m: The brahman is in front, the sacrificer behind.

4.4.4.a.s: bhūśca kaśca vāk cark ca gauśca vaṭ ca khaṃ ca dhūṃśca nūṃśca pūṃścaikākṣarāḥ pūṃrdaśamā virājo yā idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vyānaśustā no devīstarasā saṃvidānāḥ svasti yajñaṃ nayata prajānatīrbrahmāpūtā stha /
4.4.4.a.d: भूश्च कश्च वाक् चर्क् च गौश्च वट् च खं च धूंश्च नूंश्च पूंश्चैकाक्षराः पूंर्दशमा विराजो या इदं विश्वं भुवनं व्यानशुस्ता नो देवीस्तरसा संविदानाः स्वस्ति यज्ञं नयत प्रजानतीर्ब्रह्मापूता स्थ ।
4.4.4.a.m: 'Earth, and Who, and Speech, and Verse, and Cow, and Vaṭ, and Sky, and Smoke, and Now, and City—the ten single-syllabled Virājes who have pervaded this entire world—may those goddesses, in harmony, swiftly carry the sacrifice to well-being, knowing it. You are purified by the brahman. /'

4.4.4.b.s: ko vo yunakti sa vo yunaktu viśvebhyaḥ kāmebhyo devayajyāyai /
4.4.4.b.d: को वो युनक्ति स वो युनक्तु विश्वेभ्यः कामेभ्यो देवयज्यायै ।
4.4.4.b.m: 'Who yokes you? May he yoke you for all desires, for the worship of the gods.'

4.4.4.c.m: 'Those [waters] which flow in front, above, and on all sides— /'

4.4.4.d.s: tābhī raśmipavitrābhiḥ śraddhāṃ yajñamārabha iti praṇītāḥ praṇīyamānā anumantrayate //
4.4.4.d.d: ताभी रश्मिपवित्राभिः श्रद्धां यज्ञमारभ इति प्रणीताः प्रणीयमाना अनुमन्त्रयते ॥
4.4.4.d.m: 'with those, which have rays as strainers, I undertake faith and the sacrifice'—[with these words] he follows with a mantra the praṇītā waters while they are being brought forward.

4.4.4.e.s: yajamāna havirnirvapsyāmītyucyamāna oṃ nirvapety uccair anujānāti
4.4.4.e.d: यजमान हविर्निर्वप्स्यामीत्युच्यमान ओं निर्वपेत्य् उच्चैर् अनुजानाति
4.4.4.e.m: Being addressed: 'O sacrificer, I shall apportion the oblation,' he consents aloud: 'Om, apportion!'

4.4.5.a.s: agnīm hotāramiha taṃ huva iti havirnirupyamāṇam abhimantrayate
4.4.5.a.d: अग्नीम् होतारमिह तं हुव इति हविर्निरुप्यमाणम् अभिमन्त्रयते
4.4.5.a.m: With [the mantra]: 'Here I invoke Agni, the hotṛ,' he addresses the oblation being apportioned.

4.4.6.a.m: Or he touches the vessel for apportioning the oblation, or he addresses it with a mantra.

4.4.7.a.m: Having spoken that, he restrains his speech.

4.4.9.a.s: kastvā yunakti sa tvā yunaktv iti sarvaṃ vihāramanuvīkṣate
4.4.9.a.d: कस्त्वा युनक्ति स त्वा युनक्त्व् इति सर्वं विहारमनुवीक्षते
4.4.9.a.m: With [the mantra]: 'Who yokes you? May he yoke you,' he surveys the whole sacrificial ground.

4.5.1.a.s: catuḥśikhaṇḍā yuvatiḥ supeśā ghṛtapratīkā bhuvanasya madhye /
4.5.1.a.d: चतुःशिखण्डा युवतिः सुपेशा घृतप्रतीका भुवनस्य मध्ये ।
4.5.1.a.m: 'A young woman with four braids, well-adorned, facing with clarified butter in the middle of the world, /'

4.5.1.b.s: marmṛjyamānā mahate saubhagāya mahyaṃ dhukṣva yajamānāya kāmāniti vediṃ saṃmṛjyamānām
4.5.1.b.d: मर्मृज्यमाना महते सौभगाय मह्यं धुक्ष्व यजमानाय कामानिति वेदिं संमृज्यमानाम्
4.5.1.b.m: 'being cleansed for great good fortune, yield desires to me, the sacrificer'—[with this he follows] the altar ground while it is being swept.

4.5.2.a.s: yo mā hṛdā manasā yaśca vācā yo brahmaṇā karmaṇā dveṣṭi devāḥ /
4.5.2.a.d: यो मा हृदा मनसा यश्च वाचा यो ब्रह्मणा कर्मणा द्वेष्टि देवाः ।
4.5.2.a.m: 'Whoever hates me in heart and mind, and whoever in speech, whoever with sacred lore and deed, O gods, /'

4.5.2.b.s: yaḥ śrutena hṛdayeneṣṇatā ca tasyendra vajreṇa śiraśchinadmīti stambayajurhriyamāṇam
4.5.2.b.d: यः श्रुतेन हृदयेनेष्णता च तस्येन्द्र वज्रेण शिरश्छिनद्मीति स्तम्बयजुर्ह्रियमाणम्
4.5.2.b.m: 'whoever with learning, heart, and malice—his head do I cut off with Indra's thunderbolt'—[with this he follows] the grass-bundle yajus while it is being carried away.

4.5.3.a.s: idaṃ tasmai harmyaṃ karomi yo vo devāścarati brahmacaryam /
4.5.3.a.d: इदं तस्मै हर्म्यं करोमि यो वो देवाश्चरति ब्रह्मचर्यम् ।
4.5.3.a.m: 'I make this mansion for him who among you, O gods, practices celibacy, /'

4.5.3.b.s: medhāvī dikṣu manasā tapasvyantardūtaścarati mānuṣīṣv ity utkaram abhigṛhyamāṇam
4.5.3.b.d: मेधावी दिक्षु मनसा तपस्व्यन्तर्दूतश्चरति मानुषीष्व् इत्य् उत्करम् अभिगृह्यमाणम्
4.5.3.b.m: 'wise in the quarters of space with his mind, performing austerity, walking as a messenger within the human [folk]'—[with this he follows] the rubbish heap while [earth] is being taken onto it.

4.5.4.a.s: yajñasya tvā pramayābhimayā pratimayonmayā parigṛhṇāmīti vediṃ parigṛhyamāṇām
4.5.4.a.d: यज्ञस्य त्वा प्रमयाभिमया प्रतिमयोन्मया परिगृह्णामीति वेदिं परिगृह्यमाणाम्
4.5.4.a.m: With [the formula]: 'By the measure of the sacrifice, by its counter-measure, by its matching measure, by its uplifted measure do I enclose you,' [he addresses] the altar ground while it is being enclosed [by lines].

4.5.5.a.m: 'What we have injured in digging up the earth, the plants, and the waters, /'

4.5.5.b.s: adhvaryavaḥ sphyakṛtaḥ sphyenāntarikṣaṃ moru pātu tasmāt //
4.5.5.b.d: अध्वर्यवः स्फ्यकृतः स्फ्येनान्तरिक्षं मोरु पातु तस्मात् ॥
4.5.5.b.m: 'the adhvaryus who make use of the wooden sword, may the wide midspace protect me from that with the wooden sword.'

4.5.5.c.s: yadudghnanto jihiṃsima krūramasyā vediṃ cakṛmā manasā devayantaḥ /
4.5.5.c.d: यदुद्घ्नन्तो जिहिंसिम क्रूरमस्या वेदिं चकृमा मनसा देवयन्तः ।
4.5.5.c.m: 'What we have injured in digging up, what cruel harm we have done to her altar ground, seeking the gods in our mind, /'

4.5.5.d.s: mā tena heḍa upagāma bhūmyāḥ śivo no viśvairbhuvanebhirastvityuddhanyamānām //
4.5.5.d.d: मा तेन हेड उपगाम भूम्याः शिवो नो विश्वैर्भुवनेभिरस्त्वित्युद्धन्यमानाम् ॥
4.5.5.d.m: 'may we not incur the wrath of the earth on account of that; may she be auspicious to us along with all worlds'—[with these verses he follows the altar ground] while it is being dug up.

4.5.5.e.s: bhūmirbhūtvā mahimānaṃ pupoṣa tato devī vardhayate payāṃsi /
4.5.5.e.d: भूमिर्भूत्वा महिमानं पुपोष ततो देवी वर्धयते पयांसि ।
4.5.5.e.m: 'Having become the earth, she nourished majesty; then the goddess increases the streams of milk; /'

4.5.5.f.s: yajñiyā yajñaṃ vicayanti śaṃ cauṣadhīrāpa iha śkvarīśceti kriyamāṇām //
4.5.5.f.d: यज्ञिया यज्ञं विचयन्ति शं चौषधीराप इह श्क्वरीश्चेति क्रियमाणाम् ॥
4.5.5.f.m: 'the sacrificial [waters] prepare the sacrifice, and may the plants and the able waters be beneficial here'—[with this he follows the altar ground] while it is being constructed.

4.5.5.g.m: 'I, with mind intent on praise, call upon the divine waters, /'

4.5.5.h.m: 'flowing by day and night, rich in holy work'—[with this he follows] the sprinkling waters while they are being set down.

4.5.5.i.s: ūrṇāmṛdu prathamānaṃ syonaṃ devebhyo juṣṭaṃ sadanāya barhiḥ /
4.5.5.i.d: ऊर्णामृदु प्रथमानं स्योनं देवेभ्यो जुष्टं सदनाय बर्हिः ।
4.5.5.i.m: 'Soft as wool, spreading wide, pleasant, dear to the gods as a seat is the sacrificial grass /'

4.5.5.j.s: suvarge loke yajamānaṃ hi dhehi māṃ nākasya pṛṣṭhe parame vyomanniti barhirāsādyamānam
4.5.5.j.d: सुवर्गे लोके यजमानं हि धेहि मां नाकस्य पृष्ठे परमे व्योमन्निति बर्हिरासाद्यमानम्
4.5.5.j.m: "Place the sacrificer in the heavenly world; me on the back of the firmament in the highest heaven"—[with these words he touches] the barhis being set down;

4.5.6.a.m: "Purify the clarified butter with the waters, the waters with the clarified butter, completely with the strainers of Savitṛ;

4.5.6.b.s: tā devīḥ śakvarīḥ śākvareṇemaṃ yajñamavata saṃvidānā ityājyaṃ prokṣaṇīścotpūyamānāḥ
4.5.6.b.d: ता देवीः शक्वरीः शाक्वरेणेमं यज्ञमवत संविदाना इत्याज्यं प्रोक्षणीश्चोत्पूयमानाः
4.5.6.b.m: do you divine Śakvarī waters, agreeing together, protect this sacrifice with what is mighty"—[with these words he touches] the clarified butter and the sprinkling waters being purified;

4.5.7.a.m: both murmur [the formula for] the ladlings of clarified butter;

4.6.1.a.m: "We have laid down the barhis within the earth, causing the cut plants to grow up again;

4.6.1.b.s: yāsāṃ mūlamudavadhīḥ sphyena śivā nastāḥ suhavā bhavantu //
4.6.1.b.d: यासां मूलमुदवधीः स्फ्येन शिवा नस्ताः सुहवा भवन्तु ॥
4.6.1.b.m: whose roots you struck away with the wooden sword, may they be propitious and easy to invoke for us;

4.6.1.c.s: sumanaso yajamānāya santv oṣadhīrāpa iha śakvarīśca /
4.6.1.c.d: सुमनसो यजमानाय सन्त्व् ओषधीराप इह शक्वरीश्च ।
4.6.1.c.m: may the plants and the Śakvarī waters here be well-disposed to the sacrificer;

4.6.1.d.s: vṛṣṭidyāvā parjanya enā virohayatu hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śatavalśā adabdhā ityantarvedi barhirāsannam
4.6.1.d.d: वृष्टिद्यावा पर्जन्य एना विरोहयतु हिरण्यवर्णाः शतवल्शा अदब्धा इत्यन्तर्वेदि बर्हिरासन्नम्
4.6.1.d.m: may Parjanya with rainy sky make these grow up, golden-colored, hundred-branched, uninjured"—[with these words he touches] the barhis set down inside the altar ground;

4.6.2.a.s: catuḥśikhaṇḍā yuvatiḥ supeśā ghṛtapratīkā vayunāni vaste /
4.6.2.a.d: चतुःशिखण्डा युवतिः सुपेशा घृतप्रतीका वयुनानि वस्ते ।
4.6.2.a.m: "Having four locks of hair, youthful, well-formed, butter-faced, she clothes herself in designs;

4.6.2.b.s: sā stīryamāṇā mahate saubhagāya sā me dhukṣa yajamānāya kāmān //
4.6.2.b.d: सा स्तीर्यमाणा महते सौभगाय सा मे धुक्ष यजमानाय कामान् ॥
4.6.2.b.m: being strewn for great good fortune, may she yield wishes to me, the sacrificer;

4.6.2.c.s: śivā ca me śagmā caidhi syonā ca me suṣadā caidhyūrjasvatī ca me payasvatī caidhi /
4.6.2.c.d: शिवा च मे शग्मा चैधि स्योना च मे सुषदा चैध्यूर्जस्वती च मे पयस्वती चैधि ।
4.6.2.c.m: be propitious and beneficial to me, be pleasant and comfortable to sit on for me, and be rich in strength and milk for me;

4.6.2.d.s: iṣamūrjaṃ me pinvasva brahma tejo me pinvasva kṣatramojo me pinvasva viśaṃ puṣṭiṃ me pinvasvāyurannādyaṃ me pinvasva prajāṃ paśūnme pinvasveti stīryamāṇām
4.6.2.d.d: इषमूर्जं मे पिन्वस्व ब्रह्म तेजो मे पिन्वस्व क्षत्रमोजो मे पिन्वस्व विशं पुष्टिं मे पिन्वस्वायुरन्नाद्यं मे पिन्वस्व प्रजां पशून्मे पिन्वस्वेति स्तीर्यमाणाम्
4.6.2.d.m: swell nourishment and strength for me, swell sacred knowledge and fiery energy for me, swell royal power and vigor for me, swell the clan and prosperity for me, swell lifespan and food for me, swell offspring and cattle for me"—[with these words he touches the altar ground] being strewn;

4.6.3.a.m: with "You are firm" and the verses that follow, verse by verse, [he addresses] the enclosing sticks being laid round;

4.6.3.b.s: asminyajña upa bhūya innu me 'vikṣobhāya paridhīndadhāmi /
4.6.3.b.d: अस्मिन्यज्ञ उप भूय इन्नु मे ऽविक्षोभाय परिधीन्दधामि ।
4.6.3.b.m: "In this sacrifice, for further [benefit] to me, I now lay down the enclosing sticks for stability;

4.6.3.c.s: dhratā dharuṇo dharīyānagnirdveṣāṃsi nirito nu dātā iti ca
4.6.3.c.d: ध्रता धरुणो धरीयानग्निर्द्वेषांसि निरितो नु दाता इति च
4.6.3.c.m: Agni, the sustainer, holder, best supporter, will now drive away hatreds from here"; and

4.6.4.a.m: "I yoke you with divine prayer"—[with this he touches] the āhavanīya;

4.6.4.b.s: tejiṣṭhā te tapanā yā ca rocanā pratyoṣantīstanvo yāste agne /
4.6.4.b.d: तेजिष्ठा ते तपना या च रोचना प्रत्योषन्तीस्तन्वो यास्ते अग्ने ।
4.6.4.b.m: "Those sharpest burning and shining bodies of yours, O Agni, that burn against [enemies];

4.6.4.c.s: tābhirvarmāṇyabhito vyayasva mā tvā dabhanyajñahanaḥ piśācā iti ca
4.6.4.c.d: ताभिर्वर्माण्यभितो व्ययस्व मा त्वा दभन्यज्ञहनः पिशाचा इति च
4.6.4.c.m: with them gird armors all around; let not the Piśācas, the destroyers of sacrifice, harm you"; and

4.6.5.a.m: "With the two dividers I cut off rivals, rivals born and those yet to be born;

4.6.5.b.d: विशो यन्त्राभ्यां विधमाम्येनानहं स्वानामुत्तमो ऽसानि देवाः ॥
4.6.5.b.m: with the two restrainers of the clan I blow them away; O gods, may I be the highest of my own people;

4.6.5.c.s: viśo yantre nudamāne arātiṃ viśvaṃ pāpmānamamatiṃ durmarāyum /
4.6.5.c.d: विशो यन्त्रे नुदमाने अरातिं विश्वं पाप्मानममतिं दुर्मरायुम् ।
4.6.5.c.m: the two restrainers of the clan pushing away the enemy, all evil, distress, and the malicious enemy;

4.6.5.d.s: sīdantī devī sukṛtasya loke dhṛtī stho vidhṛtī svadhṛtī svadhṛtī prāṇānmayi dhārayataṃ prajāṃ mayi dhārayataṃ paśūnmayi dhārayatam iti vidhṛtī āsādyamāne
4.6.5.d.d: सीदन्ती देवी सुकृतस्य लोके धृती स्थो विधृती स्वधृती स्वधृती प्राणान्मयि धारयतं प्रजां मयि धारयतं पशून्मयि धारयतम् इति विधृती आसाद्यमाने
4.6.5.d.m: sitting, divine, in the world of good deeds, you are supports, dividers, self-supporters, self-supporters; maintain the vital breaths in me, maintain offspring in me, maintain cattle in me"—[with these words] the two dividers being set down;

4.7.1.a.s: ayaṃ prastara ubhayasya dhartā dartā prayājānāmutānūyājānām /
4.7.1.a.d: अयं प्रस्तर उभयस्य धर्ता दर्ता प्रयाजानामुतानूयाजानाम् ।
4.7.1.a.m: "This grass bunch is the upholder of both, the upholder of the fore-sacrifices and of the after-sacrifices;

4.7.1.b.s: sa dādhāra samidho viśvarūpāstasminsruco adhyāsādayāmīti prastaramāsādyamānam
4.7.1.b.d: स दाधार समिधो विश्वरूपास्तस्मिन्स्रुचो अध्यासादयामीति प्रस्तरमासाद्यमानम्
4.7.1.b.m: it supports kindling-sticks of all forms; upon it I place the offering ladles"—[with these words he addresses] the grass bunch being set down;

4.7.2.a.s: āroha patho juhu devayānānyatrarṣayaḥ prathamajā ye purāṇāḥ /
4.7.2.a.d: आरोह पथो जुहु देवयानान्यत्रर्षयः प्रथमजा ये पुराणाः ।
4.7.2.a.m: "Mount the paths leading to the gods, O juhū, where are the first-born, ancient seers;

4.7.2.b.s: hiraṇyapakṣājirā saṃbhṛtāṅgā vahāsi mā sukṛtāṃ yatra lokāḥ //
4.7.2.b.d: हिरण्यपक्षाजिरा संभृताङ्गा वहासि मा सुकृतां यत्र लोकाः ॥
4.7.2.b.m: golden-winged, quick, with collected limbs, you shall bear me to where the worlds of the righteous are;

4.7.2.c.m: you are the juhū, turned to butter, whose path is the gāyatrī, enjoyed by the wise;

4.7.2.d.s: avyathamānā yajñamanuyacchasva sunītī yajñaṃ nayāsyupa devānāgneyena śarmaṇā daivyeneti juhūm //
4.7.2.d.d: अव्यथमाना यज्ञमनुयच्छस्व सुनीती यज्ञं नयास्युप देवानाग्नेयेन शर्मणा दैव्येनेति जुहूम् ॥
4.7.2.d.m: unfaltering, keep hold of the sacrifice; with good guidance lead the sacrifice to the gods, with divine, Āgneya shelter"—[with these verses he touches] the juhū;

4.7.2.e.s: avāhaṃ bādha upabhṛtā sapatnāñjātānbhrātṛvyānye ca janiṣyamāṇāḥ /
4.7.2.e.d: अवाहं बाध उपभृता सपत्नाञ्जातान्भ्रातृव्यान्ये च जनिष्यमाणाः ।
4.7.2.e.m: "Downwards with the upabhṛt I push rivals, rivals born and those yet to be born;

4.7.2.f.s: dohai yajñaṃ sudughāmiva dhenumahamuttaro bhūyāsamadhare matsapatnāḥ //
4.7.2.f.d: दोहै यज्ञं सुदुघामिव धेनुमहमुत्तरो भूयासमधरे मत्सपत्नाः ॥
4.7.2.f.m: I milk the sacrifice like a cow that milks well; may I become superior, my rivals inferior;

4.7.2.g.m: you are well-held, the upabhṛt, turned to butter, having the triṣṭubh meter, all-knowing;

4.7.2.h.s: avyathamānā yajñamanuyacchasva sunītī yajñaṃ nayāsyupa devānaindreṇa śarmaṇā daivyenetyupabhṛtam //
4.7.2.h.d: अव्यथमाना यज्ञमनुयच्छस्व सुनीती यज्ञं नयास्युप देवानैन्द्रेण शर्मणा दैव्येनेत्युपभृतम् ॥
4.7.2.h.m: unfaltering, keep hold of the sacrifice; with good guidance lead the sacrifice to the gods, with divine, Aindra shelter"—[with these verses he touches] the upabhṛt;

4.7.2.i.m: "He who, malicious in mind, speech, and heart, acts as an enemy against me, works against me, O Agni;

4.7.2.j.s: idamasya cittamadharaṃ dhruvāyā ahamuttaro bhūyāsamadhare matsapatnāḥ //
4.7.2.j.d: इदमस्य चित्तमधरं ध्रुवाया अहमुत्तरो भूयासमधरे मत्सपत्नाः ॥
4.7.2.j.m: downward beneath the dhruvā is this mind of his; may I become superior, my rivals inferior;

4.7.2.k.s: dhruvāsi dharaṇī dhanasya pūrṇā jāgatena chandasā viśvavedāḥ /
4.7.2.k.d: ध्रुवासि धरणी धनस्य पूर्णा जागतेन छन्दसा विश्ववेदाः ।
4.7.2.k.m: you are the dhruvā, the sustainer, full of wealth, having the jagatī meter, all-knowing;

4.7.2.l.s: avyathamānā yajñamanuyacchasva sunītī yajñaṃ nayāsyupa devānvaiśvadevena śarmaṇā daivyeneti dhruvām //
4.7.2.l.d: अव्यथमाना यज्ञमनुयच्छस्व सुनीती यज्ञं नयास्युप देवान्वैश्वदेवेन शर्मणा दैव्येनेति ध्रुवाम् ॥
4.7.2.l.m: unfaltering, keep hold of the sacrifice; with good guidance lead the sacrifice to the gods, with divine, Vaiśvadeva shelter"—[with these verses he touches] the dhruvā;

4.7.2.m.s: syono me sīda suṣadaḥ pṛthivyāṃ prathayi prajayā paśubhiḥ suvarge loke /
4.7.2.m.d: स्योनो मे सीद सुषदः पृथिव्यां प्रथयि प्रजया पशुभिः सुवर्गे लोके ।
4.7.2.m.m: "Sit pleasantly for me, easy to sit upon on the earth; expand with offspring and cattle in the heavenly world;

4.7.2.n.d: दिवि सीद पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे ऽहमुत्तरो भूयासमधरे मत्सपत्नाः ॥
4.7.2.n.m: sit in heaven, on earth, in the atmosphere; may I become superior, my rivals inferior;

4.7.2.o.m: this sruva ladle brings offerings forward, having a hundred syllables with the anuṣṭubh meter;

4.7.2.p.s: sarvā yajñasya samanakti viṣṭhā bārhaspatyena śarmaṇā daivyeneti sruvam //
4.7.2.p.d: सर्वा यज्ञस्य समनक्ति विष्ठा बार्हस्पत्येन शर्मणा दैव्येनेति स्रुवम् ॥
4.7.2.p.m: it anoints all the forms of the sacrifice, with divine, Bārhaspatya shelter"—[with these verses he touches] the sruva;

4.7.2.q.s: iyaṃ sthālī ghṛtasya pūrṇācchinnapayāḥ śatadhāra utsaḥ /
4.7.2.q.d: इयं स्थाली घृतस्य पूर्णाच्छिन्नपयाः शतधार उत्सः ।
4.7.2.q.m: "This pot is full of butter, with unbroken milk, a hundred-streamed well;

4.7.2.r.m: with divine, Māruta shelter"—[with these words he touches] the butter-pot;

4.8.1.a.s: tṛptirasi gāyatraṃ chandastarpaya mā tejasā brahmavarcasena tṛptirasi traiṣṭubhaṃ chandastarpaya maujasā vīryeṇa tṛptirasi jāgataṃ chandastarpaya mā prajayā paśubhiriti puroḍāśānajyamānān
4.8.1.a.d: तृप्तिरसि गायत्रं छन्दस्तर्पय मा तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन तृप्तिरसि त्रैष्टुभं छन्दस्तर्पय मौजसा वीर्येण तृप्तिरसि जागतं छन्दस्तर्पय मा प्रजया पशुभिरिति पुरोडाशानज्यमानान्
4.8.1.a.m: "You are satisfaction, the gāyatrī meter, satisfy me with fiery energy and sacred luster; you are satisfaction, the triṣṭubh meter, satisfy me with vigor and heroism; you are satisfaction, the jagatī meter, satisfy me with offspring and cattle"—[with these words he touches] the sacrificial cakes being anointed;

4.8.2.a.s: yajño 'si sarvataḥ śritaḥ sarvato māṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyacchrayatāṃ śataṃ me santvāśiṣaḥ sahasraṃ me santu sūnṛtā irāvatīḥ paśumatīḥ prajāpatirasi sarvataḥ śritaḥ sarvato māṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyacchrayatāṃ śataṃ me santvāśiṣaḥ sahasraṃ me santu sūnṛtā irāvatīḥ paśumatīr ity āgneyaṃ puroḍāśamāsannamabhimṛśati sarvāṇi vā havīṃṣi
4.8.2.a.d: यज्ञो ऽसि सर्वतः श्रितः सर्वतो मां भूतं भविष्यच्छ्रयतां शतं मे सन्त्वाशिषः सहस्रं मे सन्तु सूनृता इरावतीः पशुमतीः प्रजापतिरसि सर्वतः श्रितः सर्वतो मां भूतं भविष्यच्छ्रयतां शतं मे सन्त्वाशिषः सहस्रं मे सन्तु सूनृता इरावतीः पशुमतीर् इत्य् आग्नेयं पुरोडाशमासन्नमभिमृशति सर्वाणि वा हवींषि
4.8.2.a.m: "You are the sacrifice supported on all sides; may the past and future support me on all sides; may a hundred blessings be mine; may a thousand true words, full of refreshing drink and rich in cattle, be mine; you are Prajāpati supported on all sides; may the past and future support me on all sides; may a hundred blessings be mine; may a thousand true words, full of refreshing drink and rich in cattle, be mine"—with this he touches the sacrificial cake for Agni that has been set down, or all the oblations;

4.8.3.a.m: "This is power of the senses, immortal vigor, with which the cattle observed Indra;

4.8.3.b.s: tena devā avatopa māmiheṣamūrjaṃ yaśaḥ saha ojaḥ saneyaṃ śṛtaṃ mayi śrayatām iti prātardoham /
4.8.3.b.d: तेन देवा अवतोप मामिहेषमूर्जं यशः सह ओजः सनेयं शृतं मयि श्रयताम् इति प्रातर्दोहम् ।
4.8.3.b.m: with that, O gods, protect me here; may I gain nourishment, strength, glory, power, vigor; may what is boiled rest in me"—[with these words he touches] the morning milking;

4.8.3.c.m: "What moved upon the earth, entering into it, with which Prajāpati poured strength into Indra;

4.8.3.d.s: idaṃ tacchukraṃ madhu vājinīvadyenopariṣṭādadhinonmahendraṃ dadhi māṃ dhinotv iti dadhi
4.8.3.d.d: इदं तच्छुक्रं मधु वाजिनीवद्येनोपरिष्टादधिनोन्महेन्द्रं दधि मां धिनोत्व् इति दधि
4.8.3.d.m: this is that bright, sweet [substance] rich in steeds, with which he gladdened Mahendra from above; may the curd gladden me"—[with these words he touches] the curd;

4.8.4.a.s: ayaṃ yajñaḥ samasadaddhviṣmānṛcā ṣamnā yajuṣā devatābhiḥ /
4.8.4.a.d: अयं यज्ञः समसदद्ध्विष्मानृचा षम्ना यजुषा देवताभिः ।
4.8.4.a.m: "This sacrifice has assembled, possessing oblations, with ṛc, sāman, yajus, and deities;

4.8.4.b.s: tena lokānsūryavato jayemendrasya sakhyamamṛtatvamaśyāmiti sarvāṇi havīṃṣi
4.8.4.b.d: तेन लोकान्सूर्यवतो जयेमेन्द्रस्य सख्यममृतत्वमश्यामिति सर्वाणि हवींषि
4.8.4.b.m: by it may we win sun-lit worlds; may I attain companionship with Indra and immortality"—[with these words he touches] all the oblations;

4.8.5.a.s: yo naḥ kanīya iha kāmayātā asminyajñe yajamānāya mahyam /
4.8.5.a.d: यो नः कनीय इह कामयाता अस्मिन्यज्ञे यजमानाय मह्यम् ।
4.8.5.a.m: "Whoever here wishes [anything] lesser for us, for me the sacrificer in this sacrifice;

4.8.5.b.s: apa tamindrāgnī bhuvanānnudetāmahaṃ prajāṃ vīravatīṃ videyetyaindrāgnam
4.8.5.b.d: अप तमिन्द्राग्नी भुवनान्नुदेतामहं प्रजां वीरवतीं विदेयेत्यैन्द्राग्नम्
4.8.5.b.m: may Indrāgnī push him away from this world; may I obtain offspring possessing heroes"—[with these words he touches the cake] dedicated to Indrāgnī;

4.8.6.a.s: mamāgne varco vihaveṣv astv ity anuvākena sarvāṇi havīṃṣy āsannāny abhimṛśed aṣṭābhir vā
4.8.6.a.d: ममाग्ने वर्चो विहवेष्व् अस्त्व् इत्य् अनुवाकेन सर्वाणि हवींष्य् आसन्नान्य् अभिमृशेद् अष्टाभिर् वा
4.8.6.a.m: He should touch all the oblations that have been set down with the section "May my luster in the invocations be, O Agni...", or with eight [verses];

4.8.7.a.s: caturhotrā paurṇamāsyāṃ havīṃṣyāsannānyabhimṛśet prajākāmaḥ pañcahotrāmāvāsyāyāṃ svargakāmo nityavad eke samāmananti
4.8.7.a.d: चतुर्होत्रा पौर्णमास्यां हवींष्यासन्नान्यभिमृशेत् प्रजाकामः पञ्चहोत्रामावास्यायां स्वर्गकामो नित्यवद् एके समामनन्ति
4.8.7.a.m: One desiring offspring should touch the oblations that have been set down on the full-moon day with the caturhotṛ formula, and on the new-moon day one desiring heaven with the pañcahotṛ formula; some hand down [this practice] as obligatory;

4.9.1.a.m: He should utter the daśahotṛ formula before the kindling verses;

4.9.2.a.s: aṅgiraso māsya yajñasya prātaranuvākairavantviti sāmidhenīnāṃ pratipadi japati
4.9.2.a.d: अङ्गिरसो मास्य यज्ञस्य प्रातरनुवाकैरवन्त्विति सामिधेनीनां प्रतिपदि जपति
4.9.2.a.m: "May the Aṅgirases protect me in this sacrifice with the morning recitations"—[with this] he murmurs at the introductory verse of the kindling verses;

4.9.3.a.s: anūcyamānāsu daśahotāraṃ vyākhyāyocchuṣmo agna iti samidhyamānam /
4.9.3.a.d: अनूच्यमानासु दशहोतारं व्याख्यायोच्छुष्मो अग्न इति समिध्यमानम् ।
4.9.3.a.m: While they are being recited, having recited the daśahotṛ formula, with "Your fury, O Agni..." [he addresses the fire] being kindled;

4.9.3.b.m: "Kindled, offered to, greeted with svāhā, may Agni bring us across;

4.9.3.c.s: svagā devebhya idaṃ nama iti samiddham
4.9.3.c.d: स्वगा देवेभ्य इदं नम इति समिद्धम्
4.9.3.c.m: easy going to the gods, this homage"—[with these words he addresses the fire] when kindled;

4.9.4.a.m: "You are the mind, related to Prajāpati"—[with this he touches] the ladle-libation being poured.

4.9.5.a.m: Touching the ladle from behind, he recites the consecratory formula: 'You are speech, belonging to Indra.'

4.9.6.a.s: devāḥ pitaraḥ pitaro devā yo 'ham asmi sa sanyaje yasyāsmi na tamantaremi svaṃ ma iṣṭaṃ svaṃ dattaṃ svaṃ pūrtaṃ svaṃ śrāntaṃ svaṃ hutam /
4.9.6.a.d: देवाः पितरः पितरो देवा यो ऽहम् अस्मि स सन्यजे यस्यास्मि न तमन्तरेमि स्वं म इष्टं स्वं दत्तं स्वं पूर्तं स्वं श्रान्तं स्वं हुतम् ।
4.9.6.a.m: 'Gods, ancestors; ancestors, gods! Whosoever I am, being that one I sacrifice. Whose I am, him I do not bypass. Mine is what has been sacrificed, mine what has been given, mine what has been dedicated to public welfare, mine the hardship endured, mine the offering made.'

4.9.6.b.s: tasya me 'gnirupadraṣṭā vāyurupaśrotādityo 'nukhyātā dyauḥ pitā pṛthivī mātā prajāpatir bandhur ya evāsmi sa sanyaja iti hotṛpravare 'dhvaryupravare ca pravriyamāṇe
4.9.6.b.d: तस्य मे ऽग्निरुपद्रष्टा वायुरुपश्रोतादित्यो ऽनुख्याता द्यौः पिता पृथिवी माता प्रजापतिर् बन्धुर् य एवास्मि स सन्यज इति होतृप्रवरे ऽध्वर्युप्रवरे च प्रव्रियमाणे
4.9.6.b.m: 'Of that [sacrifice] of mine, Agni is the overseer, Vāyu the listener, Āditya the announcer, heaven the father, earth the mother, Prajāpati the kinsman. Whosoever I am, being that one I sacrifice.' [He recites this] while the pravara of the hotṛ and the pravara of the adhvaryu are being recited.

4.9.7.a.s: caturhotāraṃ vyākhyāya vasantamṛtūnāṃ prīṇāmīty etaiḥ pratimantraṃ prayājān hutaṃhutam
4.9.7.a.d: चतुर्होतारं व्याख्याय वसन्तमृतूनां प्रीणामीत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रयाजान् हुतंहुतम्
4.9.7.a.m: Having explained the Caturhotṛ formula, with these mantras: 'I gladden spring of the seasons...', [he recites] separately for each formula over each of the fore-offerings after it is offered.

4.9.8.a.s: eko mamaikā tasya yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmo dvau mama dve tasya trayo mama tisrastasya catvāro mama catasrastasya pañca mama na tasya kiṃcana yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma ity etaiśca pratimantram
4.9.8.a.d: एको ममैका तस्य यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मो द्वौ मम द्वे तस्य त्रयो मम तिस्रस्तस्य चत्वारो मम चतस्रस्तस्य पञ्च मम न तस्य किंचन यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इत्य् एतैश्च प्रतिमन्त्रम्
4.9.8.a.m: And with each of these mantras separately: 'One is mine, one is his who hates us and whom we hate; two are mine, two are his; three are mine, three are his; four are mine, four are his; five are mine, nothing is his who hates us and whom we hate.'

4.9.9.a.m: 'Through the sacrifice to the gods Agni and Soma may I become possessed of sight,' [he recites over] the two butter-portions.

4.9.11.a.m: 'Through Agni the sacrifice is possessed of sight; through the sacrifice to Agni may I become possessed of sight.'

4.9.11.b.s: somena yajñaścakṣuṣmām̐ somasyāhaṃ devayajyayā cakṣuṣmānbhūyāsamiti vihṛtau
4.9.11.b.d: सोमेन यज्ञश्चक्षुष्माम्̐ सोमस्याहं देवयज्यया चक्षुष्मान्भूयासमिति विहृतौ
4.9.11.b.m: 'Through Soma the sacrifice is possessed of sight; through the sacrifice to Soma may I become possessed of sight.' Thus when split.

4.9.12.a.m: He should recite the Pañcahotṛ formula before cutting portions of the oblation.

4.9.13.a.s: agner ahaṃ devayajyayānnādo bhūyāsam ity āgneyaṃ hutam anumantrayate dabdhir asīty upāṃśuyājam agnīṣomayor ity agnīṣomīyam indrāgniyor ity aindrāgnam indrasyety aindraṃ sāmnāyyaṃ mahendrasyeti māhendramagneḥ sviṣṭakṛta iti sauviṣṭakṛtam
4.9.13.a.d: अग्नेर् अहं देवयज्ययान्नादो भूयासम् इत्य् आग्नेयं हुतम् अनुमन्त्रयते दब्धिर् असीत्य् उपांशुयाजम् अग्नीषोमयोर् इत्य् अग्नीषोमीयम् इन्द्राग्नियोर् इत्य् ऐन्द्राग्नम् इन्द्रस्येत्य् ऐन्द्रं साम्नाय्यं महेन्द्रस्येति माहेन्द्रमग्नेः स्विष्टकृत इति सौविष्टकृतम्
4.9.13.a.m: With 'Through the sacrifice to Agni may I become an eater of food', he recites over the offering to Agni after it is offered; with 'You are harmless', over the silent sacrifice; with 'Of Agni and Soma...', over the one to Agni and Soma; with 'Of Indra and Agni...', over the one to Indra and Agni; with 'Of Indra...', over the Indra-sāmnāyya; with 'Of Mahendra...', over the Mahendra-sāmnāyya; with 'Of Agni Sviṣṭakṛt...', over the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

4.9.14.a.m: Some teach [the offerings] to other deities before the Sviṣṭakṛt.

4.10.1.a.s: indrasya vaimṛdhasyāhaṃ devayajyayāsapatno vīryavānbhūyāsam indrasya trāturahaṃ devayajyayā trāto bhūyāsaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyor ahaṃ devayajyayobhayor lokayor ṛdhyāsaṃ /
4.10.1.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वैमृधस्याहं देवयज्ययासपत्नो वीर्यवान्भूयासम् इन्द्रस्य त्रातुरहं देवयज्यया त्रातो भूयासं द्यावापृथिव्योर् अहं देवयज्ययोभयोर् लोकयोर् ऋध्यासं ।
4.10.1.a.m: 'Through the sacrifice to Indra Vaimṛdha may I become free of rivals and full of vigor; through the sacrifice to Indra the Protector may I become protected; through the sacrifice to Heaven and Earth may I prosper in both worlds;'

4.10.1.b.m: 'May I attain abundance and a firm foundation,' according to some.

4.10.1.c.s: pūṣṇo 'haṃ devayajyayā prajaniṣīya prajayā paśubhiḥ sarasvatyā ahaṃ devayajyayā vācamannādyaṃ puṣeyaṃ viśveṣāṃ devānāmahaṃ devayajyayā prāṇaiḥ sāyujyaṃ gameyamaryamṇo 'haṃ devayajyayā svargaṃ lokaṃ gameyamadityā ahaṃ devayajyayā pra prajayā ca paśubhiś ca janiṣīyendrasyendriyāvato 'haṃ devayajyayendriyāvayannādo bhūyāsamiti yathāliṅgaṃ vaikṛtīḥ
4.10.1.c.d: पूष्णो ऽहं देवयज्यया प्रजनिषीय प्रजया पशुभिः सरस्वत्या अहं देवयज्यया वाचमन्नाद्यं पुषेयं विश्वेषां देवानामहं देवयज्यया प्राणैः सायुज्यं गमेयमर्यम्णो ऽहं देवयज्यया स्वर्गं लोकं गमेयमदित्या अहं देवयज्यया प्र प्रजया च पशुभिश् च जनिषीयेन्द्रस्येन्द्रियावतो ऽहं देवयज्ययेन्द्रियावयन्नादो भूयासमिति यथालिङ्गं वैकृतीः
4.10.1.c.m: 'Through the sacrifice to Pūṣan may I be propagated with offspring and livestock; through the sacrifice to Sarasvatī may I foster speech and food consumption; through the sacrifice to the Viśve Devas may I attain union with the vital breaths; through the sacrifice to Aryaman may I go to the heavenly world; through the sacrifice to Aditi may I bring forth offspring and livestock; through the sacrifice to Indra possessing indriya may I be endowed with indriya and an eater of food'—thus over the modified offerings according to the characteristic mark.

4.10.2.a.s: agnir mā duriṣṭāt pātv iti prāśitramavadīyamānam
4.10.2.a.d: अग्निर् मा दुरिष्टात् पात्व् इति प्राशित्रमवदीयमानम्
4.10.2.a.m: With 'May Agni protect me from an ill-performed sacrifice', [he recites over] the prāśitra portion while it is being cut off.

4.10.3.a.m: With 'You of beautiful form and of the color of rain, come!', [he recites over] the iḍā.

4.10.4.a.s: bhūyasyehi śreyasyehi vasīyasyehi citta ehi dadhiṣa ehīḍa ehi sūnṛta ehītīḍāyā upāṃśūpahave sapta devagavīrjapati /
4.10.4.a.d: भूयस्येहि श्रेयस्येहि वसीयस्येहि चित्त एहि दधिष एहीड एहि सूनृत एहीतीडाया उपांशूपहवे सप्त देवगवीर्जपति ।
4.10.4.a.m: With 'O more abundant one, come; O better one, come; O wealthier one, come; O thought, come; O supporter, come; O iḍā, come; O gracious speech, come!', he murmurs during the silent invitation of the iḍā to the seven divine cows.

4.10.4.b.s: cidasi manāsi dhīrasi rantī ramatiḥ sūnuḥ sūnarītyuccairupahave sapta manuṣyagavīḥ /
4.10.4.b.d: चिदसि मनासि धीरसि रन्ती रमतिः सूनुः सूनरीत्युच्चैरुपहवे सप्त मनुष्यगवीः ।
4.10.4.b.m: With 'You are thought, you are mind, you are meditation, rejoicing, delight, daughter, gracious', [he murmurs] during the loud invitation to the seven human cows.

4.10.4.c.s: devīrdevairabhi mā nivartadhvaṃ syonāḥ syonena ghṛtena mā samukṣata nama idamudaṃ bhiṣagṛṣirbrahmā yaddade samudrādudacanniva srucā vāgagre viprasya tiṣṭhati śṛṅgebhirdaśabhirdiśanniti ca
4.10.4.c.d: देवीर्देवैरभि मा निवर्तध्वं स्योनाः स्योनेन घृतेन मा समुक्षत नम इदमुदं भिषगृषिर्ब्रह्मा यद्ददे समुद्रादुदचन्निव स्रुचा वागग्रे विप्रस्य तिष्ठति शृङ्गेभिर्दशभिर्दिशन्निति च
4.10.4.c.m: And [he recites]: 'Divine ones, turn toward me together with the gods; gentle ones, sprinkle me with gentle clarified butter; this obeisance, this water... which the healer, the sage, the brahman took as if ladling from the ocean with a ladle, speech stands at the tip of the inspired poet, showing with ten horns.'

4.10.5.a.s: upahūyamānāyaṃ vāyaviḍā te māteti hotāramīkṣamāṇo vāyuṃ manasā dhyāyet
4.10.5.a.d: उपहूयमानायं वायविडा ते मातेति होतारमीक्षमाणो वायुं मनसा ध्यायेत्
4.10.5.a.m: While [the iḍā] is being invoked, looking at the hotṛ, he should mentally meditate on Vāyu with: 'O Vāyu, iḍā is your mother.'

4.10.6.a.m: At the benedictions: 'May that benediction of mine be true.'

4.10.7.a.s: iḍāyā ahaṃ devayajyayā paśumānbhūyāsam ity upahūtām //
4.10.7.a.d: इडाया अहं देवयज्यया पशुमान्भूयासम् इत्य् उपहूताम् ॥
4.10.7.a.m: Over [the iḍā] when invoked: 'Through the sacrifice of the iḍā may I become rich in cattle.'

4.10.7.b.s: iḍā dhenuḥ sahavatsā na āgādūrjaṃ duhānā payasā prapīnā /
4.10.7.b.d: इडा धेनुः सहवत्सा न आगादूर्जं दुहाना पयसा प्रपीना ।
4.10.7.b.m: 'The iḍā, a milch-cow accompanied by her calf, has come to us, yielding nourishment, swelling with milk.

4.10.7.c.s: sā no annene haviṣota gobhir iḍābhyas mām̐ āgād iti bhakṣāyāhriyamāṇām
4.10.7.c.d: सा नो अन्नेने हविषोत गोभिर् इडाभ्यस् माम्̐ आगाद् इति भक्षायाह्रियमाणाम्
4.10.7.c.m: May she come to us with food, with oblation, and with cows; the iḍā has come to us,' [he recites over the iḍā] while it is being brought forward for consumption.

4.10.8.a.m: The consumption of the iḍā and the cleansing have already been explained.

4.10.9.a.s: bradhna pinvasva dadato me mā kṣāyi kurvato me mopadasaddiśāṃ kḷpirasi diśo me kalpantāṃ kalpantāṃ me diśo daivīśca mānuṣīścāhorātre me kalpetāmardhamāsā me kalpantāṃ māsā me kalpantāmṛtavo me kalpantāṃ saṃvatsaro me kalpatāṃ kḷptir asi kalpatāṃ ma iti barhiṣi puroḍāśamāsannamabhimṛśati
4.10.9.a.d: ब्रध्न पिन्वस्व ददतो मे मा क्षायि कुर्वतो मे मोपदसद्दिशां कॢपिरसि दिशो मे कल्पन्तां कल्पन्तां मे दिशो दैवीश्च मानुषीश्चाहोरात्रे मे कल्पेतामर्धमासा मे कल्पन्तां मासा मे कल्पन्तामृतवो मे कल्पन्तां संवत्सरो मे कल्पतां कॢप्तिर् असि कल्पतां म इति बर्हिषि पुरोडाशमासन्नमभिमृशति
4.10.9.a.m: With 'O sun, swell; may [wealth] not fail me as I give; may it not diminish for me as I act; you are the arrangement of the directions; may the directions be arranged for me; may the divine and human directions be arranged for me; may the day and night be arranged for me; may the fortnights be arranged for me; may the months be arranged for me; may the seasons be arranged for me; may the year be arranged for me; you are the arrangement, let it be arranged for me', he touches the sacrificial cake placed on the sacrificial grass.

4.11.1.a.m: Then he pushes it out toward the directions with: 'To you, [belonging] to the regions, to the four immortal guardians of the regions;

4.11.1.b.m: let us honor these overseers of what has come into being with the oblation.

4.11.1.c.s: brahmapā hi bhajatāṃ bhāgi bhāgaṃ mābhāgo bhakta nirabhāgaṃ bhajāmaḥ /
4.11.1.c.d: ब्रह्मपा हि भजतां भागि भागं माभागो भक्त निरभागं भजामः ।
4.11.1.c.m: Indeed let the protector of sacred knowledge take a share; let the sharer [receive] the portion; let him who is without a portion not share; we exclude the unportioned.

4.11.1.d.m: Swell the waters, enliven the plants, protect the two-footed, favor the four-footed, send rain down from heaven!

4.11.1.e.m: This oblation belongs to the brāhmaṇas who are worthy of soma and drink soma.

4.11.1.f.m: The non-brāhmaṇa is excluded; there is nothing here for a non-brāhmaṇa.'

4.11.2.a.s: upahūto dyauḥ pitopa māṃ dyauḥ pitā hvayatām agnirāgnīdhrādāyuṣe varcase jivātvai puṇyāyopahūtā pṛthivī mātopa māṃ mātā pṛthivī hvayatāmagnirāgnīdhrādāyuṣe varcase jīvātvai puṇyāyetyāgnīdhrabhāgasya vaiśeṣikam
4.11.2.a.d: उपहूतो द्यौः पितोप मां द्यौः पिता ह्वयताम् अग्निराग्नीध्रादायुषे वर्चसे जिवात्वै पुण्यायोपहूता पृथिवी मातोप मां माता पृथिवी ह्वयतामग्निराग्नीध्रादायुषे वर्चसे जीवात्वै पुण्यायेत्याग्नीध्रभागस्य वैशेषिकम्
4.11.2.a.m: 'Invoked is Father Heaven; may Father Heaven call me; may Agni from the Āgnīdhra [hearth] [give] life, splendor, livelihood, merit. Invoked is Mother Earth; may Mother Earth call me; may Agni from the Āgnīdhra [hearth] [give] life, splendor, livelihood, merit'—this is specific to the portion of the agnīdh.

4.11.3.a.m: With 'O sun, swell...', he touches the anvāhārya cooked rice placed inside the altar ground.

4.11.3.b.s: iyaṃ sthālyamṛtasya pūrṇā sahasradhāra utso akṣīyamāṇaḥ /
4.11.3.b.d: इयं स्थाल्यमृतस्य पूर्णा सहस्रधार उत्सो अक्षीयमाणः ।
4.11.3.b.m: And: 'This pot is full of immortality, a thousand-streamed, unfailing spring;

4.11.3.c.s: sa dādhāra pṛthivīmantarikṣaṃ divaṃ ca tenaudanenātitarāṇi mṛtyum iti ca
4.11.3.c.d: स दाधार पृथिवीमन्तरिक्षं दिवं च तेनौदनेनातितराणि मृत्युम् इति च
4.11.3.c.m: it holds heaven, earth, and the intermediate space; by means of that cooked rice may I transcend death.'

4.11.4.a.m: The ritual call and the giving of the anvāhārya cooked rice have already been explained.

4.11.5.a.s: eṣā te agne samid ity ānūyājikīṃ samidhamādhīyamānām //
4.11.5.a.d: एषा ते अग्ने समिद् इत्य् आनूयाजिकीं समिधमाधीयमानाम् ॥
4.11.5.a.m: With 'This is your kindling stick, O Agni...', [he recites over] the after-offering kindling stick being placed [on the fire].

4.11.5.b.s: yaṃ te agna āvṛścāmyahaṃ vā kṣipitaścaran /
4.11.5.b.d: यं ते अग्न आवृश्चाम्यहं वा क्षिपितश्चरन् ।
4.11.5.b.m: 'Whomsoever I cut off for you, O Agni, or wandering about hungry,

4.11.5.c.s: prajāṃ ca tasya mūlaṃ ca nīcairdevā nivṛścata //
4.11.5.c.d: प्रजां च तस्य मूलं च नीचैर्देवा निवृश्चत ॥
4.11.5.c.m: both his offspring and his root do you, O gods, cut down below.

4.11.5.d.s: agne yo no 'bhidāsati samāno yaś ca niṣṭyaḥ /
4.11.5.d.d: अग्ने यो नो ऽभिदासति समानो यश् च निष्ट्यः ।
4.11.5.d.m: O Agni, he who plots against us, whether an equal or a stranger,

4.11.5.e.m: like a burning piece of firewood, let nothing remain of him!

4.11.5.f.s: yo māṃ dveṣṭi jātavedo yaṃ cāhaṃ dveṣmi yaśca mām /
4.11.5.f.d: यो मां द्वेष्टि जातवेदो यं चाहं द्वेष्मि यश्च माम् ।
4.11.5.f.m: Whoever hates me, O Jātavedas, and whomsoever I hate, and whoever [hates] me—

4.11.5.g.s: sarvāṃstānagne saṃdaha yāṃścāhaṃ dveṣmi ye ca mām ity āhitāyām agnim
4.11.5.g.d: सर्वांस्तानग्ने संदह यांश्चाहं द्वेष्मि ये च माम् इत्य् आहितायाम् अग्निम्
4.11.5.g.m: burn all of them completely, O Agni, whom I hate and who [hate] me'—[he recites this over] Agni when it is placed [on the fire].

4.11.6.a.m: 'Altar ground, sacrificial grass, cooked oblation, firewood, enclosing sticks, ladles,

4.11.6.b.m: ghee, sacrifice, verses, formulas, consecratory verses, and vaṣaṭ-calls,

4.11.6.c.s: saṃ me saṃnatayo namantāmidhmasaṃnahane huta iti saṃmārgān hutān
4.11.6.c.d: सं मे संनतयो नमन्तामिध्मसंनहने हुत इति संमार्गान् हुतान्
4.11.6.c.m: may my homages bend down harmoniously; offered in the tying of the firewood', [he recites over] the sweeping-grasses after they are offered.

4.11.7.a.s: saptahotāraṃ vadet purastād anūyājānām upariṣṭād vā
4.11.7.a.d: सप्तहोतारं वदेत् पुरस्ताद् अनूयाजानाम् उपरिष्टाद् वा
4.11.7.a.m: He should recite the Saptahotṛ formula before or after the after-offerings.

4.12.1.a.s: barhiṣo 'haṃ devayajyayā prajāvānbhūyāsam ity etaiḥ pratimantram anūyājān hutaṃhutam
4.12.1.a.d: बर्हिषो ऽहं देवयज्यया प्रजावान्भूयासम् इत्य् एतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम् अनूयाजान् हुतंहुतम्
4.12.1.a.m: With 'Through the sacrifice to the sacrificial grass may I become possessed of offspring...', [he recites] separately for each formula over each of the after-offerings after it is offered.

4.12.2.a.m: Both [the adhvaryu and the sacrificer] murmur the two Vājavatī verses.

4.12.3.a.m: 'I have gladdened the divine Vasus with the sacrifice; I have gladdened the divine Rudras with the sacrifice; I have gladdened the divine Ādityas with the sacrifice'—[he recites this] with each formula over the enclosing sticks while they are being anointed.

4.12.3.b.s: samaṅktāṃ barhirhaviṣā ghṛtena samādityairvasubhiḥ saṃ marudbhiḥ /
4.12.3.b.d: समङ्क्तां बर्हिर्हविषा घृतेन समादित्यैर्वसुभिः सं मरुद्भिः ।
4.12.3.b.m: 'May the sacrificial grass be anointed with the oblation, with ghee, together with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Maruts;

4.12.3.c.s: samindreṇa viśvebhir devebhir aṅktāṃ divyaṃ nabho gacchatu yatsvāheti prastaramajyamānam
4.12.3.c.d: समिन्द्रेण विश्वेभिर् देवेभिर् अङ्क्तां दिव्यं नभो गच्छतु यत्स्वाहेति प्रस्तरमज्यमानम्
4.12.3.c.m: [He follows] the grass bunch being anointed with: 'May it be anointed with Indra, with the All-gods! May it go to the divine sky! Svāhā!'

4.12.4.a.m: With: 'After the triumph of Agni may I triumph,' according to their characteristics, [he addresses] the deities of the sūktavāka.

4.12.5.a.s: yadā cāsya hotā nāma gṛhṇīyādatha brūyād emā agmannāśiṣo dohakāmā iti
4.12.5.a.d: यदा चास्य होता नाम गृह्णीयादथ ब्रूयाद् एमा अग्मन्नाशिषो दोहकामा इति
4.12.5.a.m: And when the hotṛ pronounces his name, he should then say: 'Hither have these wishes come, fulfilling wishes.'

4.12.6.a.s: sā me satyāśīrdevāngamyājjuṣṭājjuṣṭatarā paṇyātpaṇyatarāreḍatā manasā devāngamyādyajño devāngacchatvado ma āgacchatv iti sūktavākasyāśiḥṣu yatkāmayate tasya nāma gṛhṇāti
4.12.6.a.d: सा मे सत्याशीर्देवान्गम्याज्जुष्टाज्जुष्टतरा पण्यात्पण्यतरारेडता मनसा देवान्गम्याद्यज्ञो देवान्गच्छत्वदो म आगच्छत्व् इति सूक्तवाकस्याशिःषु यत्कामयते तस्य नाम गृह्णाति
4.12.6.a.m: At the blessings of the sūktavāka, with: 'May that true blessing of mine go to the gods, welcomed, more welcomed, praised, more praised! With ungrudging mind may it go to the gods! May the sacrifice go to the gods, may that [such-and-such] come to me!' he names whatever he desires.

4.12.7.a.s: rohitena tvāgnirdevatāṃ gamayatvityetaiḥ pratimantramagnīdhā prastaraṃ prahriyamāṇam
4.12.7.a.d: रोहितेन त्वाग्निर्देवतां गमयत्वित्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रमग्नीधा प्रस्तरं प्रह्रियमाणम्
4.12.7.a.m: [He follows] the grass bunch being cast into the fire by the agnīdh with these mantras, one for each: 'May Agni lead you to the deity by means of his red steed!'

4.12.8.a.m: 'The peg has stretched down from heaven, arisen from the earth;

4.12.8.b.m: With that, thousand-jointed, do we torment him who hates us.

4.12.8.c.s: dviṣanme bahu śocatvoṣadhe mo ahaṃ śucam iti prastaratṛṇe prahriyamāṇe
4.12.8.c.d: द्विषन्मे बहु शोचत्वोषधे मो अहं शुचम् इति प्रस्तरतृणे प्रह्रियमाणे
4.12.8.c.m: May he who hates me be tormented greatly! O herb, may I not be tormented!' [with these words he follows] two blades from the grass bunch being cast into the fire.

4.12.9.a.m: With: 'I unloose you,' while the enclosing sticks are being unloosed.

4.12.10.a.m: At the śaṃyuvāka, with: 'Of Viṣṇu, blessing and relief!'

4.12.10.b.s: yajña namaste yajña namo namaśca te yajña śivena me saṃtiṣṭhasva syonena me saṃtiṣṭhasva subhūtena me saṃtiṣṭhasva brahmavarcasena me saṃtiṣṭhasva yajñasyarddhimanu saṃtiṣṭhasvopa te yajña nama upa te nama upa te nama iti ca //
4.12.10.b.d: यज्ञ नमस्ते यज्ञ नमो नमश्च ते यज्ञ शिवेन मे संतिष्ठस्व स्योनेन मे संतिष्ठस्व सुभूतेन मे संतिष्ठस्व ब्रह्मवर्चसेन मे संतिष्ठस्व यज्ञस्यर्द्धिमनु संतिष्ठस्वोप ते यज्ञ नम उप ते नम उप ते नम इति च ॥
4.12.10.b.m: And with: 'O sacrifice, homage to you! O sacrifice, homage and homage to you, O sacrifice! Conclude auspiciously for me, conclude pleasantly for me, conclude with prosperity for me, conclude with spiritual lustre for me, conclude in accordance with the success of the sacrifice! Near unto you, O sacrifice, homage! Near unto you, homage! Near unto you, homage!'

4.12.10.c.m: 'The sacrifice has been offered, bestowing wealth through the Bhṛgus, bestowing blessings through the Yatis, full of blessings through the Vasus;

4.12.10.d.s: atharvabhistasya meṣṭasya vītasya draviṇehāgameriti saṃsrāvaṃ hutam
4.12.10.d.d: अथर्वभिस्तस्य मेष्टस्य वीतस्य द्रविणेहागमेरिति संस्रावं हुतम्
4.12.10.d.m: Through the Atharvans, from that which has been offered and accepted, may wealth come to me here!' [with this he follows] the combined remnants [of clarified butter] offered.

4.13.1.a.s: somasyāhaṃ devayajyayā suretā reto dhiṣīyeti yathāliṅgaṃ patnīsaṃyājān hutaṃhutam
4.13.1.a.d: सोमस्याहं देवयज्यया सुरेता रेतो धिषीयेति यथालिङ्गं पत्नीसंयाजान् हुतंहुतम्
4.13.1.a.m: With: 'Through the god-worship of Soma, well-seeded may I bear seed,' according to their characteristics, [he follows] each wife-sacrifice (patnīsaṃyāja) as it is offered.

4.13.2.a.s: rākāyā ahaṃ devayajyayā prajāvānbhūyāsaṃ sinīvalyā ahaṃ devayajyayā paśumānbhūyāsaṃ kuhvā ahaṃ devayajyayā puṣṭimān paśumān bhūyāsam iti kāmyāḥ
4.13.2.a.d: राकाया अहं देवयज्यया प्रजावान्भूयासं सिनीवल्या अहं देवयज्यया पशुमान्भूयासं कुह्वा अहं देवयज्यया पुष्टिमान् पशुमान् भूयासम् इति काम्याः
4.13.2.a.m: 'Through the god-worship of Rākā may I become rich in offspring! Through the god-worship of Sinīvālī may I become rich in cattle! Through the god-worship of Kuhū may I become prosperous and rich in cattle!'—these are optional.

4.13.3.a.s: rākāyā ahaṃ devayajyayā prajāvatī bhūyāsaṃ sinīvālyā ahaṃ devayajyayā paśumatī bhūyāsaṃ kuhvā ahaṃ devayajyayā puṣṭimatī paśumatī bhūyāsam iti patnyanumantrayate
4.13.3.a.d: राकाया अहं देवयज्यया प्रजावती भूयासं सिनीवाल्या अहं देवयज्यया पशुमती भूयासं कुह्वा अहं देवयज्यया पुष्टिमती पशुमती भूयासम् इति पत्न्यनुमन्त्रयते
4.13.3.a.m: The wife follows with: 'Through the god-worship of Rākā may I become rich in offspring! Through the god-worship of Sinīvālī may I become rich in cattle! Through the god-worship of Kuhū may I become prosperous and rich in cattle!'

4.13.4.a.s: iḍāsmānanu vastāṃ ghṛtena yasyāḥ pade punate devayantaḥ /
4.13.4.a.d: इडास्माननु वस्तां घृतेन यस्याः पदे पुनते देवयन्तः ।
4.13.4.a.m: 'May Iḍā clothe us with clarified butter, in whose footprint those who seek the gods purify themselves;

4.13.4.b.s: vaiśvānarī śakvarī vāvṛdhānopa yajñamasthita vaiśvadevīty ājyeḍām
4.13.4.b.d: वैश्वानरी शक्वरी वावृधानोप यज्ञमस्थित वैश्वदेवीत्य् आज्येडाम्
4.13.4.b.m: Belonging to Vaiśvānara, mighty, strengthened, belonging to the All-gods, she has approached the sacrifice'—[with this he follows] the butter-iḍā.

4.13.5.a.m: Having placed the veda-broom inside the altar ground, he touches it with: 'You are the veda.'

4.13.6.a.m: At 'before I may obtain', he should name whatever of his rival's he covets:

4.13.6.b.m: 'It is recognized that he strips away all that of his.'

4.13.7.a.s: yā sarasvatī viśobhagīnā tasyāṃ me rāsva tasyāste bhaktivāno bhūyāsmeti phalīkaraṇahome hute mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe
4.13.7.a.d: या सरस्वती विशोभगीना तस्यां मे रास्व तस्यास्ते भक्तिवानो भूयास्मेति फलीकरणहोमे हुते मुखं विमृष्टे
4.13.7.a.m: When the oblation of grain-chaff has been offered, he wipes his face with: 'The Sarasvatī who is beneficial to all people, grant [a share] in her to me; may we share in her!'

4.13.8.a.s: vasuryajño vasumānyajñastasya mā yajñasya vasorvasumato vasvāgacchatvado ma āgacchatv iti samiṣṭayajurhutamanumantrayate /
4.13.8.a.d: वसुर्यज्ञो वसुमान्यज्ञस्तस्य मा यज्ञस्य वसोर्वसुमतो वस्वागच्छत्वदो म आगच्छत्व् इति समिष्टयजुर्हुतमनुमन्त्रयते ।
4.13.8.a.m: He follows the offered samiṣṭayajus with: 'The sacrifice is rich, the sacrifice possesses wealth; may the wealth of that rich, wealth-possessing sacrifice come to me! May that [such-and-such] come to me!'

4.13.9.a.m: He eats the sacrificer's portion with: 'United with the blessing, the lord of the sacrifice...'

4.14.1.a.m: With: 'I have praised Dadhikrāvan,' [he eats] the evening milking;

4.14.1.b.m: With: 'This offering...' [he eats] the morning milking.

4.14.2.a.m: A non-Brahmin should not eat the curd-and-milk offering (sāṃnāyya).

4.14.3.a.m: From the praṇītā water inside the altar ground, the adhvaryu pours an unbroken stream of water;

4.14.3.b.s: sadasi sanme bhūyā ity ānīyamānāyāṃ japati
4.14.3.b.d: सदसि सन्मे भूया इत्य् आनीयमानायां जपति
4.14.3.b.m: While it is being led forth, [the sacrificer] whispers: 'Sitting in the assembly, may there be good for me!'

4.14.4.a.s: prācyāṃ diśi devā ṛtvijo mārjayantām ity etair yathāliṅgaṃ vyutsicya samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomi svām yonim apigacchata /
4.14.4.a.d: प्राच्यां दिशि देवा ऋत्विजो मार्जयन्ताम् इत्य् एतैर् यथालिङ्गं व्युत्सिच्य समुद्रं वः प्रहिणोमि स्वाम् योनिम् अपिगच्छत ।
4.14.4.a.m: Having poured it out in different directions according to the marks with these [formulas]: 'In the eastern direction may the divine priests cleanse themselves...', [he recites:] 'I send you to the ocean; go to your own source!

4.14.4.b.s: acchidraḥ prajayā bhūyāsaṃ mā parāseci matpaya ityantarvedi śeṣaṃ ninīya yadapsu te sarasvati goṣvaśveṣu yan madhu /
4.14.4.b.d: अच्छिद्रः प्रजया भूयासं मा परासेचि मत्पय इत्यन्तर्वेदि शेषं निनीय यदप्सु ते सरस्वति गोष्वश्वेषु यन् मधु ।
4.14.4.b.m: May I be unbroken with offspring; may my milk not be poured away!' Having poured the remainder inside the altar ground, [and with:] 'Whatever honey of yours is in the waters, O Sarasvatī, whatever in cows, in horses,

4.14.4.c.m: Therewith, O swift one, anoint my face, O Sarasvatī!

4.14.4.d.s: yā sarasvatī vaiśambalyā tasyāṃ me rāsva tasyāste bhakṣīya tasyāste bhūyiṣṭhabhājo bhūyāsmeti mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe
4.14.4.d.d: या सरस्वती वैशम्बल्या तस्यां मे रास्व तस्यास्ते भक्षीय तस्यास्ते भूयिष्ठभाजो भूयास्मेति मुखं विमृष्टे
4.14.4.d.m: The Sarasvatī who is Vaiśambalyā, grant [a share] in her to me; may I partake of her; may we be the greatest recipients of her!' he wipes his face.

4.14.5.a.m: Both whisper the formula for releasing the potsherds.

4.14.6.a.s: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'sīti dakṣiṇe vedyante dakṣiṇena padā caturo viṣṇukramānprācaḥ krāmatyuttaramuttaraṃ jyāyāmsamanatiharansavyam
4.14.6.a.d: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति दक्षिणे वेद्यन्ते दक्षिणेन पदा चतुरो विष्णुक्रमान्प्राचः क्रामत्युत्तरमुत्तरं ज्यायाम्समनतिहरन्सव्यम्
4.14.6.a.m: With: 'You are the stride of Viṣṇu,' on the southern edge of the altar ground, he takes four Viṣṇu-strides towards the east with the right foot, each succeeding stride greater, without crossing the left foot over.

4.14.7.a.m: He does not step beyond the āhavanīya.

4.14.8.a.m: Stopping short, he whispers the fourth.

4.14.9.a.s: viṣṇukramān viṣṇvatikramān atīmokṣān iti vyatiṣaktān eke samāmananti /
4.14.9.a.d: विष्णुक्रमान् विष्ण्वतिक्रमान् अतीमोक्षान् इति व्यतिषक्तान् एके समामनन्ति ।
4.14.9.a.m: Some teach the Viṣṇu-strides, Viṣṇu-over-strides, and releases intertwined;

4.14.10.a.m: 'With the god Agni I conquer the armies'—these are the Viṣṇu-over-strides;

4.14.10.b.m: 'Which gods slay the sacrifice...'—these are the releases.

4.14.11.a.m: With: 'We have gone to the light, to the light we have gone,' he pays reverence to the sun.

4.15.1.a.m: 'Rising today, O you of friendly majesty, destroy my rivals!

4.15.1.b.m: Slay them by day with lightning; setting, make them sink below!

4.15.1.c.s: udyannadya vi no bhaja pitā putrebhyo yathā /
4.15.1.c.d: उद्यन्नद्य वि नो भज पिता पुत्रेभ्यो यथा ।
4.15.1.c.m: Rising today, apportion to us as a father to his sons;

4.15.1.d.s: dīrghāyutvasya heśiṣe tasya no dehi sūrya //
4.15.1.d.d: दीर्घायुत्वस्य हेशिषे तस्य नो देहि सूर्य ॥
4.15.1.d.m: For you rule over longevity: grant that to us, O Sūrya!

4.15.1.e.m: Rising today, O you of friendly majesty, ascending to the higher sky,

4.15.1.f.s: hṛdrogaṃ mama sūrya harimāṇaṃ ca nāśaya //
4.15.1.f.d: हृद्रोगं मम सूर्य हरिमाणं च नाशय ॥
4.15.1.f.m: My heartache and jaundice, O Sūrya, banish!

4.15.1.g.m: Into parrots and starling-birds we deposit my jaundice,

4.15.1.h.m: And also into yellow wagtails we deposit my jaundice.

4.15.1.i.m: This sun has risen together with all power,

4.15.1.j.s: dviṣantaṃ mama randhayanmo ahaṃ dviṣato radham //
4.15.1.j.d: द्विषन्तं मम रन्धयन्मो अहं द्विषतो रधम् ॥
4.15.1.j.m: Subduing him who hates me; let me not be subdued by him who hates me!

4.15.1.k.s: yo naḥ śapādaśapato yaśca naḥ śapataḥ śapāt /
4.15.1.k.d: यो नः शपादशपतो यश्च नः शपतः शपात् ।
4.15.1.k.m: He who curses us when we curse not, and he who curses us when we curse,

4.15.1.l.s: uṣāśca tasmai nimrukca sarvaṃ pāpaṃ samūhatām iti ca
4.15.1.l.d: उषाश्च तस्मै निम्रुक्च सर्वं पापं समूहताम् इति च
4.15.1.l.m: Upon him may dawn and sunset sweep together all evil!' and with this.

4.15.2.a.m: With: 'I turn with the turning of Indra,' he turns sunwise.

4.15.3.a.s: yadyabhicaredidamahamamuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya prāṇaṃ niveṣṭayāmīti dakṣiṇasya padaḥ pārṣṇyā nimṛdgīyāt
4.15.3.a.d: यद्यभिचरेदिदमहममुष्यामुष्यायणस्य प्राणं निवेष्टयामीति दक्षिणस्य पदः पार्ष्ण्या निमृद्गीयात्
4.15.3.a.m: If he should practice sorcery, he should crush [the ground] with the heel of his right foot, saying: 'Here I wrap up the life-breath of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'

4.15.4.a.s: puṇyā bhavantu yā lakṣmīḥ parābhavantu yāḥ pāpīrity uktvā samahaṃ prajayā saṃ mayā prajeti punarupāvartate
4.15.4.a.d: पुण्या भवन्तु या लक्ष्मीः पराभवन्तु याः पापीरित्य् उक्त्वा समहं प्रजया सं मया प्रजेति पुनरुपावर्तते
4.15.4.a.m: Having said: 'May the good fortunes become auspicious; may the evil fortunes perish,' he turns back with: 'Together may I be with offspring, together with me may offspring be!'

4.15.5.a.s: samiddho agne me dīdihi sameddhā te agne dīdyāsamityāhavanīyamupasaminddhe /
4.15.5.a.d: समिद्धो अग्ने मे दीदिहि समेद्धा ते अग्ने दीद्यासमित्याहवनीयमुपसमिन्द्धे ।
4.15.5.a.m: With: 'Enkindled, O Agni, shine for me; enkindling, may I shine for you, O Agni!' he kindles the āhavanīya;

4.15.5.b.m: With: 'Possessing wealth is the sacrifice, may I become wealthier!' he pays reverence [to it].

4.16.1.a.s: yo naḥ sapatno yo 'raṇo marto 'bhidāsati devāḥ /
4.16.1.a.d: यो नः सपत्नो यो ऽरणो मर्तो ऽभिदासति देवाः ।
4.16.1.a.m: "Whatever rival of ours, whatever alien mortal plots against us, O gods,

4.16.1.b.s: idhmasyeva prakṣāyato mā tasyoccheṣi kiṃcaneti ca
4.16.1.b.d: इध्मस्येव प्रक्षायतो मा तस्योच्छेषि किंचनेति च
4.16.1.b.m: like a burning log of firewood, let nothing of him remain!"—and with this [he attends the āhavanīya].

4.16.2.a.s: agna āyūṃṣi pavasa ity āgnipāvamānībhyāṃ gārhapatyamupatiṣṭhate /
4.16.2.a.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवस इत्य् आग्निपावमानीभ्यां गार्हपत्यमुपतिष्ठते ।
4.16.2.a.m: With the two verses addressed to Agni Pavamāna, "O Agni, you purify our life-spans", he attends the gārhapatya,

4.16.3.a.s: putrasya nāma gṛhṇāti tāmāśiṣamāśāse tantava ity ajātasya /
4.16.3.a.d: पुत्रस्य नाम गृह्णाति तामाशिषमाशासे तन्तव इत्य् अजातस्य ।
4.16.3.a.m: He mentions the name of his son: for one unborn, with "I pray for that blessing for the lineage";

4.16.4.a.s: jyotiṣe tantave tvāsāvanu mā tanvacchinno daivyastantur mā manuṣyaśchedi divyāddhāmno mā cchitsi mā mānuṣāditi priyasya putrasya nāma gṛhṇāti
4.16.4.a.d: ज्योतिषे तन्तवे त्वासावनु मा तन्वच्छिन्नो दैव्यस्तन्तुर् मा मनुष्यश्छेदि दिव्याद्धाम्नो मा च्छित्सि मा मानुषादिति प्रियस्य पुत्रस्य नाम गृह्णाति
4.16.4.a.m: With: "For light, for lineage, you, so-and-so, may you stretch out after me; may the divine thread not be broken, may the human thread not be severed; may I not be cut off from the divine realm, nor from the human!", he mentions the name of his beloved son.

4.16.5.a.s: agne vahne svaditaṃ nastanaye pituṃ paca /
4.16.5.a.d: अग्ने वह्ने स्वदितं नस्तनये पितुं पच ।
4.16.5.a.m: "O Agni, the conveyer, cook well-seasoned food for our offspring,

4.16.5.b.s: śaṃ tokāya tanuve syona iti dakṣiṇāgnim
4.16.5.b.d: शं तोकाय तनुवे स्योन इति दक्षिणाग्निम्
4.16.5.b.m: peace for our descendants, pleasant for our bodies"—with this [he attends] the dakṣiṇāgni.

4.16.6.a.m: With: "For light, for lineage, to you…", he sits down inside the altar ground.

4.16.6.b.m: The mentioning of the name is as before.

4.16.7.a.m: Having sat down, he whispers: "You are light, for lineage…".

4.16.8.a.m: Having placed the veda on his lap, seated inside the altar ground, he whispers the Atīmokṣa formulas.

4.16.9.a.s: atra vedastaraṇaṃ yajamānabhāgasya ca prāśanam eke samāmananti
4.16.9.a.d: अत्र वेदस्तरणं यजमानभागस्य च प्राशनम् एके समामनन्ति
4.16.9.a.m: At this point, some teachers prescribe the strewing of the veda and the consumption of the sacrificer's share.

4.16.10.a.s: kastvā yunakti sa tvā vimuñcatviti yajñaṃ vimuñcati
4.16.10.a.d: कस्त्वा युनक्ति स त्वा विमुञ्चत्विति यज्ञं विमुञ्चति
4.16.10.a.m: With: "Who unyokes you? May he unyoke you", he unyokes the sacrifice.

4.16.11.a.s: agne vratapate vratam acāriṣam iti vrataṃ visṛjate
4.16.11.a.d: अग्ने व्रतपते व्रतम् अचारिषम् इति व्रतं विसृजते
4.16.11.a.m: With: "O Agni, lord of vows, I have observed my vow", he releases the vow.

4.16.12.a.m: With: "The sacrifice has come to be", he whispers the formula for resuming the sacrifice.

4.16.13.a.m: Having stepped forward toward the east, he whispers the Gomatī verse: "Possessing cows…".

4.16.14.a.m: Or at this point he may consume the sacrificer's share.

4.16.15.a.s: yajña śaṃ ca ma upa ca ma āyuśca me balaṃ ca me yajña śivo me saṃtiṣṭhasva yajña sviṣṭo me saṃtiṣṭhasva yajñāriṣṭo me saṃtiṣṭhasveti darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ somena paśunā veṣṭvā japati
4.16.15.a.d: यज्ञ शं च म उप च म आयुश्च मे बलं च मे यज्ञ शिवो मे संतिष्ठस्व यज्ञ स्विष्टो मे संतिष्ठस्व यज्ञारिष्टो मे संतिष्ठस्वेति दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यां सोमेन पशुना वेष्ट्वा जपति
4.16.15.a.m: Having sacrificed with the New and Full Moon sacrifices, or with soma, or with an animal sacrifice, he whispers: "O sacrifice, be peace to me and access to me, life to me and strength to me; O sacrifice, turn out auspiciously for me; O sacrifice, turn out well-offered for me; O sacrifice, turn out unharmed for me!".

4.16.16.a.m: With: "You are rain; cut off my evil! From non-truth I have arrived at truth", having sacrificed, he touches water.

4.16.16.b.m: This touching [of water] applies in all sacrifices.

4.16.18.a.m: When he is setting out on a journey, facing the sacred hearths at the proper time, he whispers the sacrificer's formulas.

4.16.19.a.m: He takes the Viṣṇu strides towards the east.

4.16.20.a.m: Having stepped forward toward the east, he whispers, he whispers the Gomatī verse.

5.1.1.a.m: We shall explain the setting up of the sacred fires.

5.1.2.a.s: yo aśvatthaḥ śamīgarbha āruroha tve sacā /
5.1.2.a.d: यो अश्वत्थः शमीगर्भ आरुरोह त्वे सचा ।
5.1.2.a.m: "The aśvattha tree which grew inside the śamī, having ascended together with you:

5.1.2.b.s: taṃ te harāmi brahmaṇā yajñiyaiḥ ketubhiḥ saheti śamīgarbhasyāśvatthasyāraṇī āharati
5.1.2.b.d: तं ते हरामि ब्रह्मणा यज्ञियैः केतुभिः सहेति शमीगर्भस्याश्वत्थस्यारणी आहरति
5.1.2.b.m: that [wood] of yours I fetch with sacred prayer along with sacrificial signs"—with this he fetches the two kindling sticks from an aśvattha tree grown inside a śamī tree.

5.1.3.a.m: Even if not grown inside a śamī tree, says the Vājasaneyaka.

5.1.4.a.m: "From the aśvattha, from the conveyer of oblations, I collect the sacrificial body of Agni that is born:

5.1.4.b.m: having a peaceful womb, born inside a śamī, for Agni to be generated!

5.1.4.c.s: āyurmayi dhehyāyuryajamāna ityaraṇī abhimantrya sapta pārthivān saṃ bhārānāharati /
5.1.4.c.d: आयुर्मयि धेह्यायुर्यजमान इत्यरणी अभिमन्त्र्य सप्त पार्थिवान् सं भारानाहरति ।
5.1.4.c.m: Bestow life upon me, life upon the sacrificer"—having addressed the two kindling sticks with this, he fetches the seven earthly materials

5.1.6.a.m: He should not collect the materials, says the Vājasaneyaka.

5.1.7.a.m: "Form of Vaiśvānara, overflowing upon the earth,

5.1.7.b.m: let them enter our abode gently"—[with this he fetches] sand.

5.1.7.c.s: yadidaṃ divo yadadaḥ pṛthivyāḥ saṃjajñāne rodasī saṃbabhūvatuḥ /
5.1.7.c.d: यदिदं दिवो यददः पृथिव्याः संजज्ञाने रोदसी संबभूवतुः ।
5.1.7.c.m: "Whatever is this of heaven, whatever is that of earth, the two world-halves having agreed came into being;

5.1.7.d.m: may the saline soil protect the black antelope skin, may the black antelope skin protect the saline soil; the most fit for sacrifice of both has come here"—[with this he fetches] saline soil.

5.1.7.e.m: "Providing protections, when you wandered over the earth, assuming a hidden form, taking on the shape of a mole:

5.1.7.f.s: tatte nyaktamiha saṃbharantaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ suvīrā ityākhukarīṣam //
5.1.7.f.d: तत्ते न्यक्तमिह संभरन्तः शतं जीवेम शरदः सुवीरा इत्याखुकरीषम् ॥
5.1.7.f.m: collecting here that indented trace of yours, may we live a hundred autumns with good heroes!"—[with this he fetches] molehill-earth.

5.1.7.g.s: ūrjaṃ pṛthivyā rasamābharantaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ purūcīḥ /
5.1.7.g.d: ऊर्जं पृथिव्या रसमाभरन्तः शतं जीवेम शरदः पुरूचीः ।
5.1.7.g.m: "Bringing vigor, the sap of the earth, may we live a hundred full autumns;

5.1.7.h.s: vamrībhiranuvittaṃ guhāsu śrotraṃ ta urvyabadhirā bhavāma iti valmīkavapām //
5.1.7.h.d: वम्रीभिरनुवित्तं गुहासु श्रोत्रं त उर्व्यबधिरा भवाम इति वल्मीकवपाम् ॥
5.1.7.h.m: found by the ants in the cavities, O wide earth, may we become non-deaf ears to you"—[with this he fetches] an anthill-core.

5.1.7.i.s: prajāpatisṛṣṭānāṃ prajānāṃ kṣudho 'pahatyai suvitaṃ no astu /
5.1.7.i.d: प्रजापतिसृष्टानां प्रजानां क्षुधो ऽपहत्यै सुवितं नो अस्तु ।
5.1.7.i.m: "For the warding off of hunger of the creatures created by Prajāpati, may there be welfare for us;

5.1.7.j.s: upaprabhinnamiṣamūrjaṃ prajābhyaḥ sūdaṃ gṛhebhyo rasamābharāmīti sūdam //
5.1.7.j.d: उपप्रभिन्नमिषमूर्जं प्रजाभ्यः सूदं गृहेभ्यो रसमाभरामीति सूदम् ॥
5.1.7.j.m: food and vigor split open for the creatures, mud, the sap, I fetch for the houses"—[with this he fetches] swamp-mud.

5.1.7.k.s: yasya rūpaṃ bibhradimāmavindadguhā praviṣṭāṃ sarirasya madhye /
5.1.7.k.d: यस्य रूपं बिभ्रदिमामविन्दद्गुहा प्रविष्टां सरिरस्य मध्ये ।
5.1.7.k.m: "Bearing whose form, he found her who had entered the hidden depths in the midst of the water:

5.1.7.l.m: fetching here this earth turned up by him, may we perform worship on her without stumbling!"—[with this he fetches] earth turned up by a boar.

5.2.1.a.m: "With which he made firm the support of the world, this broad supporter of all people,

5.2.1.b.s: tā naḥ śivāḥ śarkarāḥ santu sarvā iti śarkarāḥ //
5.2.1.b.d: ता नः शिवाः शर्कराः सन्तु सर्वा इति शर्कराः ॥
5.2.1.b.m: may all those gravel-stones be auspicious to us"—[with this he fetches] gravel-stones.

5.2.1.c.m: "Agni's seed, shining, gold born from the waters, immortal among offspring:

5.2.1.d.m: collecting that, placing it on the north, handing it over, may I cross beyond misfortune"—[with this he fetches] gold.

5.2.3.a.m: If there are five, pieces of udumbara wood or pieces of copper become the fifth.

5.2.4.a.s: aśvo rūpaṃ kṛtvā yadaśvatthe 'tiṣṭhaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ devebhyo nilāya /
5.2.4.a.d: अश्वो रूपं कृत्वा यदश्वत्थे ऽतिष्ठः संवत्सरं देवेभ्यो निलाय ।
5.2.4.a.m: "Assuming the form of a horse, when you stayed in the aśvattha for a year, hiding from the gods:

5.2.4.b.s: tatte nyaktamiha saṃbharantaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ suvīrā ity aśvattham //
5.2.4.b.d: तत्ते न्यक्तमिह संभरन्तः शतं जीवेम शरदः सुवीरा इत्य् अश्वत्थम् ॥
5.2.4.b.m: collecting here that indented trace of yours, may we live a hundred autumns with good heroes!"—[with this he fetches] aśvattha wood.

5.2.4.c.s: ūrjaḥ pṛthivyā adhyutthito 'si vanaspate śatavalśo viroha /
5.2.4.c.d: ऊर्जः पृथिव्या अध्युत्थितो ऽसि वनस्पते शतवल्शो विरोह ।
5.2.4.c.m: "You have arisen from the vigor of the earth; O tree, sprout with a hundred branches!

5.2.4.d.s: tvayā vayamiṣamūrjaṃ madanto rāyaspoṣeṇa samiṣā mademetyudumbaram //
5.2.4.d.d: त्वया वयमिषमूर्जं मदन्तो रायस्पोषेण समिषा मदेमेत्युदुम्बरम् ॥
5.2.4.d.m: Exulting in food and vigor through you, may we exult in wealth and prosperity, with abundance of food"—[with this he fetches] udumbara wood.

5.2.4.e.d: गायत्रिया ह्रियमाणस्य यत्ते पर्णमपतत्तृतीयस्यै दिवो ऽधि ।
5.2.4.e.m: "What leaf of yours fell from the third heaven as it was being carried away by the Gāyatrī...

5.2.4.f.s: so 'yaṃ parṇaḥ somaparṇāddhi jātastato harāmi somapīthasyāvaruddhyai //
5.2.4.f.d: सो ऽयं पर्णः सोमपर्णाद्धि जातस्ततो हरामि सोमपीथस्यावरुद्ध्यै ॥
5.2.4.f.m: ‘This parṇa tree was born from the leaf of Soma; therefore I fetch it to obtain the drinking of Soma.’

5.2.4.g.s: devānāṃ brahmavādaṃ vadatāṃ yadupāśṛṇoḥ suśravā vai śruto 'si /
5.2.4.g.d: देवानां ब्रह्मवादं वदतां यदुपाशृणोः सुश्रवा वै श्रुतो ऽसि ।
5.2.4.g.m: ‘As you listened to the gods speaking of sacred lore, you are indeed renowned as Suśravas;

5.2.4.h.s: tato māmāviśatu brahmavarcasaṃ tatsaṃbharaṃstadavarundhīya sākṣādityetābhyāṃ parṇam //
5.2.4.h.d: ततो मामाविशतु ब्रह्मवर्चसं तत्संभरंस्तदवरुन्धीय साक्षादित्येताभ्यां पर्णम् ॥
5.2.4.h.m: may spiritual radiance enter me therefrom; bringing it together, may I obtain that directly’—with these two [verses he fetches the wood of] the parṇa tree.

5.2.4.i.m: ‘With which Prajāpati pacified the missile of Agni when he had been created,

5.2.4.j.m: that śamī tree I fetch for appeasement, that there be no burning down’—[with this verse he fetches the wood of] the śamī tree.

5.2.4.k.s: yatte sṛṣṭasya yato vikaṅkataṃ bhā ārchajjātavedaḥ /
5.2.4.k.d: यत्ते सृष्टस्य यतो विकङ्कतं भा आर्छज्जातवेदः ।
5.2.4.k.m: ‘When you were created, O Jātavedas, from whom radiance reached the vikaṅkata tree,

5.2.4.l.s: tayā bhāsā saṃmita uruṃ no lokamanuprabhāhīti vikaṅkatam /
5.2.4.l.d: तया भासा संमित उरुं नो लोकमनुप्रभाहीति विकङ्कतम् ।
5.2.4.l.m: measuring up to us with that radiance, shine along our wide world’—[with this verse he fetches the wood of] the vikaṅkata tree.

5.2.4.m.m: ‘When you were moving, O Jātavedas, the Maruts, causing rain with waters, snatched away your heart;

5.2.4.n.s: etat te tad aśaneḥ saṃbharāmi sātmā agne sahṛdayo bhavehetyaśanihatasya vṛkṣasya //
5.2.4.n.d: एतत् ते तद् अशनेः संभरामि सात्मा अग्ने सहृदयो भवेहेत्यशनिहतस्य वृक्षस्य ॥
5.2.4.n.m: this of yours I collect from that lightning; O Agni, become embodied, endowed with a heart here’—[with this verse he fetches the wood] of a lightning-struck tree.

5.2.4.o.m: ‘When he looked around the middle of the sea, he saw the broad earth, the foundation of the world;

5.2.4.p.s: tatpuṣkarasyāyatanāddhi jātaṃ parṇaṃ pṛthivyāḥ prathanaṃ harāmīti puṣkaraparṇam //
5.2.4.p.d: तत्पुष्करस्यायतनाद्धि जातं पर्णं पृथिव्याः प्रथनं हरामीति पुष्करपर्णम् ॥
5.2.4.p.m: that leaf born from the abode of the lotus, the expansion of the earth, I fetch’—[with this verse he fetches] a lotus leaf.

5.3.1.a.s: yaṃ tvā samabharaṃ jātavedo yathā śarīraṃ bhūteṣu nyaktam /
5.3.1.a.d: यं त्वा समभरं जातवेदो यथा शरीरं भूतेषु न्यक्तम् ।
5.3.1.a.m: ‘Thee, whom I have collected, O Jātavedas, as the body embedded in beings,

5.3.1.b.s: sa saṃbhṛtaḥ sīda śivaḥ prajābhya uruṃ no lokamanuneṣi vidvāniti saṃbhṛtya nidadhāti
5.3.1.b.d: स संभृतः सीद शिवः प्रजाभ्य उरुं नो लोकमनुनेषि विद्वानिति संभृत्य निदधाति
5.3.1.b.m: do thou, thus collected, sit auspicious for offspring; knowing, lead us to the wide world’—having collected [them], he deposits them [with this verse].

5.3.3.a.s: kṛttikāsu brāhmaṇa ādadhīta mukhyo brahmavarcasī bhavati
5.3.3.a.d: कृत्तिकासु ब्राह्मण आदधीत मुख्यो ब्रह्मवर्चसी भवति
5.3.3.a.m: A brāhmaṇa should set up [the fires] under the Kṛttikās; he becomes eminent [and] endowed with spiritual radiance.

5.3.4.a.m: His fire burns down his houses.

5.3.5.a.m: Having set them up under Rohiṇī, he attains all attainments.

5.3.6.a.m: Under Mṛgaśīrṣa, one who is desirous of spiritual radiance or desirous of sacrifice [should set them up].

5.3.7.a.m: One who, having previously been prosperous, has become degraded, [should set them up] under the Punarvasus.

5.3.8.a.s: pūrvayoḥ phalgunyoryaḥ kāmayeta dānakāmā me prajā syur iti
5.3.8.a.d: पूर्वयोः फल्गुन्योर्यः कामयेत दानकामा मे प्रजा स्युर् इति
5.3.8.a.m: Under the Pūrva Phalgunīs, one who desires: ‘May my offspring be generous!’

5.3.9.a.m: Under the Uttara [Phalgunīs], one who desires: ‘May I be fortunate and an eater of food!’

5.3.11.b.s: pūrvayor ādhāya pāpīyān bhavaty uttarayor vasīyān
