5.3.11.b.d: पूर्वयोर् आधाय पापीयान् भवत्य् उत्तरयोर् वसीयान्
5.3.11.b.m: Having set them up under the former, he becomes worse off; under the latter, he becomes wealthier.

5.3.12.a.s: haste yaḥ kāmayeta pra me dīyeteti
5.3.12.a.d: हस्ते यः कामयेत प्र मे दीयेतेति
5.3.12.a.m: Under Hasta, one who desires: ‘May [gifts] be given to me!’

5.3.13.a.m: Under Citrā, a rājanya or one who has a rival [should set them up].

5.3.14.a.s: viśākhayoḥ prajākāmo 'nurādheṣvṛddhikāmaḥ śravaṇe puṣṭikāma uttareṣu proṣṭhapadeṣu pratiṣṭhākāmaḥ
5.3.14.a.d: विशाखयोः प्रजाकामो ऽनुराधेष्वृद्धिकामः श्रवणे पुष्टिकाम उत्तरेषु प्रोष्ठपदेषु प्रतिष्ठाकामः
5.3.14.a.m: Under the Viśākhās, one desirous of offspring; under Anurādhā, one desirous of prosperity; under Śravaṇa, one desirous of nourishment; under the Uttara Proṣṭhapadās, one desirous of a firm foundation.

5.3.15.a.m: Some recite all [these asterisms] as optional alternatives.

5.3.16.a.d: फल्गुनीपूर्णमास आदधीतेत्युक्त्वाह यत्फल्गुनीपूर्णमास आदध्यात्संवत्सरस्यैनमासन्दध्याद्द्व्यहे पुरैकाहे वा
5.3.16.a.m: Having said: ‘He should set up [the fires] at the Phalgunī full moon,’ [the sacred text] says: ‘If he sets them up at the Phalgunī full moon, he would set them up in the face of the year, two days before or one day before.’

5.3.17.a.m: They are to be set up on a new moon or on a full moon.

5.3.18.a.s: vasanto brāhmaṇasya grīṣmo rājanyasya hemanto vā śaradvaiśyasya varṣā rathakārasya
5.3.18.a.d: वसन्तो ब्राह्मणस्य ग्रीष्मो राजन्यस्य हेमन्तो वा शरद्वैश्यस्य वर्षा रथकारस्य
5.3.18.a.m: Spring is for a brāhmaṇa, summer or winter for a rājanya, autumn for a vaiśya, the rainy season for a chariot-maker.

5.3.19.a.m: Those who perform this work belonging to the three castes—this is the time for them.

5.3.20.a.m: The cool season is common to all castes.

5.3.21.a.m: One who intends to sacrifice with soma should heed neither season nor asterism.

5.3.22.a.m: A householder should set up [the fires] after moving to a new abode; a wanderer without moving to a new abode.

5.4.1.a.m: ‘May the impure evil of this earth, being dug up, strike down the sin of the sacrificer;

5.4.1.b.s: śivā naḥ santu pradiśaścatasraḥ śaṃ no mātā pṛthivī tokasāteti prācīnapravaṇaṃ devayajanamuddhatya śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaya āpo bhavantu pītaye /
5.4.1.b.d: शिवा नः सन्तु प्रदिशश्चतस्रः शं नो माता पृथिवी तोकसातेति प्राचीनप्रवणं देवयजनमुद्धत्य शं नो देवीरभिष्टय आपो भवन्तु पीतये ।
5.4.1.b.m: may the four quarters be auspicious for us, may mother earth be salutary to us for gaining offspring’—having thus prepared the sacrificial place sloping towards the east; and [saying]: ‘May the divine waters be for our aid, for our drinking;

5.4.1.c.s: śaṃyorabhisravantu na ity adbhir avokṣya tasminnudīcīnavaṃśaṃ śaraṇaṃ karoti
5.4.1.c.d: शंयोरभिस्रवन्तु न इत्य् अद्भिर् अवोक्ष्य तस्मिन्नुदीचीनवंशं शरणं करोति
5.4.1.c.m: may they flow towards us for wellbeing and blessing’—having sprinkled [the ground] with waters, he constructs a shelter with its ridgepole pointing north.

5.4.2.a.m: In front of its central beam is the fireplace of the gārhapatya.

5.4.3.a.m: Eastward from that at [a distance of] eight paces is the fireplace of the āhavanīya for a brāhmaṇa;

5.4.4.a.s: caturviṃśatyāmaparimite yāvatā vā cakṣuṣā manyate tasmānnātidūramādheya iti sarveṣāmaviśeṣeṇa śrūyate
5.4.4.a.d: चतुर्विंशत्यामपरिमिते यावता वा चक्षुषा मन्यते तस्मान्नातिदूरमाधेय इति सर्वेषामविशेषेण श्रूयते
5.4.4.a.m: ‘At twenty-four, [or] at an unmeasured [distance], or as far as he considers by sight: from that [distance] it should not be set up too far’—so it is heard without distinction for all.

5.4.5.a.m: To the south-east, in the third-part space nearer to the gārhapatya, is the fireplace of the dakṣiṇāgni.

5.4.6.a.m: One shed is for the āhavanīya; another for the gārhapatya.

5.4.7.a.m: In front of the āhavanīya, in the assembly hall, is the sabhya fire.

5.4.8.a.m: East of it, in the residence, is the āvasathya fire.

5.4.9.a.m: He shaves his head and beard, pares his nails, and bathes.

5.4.10.a.m: Wearing linen garments, the husband and wife should set up the fires.

5.4.11.a.m: Those [garments] they give to the adhvaryu at the time of the sacrificial gifts.

5.4.12.a.m: In the afternoon, or when the sun is above the trees, having brought fire from the aupāsana [fire], he sets up the brāhmaudanika fire behind the gārhapatya fireplace.

5.4.15.a.s: yadi sarvamaupāsanamāharedapūpaṃ yavamayaṃ vrīhimayaṃ caudumbaraparṇābhyāṃ saṃgṛhyāyatana upāsyedyavamayaṃ paścādvrīhimayaṃ purastāttasminnādadhyāt
5.4.15.a.d: यदि सर्वमौपासनमाहरेदपूपं यवमयं व्रीहिमयं चौदुम्बरपर्णाभ्यां संगृह्यायतन उपास्येद्यवमयं पश्चाद्व्रीहिमयं पुरस्तात्तस्मिन्नादध्यात्
5.4.15.a.m: If he brings the entire aupāsana [fire], he should wrap a barley cake and a rice cake with two udumbara leaves and cast them into the fireplace—the barley cake in the west, the rice cake in the east—[and] set up [the fire] upon that.

5.4.16.a.m: Even when bringing the entire aupāsana fire, he need not cast the two cakes—thus another [rule].

5.5.1.a.s: apareṇa brāhmaudanikaṃ lohite carmaṇyānaḍuhe prācīnagrīva uttaralomni pājake vā niśāyāṃ brahmaudanaṃ catuḥśarāvaṃ nirvapati
5.5.1.a.d: अपरेण ब्राह्मौदनिकं लोहिते चर्मण्यानडुहे प्राचीनग्रीव उत्तरलोम्नि पाजके वा निशायां ब्रह्मौदनं चतुःशरावं निर्वपति
5.5.1.a.m: Behind the brāhmaudanika fire, on a red ox-hide with the neck to the east and the hairy side turned up, or in a winnowing basket, at night, he measures out the four-cup mess of cooked rice for the brāhmaṇas.

5.5.2.a.s: devasya tvetyanudrutya brahmaṇe prāṇāya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmīti prathamamapānāyeti dvitīyaṃ vyānāyeti tṛtīyaṃ brahmaṇe juṣṭam iti caturtham
5.5.2.a.d: देवस्य त्वेत्यनुद्रुत्य ब्रह्मणे प्राणाय जुष्टं निर्वपामीति प्रथममपानायेति द्वितीयं व्यानायेति तृतीयं ब्रह्मणे जुष्टम् इति चतुर्थम्
5.5.2.a.m: Having recited after ‘At the impulse of god Savitṛ…’, [he pours it out saying]: ‘For the Brahman, for the out-breath, I measure thee out, agreeable’—the first [cup]; ‘For the in-breath’—the second; ‘For the diffused breath’—the third; ‘For the Brahman, agreeable’—the fourth.

5.5.4.a.m: He cooks [it] in four water vessels.

5.5.5.a.m: He does not wash [the grains], nor does he drain off the water.

5.5.7.a.m: "He cooks it so that the grains remain as if alive," thus it is known from the scripture.

5.5.8.a.s: darvyā brahmaudanāduddhṛtya pra vedhase kavaye medhyāya vaco vandāru vṛṣabhāya vṛṣṇe /
5.5.8.a.d: दर्व्या ब्रह्मौदनादुद्धृत्य प्र वेधसे कवये मेध्याय वचो वन्दारु वृषभाय वृष्णे ।
5.5.8.a.m: Having ladled out from the brahmaudana with a spoon, [with the verse:] "To the wise, the poet, the holy, reverent speech to the bull, the manly;

5.5.8.b.s: yato bhayamabhayaṃ tanno astvava devānyajeheḍyāniti juhoty abhi vā mantrayate
5.5.8.b.d: यतो भयमभयं तन्नो अस्त्वव देवान्यजेहेड्यानिति जुहोत्य् अभि वा मन्त्रयते
5.5.8.b.m: From where there is fear, let there be fearlessness for us; turn aside the anger of the gods!"—he offers, or he recites over [it].

5.5.9.a.s: caturdhā brahmaudanaṃ vyuddhṛtya prabhūtena sarpiṣopasicya karṣannanucchindaṃścaturbhya ārṣeyebhya ṛtvigbhya upohati
5.5.9.a.d: चतुर्धा ब्रह्मौदनं व्युद्धृत्य प्रभूतेन सर्पिषोपसिच्य कर्षन्ननुच्छिन्दंश्चतुर्भ्य आर्षेयेभ्य ऋत्विग्भ्य उपोहति
5.5.9.a.m: Having apportioned the brahmaudana into four parts and poured plenty of clarified butter over it, dragging it without lifting it off, he pushes it toward the four officiating priests of ṛṣi descent.

5.5.10.a.m: "The first morsels are taken; the hands are unimpeded;

5.5.10.b.s: atha brahmaudanaśeṣaṃ saṃkṛṣya tasminnājyaśeṣamānīya tasmiṃścitriyasyāśvatthasya tisraḥ samidha ārdrāḥ sapalāśāḥ prādeśamātryaḥ stibhigavatyo vivartayati
5.5.10.b.d: अथ ब्रह्मौदनशेषं संकृष्य तस्मिन्नाज्यशेषमानीय तस्मिंश्चित्रियस्याश्वत्थस्य तिस्रः समिध आर्द्राः सपलाशाः प्रादेशमात्र्यः स्तिभिगवत्यो विवर्तयति
5.5.10.b.m: Then, having gathered the remainder of the brahmaudana, poured the remainder of the clarified butter into it, he rolls in it three wet firewood sticks with leaves, a span in length and possessing sprouts, from an aśvattha tree grown on a holy site,

5.6.1.a.m: [reciting:] "Gathered from an aśvattha grown on a holy site, great ones, you have prepared the body;

5.6.1.b.m: Equal to Prajāpati, the mouth of the sacrifice, three united with threefold [qualities] for procreation."

5.6.2.a.m: Then he places [them on the fire] with butter-filled verses dedicated to Agni: with Gāyatrī verses for a Brāhmaṇa, with Triṣṭubh verses for a Rājanya, with Jagatī verses for a Vaiśya.

5.6.3.a.m: "Attend upon Agni with firewood..." is this [first verse].

5.6.3.b.m: "To you, O Agni, let the butter-bearing [ladles], full of oblation, go, O lovely one;

5.6.3.d.m: "We increase you, that one, with firewood, O Aṅgiras, with clarified butter;

5.6.3.e.m: Flame up greatly, O youngest one!"—these are for a Brāhmaṇa.

5.6.3.f.s: samidhyamānaḥ prathamo nu dharmaḥ samaktubhirajyate viśvavāraḥ /
5.6.3.f.d: समिध्यमानः प्रथमो नु धर्मः समक्तुभिरज्यते विश्ववारः ।
5.6.3.f.m: "Being kindled, the first law is now anointed with balms, possessing all boons;

5.6.3.g.s: śociṣkeśo ghṛtanirṇik pāvakaḥ suyajño agniryajathāya devān //
5.6.3.g.d: शोचिष्केशो घृतनिर्णिक् पावकः सुयज्ञो अग्निर्यजथाय देवान् ॥
5.6.3.g.m: Flaming-haired, robed in clarified butter, purifying, of fair sacrifice, Agni [is ready] to sacrifice to the gods."

5.6.3.h.m: "Agni whose face is butter, whose womb is butter, kindled with butter; butter is his food;

5.6.3.i.s: ghṛtapruṣastvā sarito vahanti ghṛtaṃ pibansuyajā yakṣi devān //
5.6.3.i.d: घृतप्रुषस्त्वा सरितो वहन्ति घृतं पिबन्सुयजा यक्षि देवान् ॥
5.6.3.i.m: Streams dripping butter bear you; drinking butter, sacrifice well to the gods!"

5.6.3.j.m: "Giver of life, O Agni..."—these are for a Rājanya.

5.6.3.k.s: tvāmagne samidhānaṃ yaviṣṭha devā dūtaṃ cakrire havyavāham /
5.6.3.k.d: त्वामग्ने समिधानं यविष्ठ देवा दूतं चक्रिरे हव्यवाहम् ।
5.6.3.k.m: "The gods made you, O Agni, when kindled, O youngest one, their messenger, oblation-bearer;

5.6.3.l.m: Wide-ranging, having butter for your womb, offered unto, they placed brilliant sight in the impelling one."

5.6.3.m.s: tvāmagne pradiva āhutaṃ ghṛtena sumnāyavaḥ suṣamidhā samīdhire /
5.6.3.m.d: त्वामग्ने प्रदिव आहुतं घृतेन सुम्नायवः सुषमिधा समीधिरे ।
5.6.3.m.m: "You, O Agni, offered unto with butter since ancient times, those desirous of favour have kindled with good firewood;

5.6.3.n.s: sa vāvṛdhāna oṣadhībhirukṣita uru jrayāṃsi pārthivā vitiṣṭhase //
5.6.3.n.d: स वावृधान ओषधीभिरुक्षित उरु ज्रयांसि पार्थिवा वितिष्ठसे ॥
5.6.3.n.m: Having grown, invigorated by plants, you extend across the broad earthly expanses."

5.6.3.o.s: ghṛtapratīkaṃ va ṛtasya dhūrṣadamagniṃ mitraṃ na samidhāna ṛñjate /
5.6.3.o.d: घृतप्रतीकं व ऋतस्य धूर्षदमग्निं मित्रं न समिधान ऋञ्जते ।
5.6.3.o.m: "Agni, whose face is butter, who sits at the yoke of truth, they praise as a friend when kindling;

5.6.3.p.s: indhāno akro vidatheṣu dīdyacchukravarṇāmudu no yaṃsate dhiyamiti vaiśyasya
5.6.3.p.d: इन्धानो अक्रो विदथेषु दीद्यच्छुक्रवर्णामुदु नो यंसते धियमिति वैश्यस्य
5.6.3.p.m: The banner shining bright at the rites, burning, shall extend for us shining insight"—these are for a Vaiśya.

5.7.1.a.m: At the [placing of] the firewood sticks, he gives three heifers.

5.7.2.a.m: The Brāhmaṇas eat the boiled rice.

5.7.3.a.m: To those who have eaten, he gives an equal choice boon.

5.7.4.a.s: yasminnakṣatre 'gnimādhāsyansyāttasminsaṃvatsare purastādetāḥ samidha ādadhyāddvādaśāhe dvyahe tryaha ekāhe vā
5.7.4.a.d: यस्मिन्नक्षत्रे ऽग्निमाधास्यन्स्यात्तस्मिन्संवत्सरे पुरस्तादेताः समिध आदध्याद्द्वादशाहे द्व्यहे त्र्यह एकाहे वा
5.7.4.a.m: Under whatever asterism he intends to establish the fires, under that [same asterism] a year beforehand he should place these firewood sticks, or twelve days, or two days, or three days, or one day beforehand.

5.7.5.a.m: They must indeed be placed by one establishing the fire.

5.7.6.a.s: atha vrataṃ carati na māṃsamaśnāti na striyamupaiti nāsyāgniṃ gṛhāddharanti nānyata āharanti
5.7.6.a.d: अथ व्रतं चरति न मांसमश्नाति न स्त्रियमुपैति नास्याग्निं गृहाद्धरन्ति नान्यत आहरन्ति
5.7.6.a.m: Then he observes a vow: he does not eat meat, he does not approach a woman, they do not carry his fire away from the house, nor do they bring in [fire] from elsewhere.

5.7.7.a.m: He should remain for a year with the brahmaudana fire.

5.7.8.a.m: If the domestic fire has been established, his fire-rites are performed in this [fire].

5.7.11.a.s: yadi prayāyādanu vā gacchedbrahmaudanaṃ paktvaitayaivāvṛtā samidha ādadhyāt
5.7.11.a.d: यदि प्रयायादनु वा गच्छेद्ब्रह्मौदनं पक्त्वैतयैवावृता समिध आदध्यात्
5.7.11.a.m: If he goes on a journey or if it goes out, having cooked the brahmaudana, he should place the firewood sticks by this very ritual procedure.

5.7.12.a.s: yadyenaṃ saṃvatsare 'gnyādheyaṃ nopanamedbrahmaudanaṃ paktvā samidha ādhāya yadainamupanamedathādadhīta
5.7.12.a.d: यद्येनं संवत्सरे ऽग्न्याधेयं नोपनमेद्ब्रह्मौदनं पक्त्वा समिध आधाय यदैनमुपनमेदथादधीत
5.7.12.a.m: If the establishment of the fires does not present itself to him in the course of the year, having cooked the brahmaudana and placed the firewood sticks, he should establish [the fires] whenever it presents itself to him.

5.7.13.a.m: Concerning it, there is free choice among the modes of maintaining [the fire].

5.7.14.a.m: He should observe [the vow] for twelve days or for one day.

5.7.15.a.m: Intending to establish [the fires] on the morrow, he cooks the brahmaudana again.

5.7.16.a.s: yo 'syāgnimādhāsyan syāt sa etāṃ rātriṃ vrataṃ carati na māṃsam aśnāti na striyam upaiti
5.7.16.a.d: यो ऽस्याग्निमाधास्यन् स्यात् स एतां रात्रिं व्रतं चरति न मांसम् अश्नाति न स्त्रियम् उपैति
5.7.16.a.m: Whoever is about to establish his fires observes a vow on that night: he does not eat meat, he does not approach a woman.

5.7.17.a.m: "Settle the offspring, O Agni, and the quarters together with the beasts;

5.7.17.b.s: rāṣṭrāṇyasmā ādhehi yānyāsansavituḥ sava ity uttareṇa gārhapatyāyatanaṃ kalmāṣamajaṃ badhnāti
5.7.17.b.d: राष्ट्राण्यस्मा आधेहि यान्यासन्सवितुः सव इत्य् उत्तरेण गार्हपत्यायतनं कल्माषमजं बध्नाति
5.7.17.b.m: Establish for him the realms that were in the impulsion of Savitṛ"—with this, he binds a spotted he-goat to the north of the gārhapatya fire-hearth.

5.8.1.a.s: atha yajamāno vratamupaiti vācaṃ ca yacchatyanṛtātsatyamupaimi mānuṣāddaivyamupaimi daivīṃ vācaṃ yacchāmīti
5.8.1.a.d: अथ यजमानो व्रतमुपैति वाचं च यच्छत्यनृतात्सत्यमुपैमि मानुषाद्दैव्यमुपैमि दैवीं वाचं यच्छामीति
5.8.1.a.m: Then the sacrificer undertakes the vow and restrains his speech, [saying:] "From untruth I enter upon truth; from the human I enter upon the divine; I restrain divine speech."

5.8.2.a.m: They keep him awake on that night with lute and flute.

5.8.3.a.s: api vā na jāgarti na vācaṃ yacchati
5.8.3.a.d: अपि वा न जागर्ति न वाचं यच्छति
5.8.3.a.m: Or rather, he does not stay awake, nor does he restrain speech.

5.8.4.a.s: śalkairetāṃ rātrimetamagnimindhāna āste śalkairagnimindhāna ubhau lokau sanemaham /
5.8.4.a.d: शल्कैरेतां रात्रिमेतमग्निमिन्धान आस्ते शल्कैरग्निमिन्धान उभौ लोकौ सनेमहम् ।
5.8.4.a.m: Kindling this fire with chips of wood through that night, he sits, [reciting:] "Kindling the fire with chips of wood, may I win both worlds;

5.8.4.b.m: Prospering in both worlds, may I cross beyond death"—with this verse.

5.8.5.a.s: tasminnupavyuṣamaraṇī niṣṭapati jātavedo bhuvanasya reta iha siñca tapaso yajjaniṣyate /
5.8.5.a.d: तस्मिन्नुपव्युषमरणी निष्टपति जातवेदो भुवनस्य रेत इह सिञ्च तपसो यज्जनिष्यते ।
5.8.5.a.m: Over it, toward daybreak, he heats the churning sticks, [reciting:] "O Jātavedas, pour here the seed of the world, that which shall be born of heat,

5.8.5.b.m: Generating Agni, the oblation-bearer, from the aśvattha born of the śamī, the source of delight;

5.8.5.c.s: ayaṃ te yonir ṛtviya ity etābhyām
5.8.5.c.d: अयं ते योनिर् ऋत्विय इत्य् एताभ्याम्
5.8.5.c.m: This is your seasonal womb..."—with these two [verses].

5.8.6.a.m: "Agni drives away the demons, bright-flaming, immortal;

5.8.6.b.s: śuciḥ pāvaka īḍya ityaraṇī abhimantrya mahī viśpatnī sadane ṛtasyārvācī etaṃ dharuṇe rayīṇām /
5.8.6.b.d: शुचिः पावक ईड्य इत्यरणी अभिमन्त्र्य मही विश्पत्नी सदने ऋतस्यार्वाची एतं धरुणे रयीणाम् ।
5.8.6.b.m: Pure, purifying, praiseworthy"—having addressed the two churning sticks with this verse; the sacrificer looks at the two churning sticks as they are being brought, [reciting:] "Great ones, mistresses of the clan, in the seat of truth, come hither, O two supports of wealth; / pregnant, give birth to the people's Jātavedas, the leader of the rites."

5.8.6.c.s: antarvatnī janyaṃ jātavedasamadhvarāṇāṃ janayathaḥ purogāmityaraṇī āhriyamāṇe yajamānaḥ pratīkṣate
5.8.6.c.d: अन्तर्वत्नी जन्यं जातवेदसमध्वराणां जनयथः पुरोगामित्यरणी आह्रियमाणे यजमानः प्रतीक्षते
5.8.6.c.m: He gives [them] to the sacrificer, saying: "She who is to be milked, and she who bears milk, and she who is fertile: I give you your share."

5.8.7.a.s: dohyā ca te dugdhabhṛccorvarī te te bhāgadheyaṃ prayacchāmīti yajamānāya prayacchati
5.8.7.a.d: दोह्या च ते दुग्धभृच्चोर्वरी ते ते भागधेयं प्रयच्छामीति यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
5.8.7.a.m: "Mount the ten Śakvarī verses of mine, along with an immortal lifespan, O Agni, with splendour;

5.8.8.a.s: ārohataṃ daśataṃ śakvarīrmamartenāgna āyuṣā varcasā saha /
5.8.8.a.d: आरोहतं दशतं शक्वरीर्ममर्तेनाग्न आयुषा वर्चसा सह ।

5.8.8.b.s: jyogjīvanta uttarāmuttarāṃ samāṃ darśamahaṃ pūrṇamāsaṃ yajñaṃ yathā yajā iti pratigṛhyartviyavatī stho agniretasau garbhaṃ dadhāthāṃ te vāmahaṃ dade /
5.8.8.b.d: ज्योग्जीवन्त उत्तरामुत्तरां समां दर्शमहं पूर्णमासं यज्ञं यथा यजा इति प्रतिगृह्यर्त्वियवती स्थो अग्निरेतसौ गर्भं दधाथां ते वामहं ददे ।
5.8.8.b.m: ‘So that I may sacrifice, living a long life, year after year, with the New and Full Moon sacrifices,’ having accepted [them with this formula, he recites]: ‘You two possess the proper season, bearing the seed of Agni; bear the embryo! I receive the two of you.’

5.8.8.c.m: ‘That is true, since you bear a hero, you will bring forth a hero.’

5.8.8.d.s: te matprātaḥ prajaniṣyethe te mā prajāte prajanayiṣyathaḥ /
5.8.8.d.d: ते मत्प्रातः प्रजनिष्येथे ते मा प्रजाते प्रजनयिष्यथः ।
5.8.8.d.m: ‘You two shall be born from me in the morning; having been born, you shall bring forth for me’

5.8.8.e.s: prajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasena suvarge loka iti pratigṛhyābhimantrayate yajamānaḥ
5.8.8.e.d: प्रजया पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन सुवर्गे लोक इति प्रतिगृह्याभिमन्त्रयते यजमानः
5.8.8.e.m: ‘offspring, cattle, spiritual luster, in the heavenly world.’ Having accepted [them], the sacrificer addresses [them].

5.9.1.a.s: mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agniṃ yo no agniḥ pitara ity ubhau japataḥ /
5.9.1.a.d: मयि गृह्णाम्यग्रे अग्निं यो नो अग्निः पितर इत्य् उभौ जपतः ।
5.9.1.a.m: Both mutter: ‘I take into myself Agni first…’, ‘Whatever fire of ours, O fathers…’

5.9.1.b.s: apeta vīteti gārhapatyāyatanamuddhatya śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaya ityadbhiravokṣati
5.9.1.b.d: अपेत वीतेति गार्हपत्यायतनमुद्धत्य शं नो देवीरभिष्टय इत्यद्भिरवोक्षति
5.9.1.b.m: Having dug up the hearth of the gārhapatya with ‘Begone, disperse!’, he sprinkles it with water using ‘May the divine waters be for our welfare and aid…’

5.9.2.a.m: In this same way [he proceeds] for the dakṣiṇāgni, the āhavanīya, and the sabhya and āvasathya.

5.9.3.a.m: In this very order are the rites performed henceforth on these [hearths].

5.9.4.a.s: sikatānāmardhaṃ dvaidhaṃ vibhajyārdhaṃ gārhapatyāyatane nivapaty ardhaṃ dakṣiṇāgneḥ /
5.9.4.a.d: सिकतानामर्धं द्वैधं विभज्यार्धं गार्हपत्यायतने निवपत्य् अर्धं दक्षिणाग्नेः ।
5.9.4.a.m: Dividing half of the sand into two parts, he scatters half in the hearth of the gārhapatya and half in that of the dakṣiṇāgni.

5.9.4.b.m: Dividing the [other] half into three parts, [he scatters them] on the eastern [hearths].

5.9.5.a.m: According to this very rule he scatters all the earthen materials.

5.9.6.a.m: He scatters the sand with: ‘You are the ash of Agni.’

5.9.7.a.m: Scattering them, he meditates in his mind: ‘What is black in yonder moon, let that be here.’

5.9.8.a.s: udehyagne adhi mātuḥ pṛthivyā viśa āviśa mahataḥ sadhasthāt /
5.9.8.a.d: उदेह्यग्ने अधि मातुः पृथिव्या विश आविश महतः सधस्थात् ।
5.9.8.a.m: ‘Rise up, O Agni, upon Mother Earth! Enter into the settlements from the great dwelling!’

5.9.8.b.s: ākhuṃ tvā ye dadhire devayanto havyavāhaṃ bhuvanasya gopāmityākhukarīṣam //
5.9.8.b.d: आखुं त्वा ये दधिरे देवयन्तो हव्यवाहं भुवनस्य गोपामित्याखुकरीषम् ॥
5.9.8.b.m: ‘Thee, whom god-fearing men set as a mole, as the carrier of oblations, the protector of the world…’—with this, [he scatters] the earth from a mole-hill.

5.9.8.c.m: ‘That immortal part of the earth which arose in union with thee,’

5.9.8.d.m: ‘which Agni gave to Agni: on that let this one be established’—with this he scatters the ant-hill earth in the hearth of the gārhapatya.

5.9.9.a.m: With ‘That of the midspace…’ on that of the dakṣiṇāgni.

5.9.10.a.m: ‘From the ocean has arisen the sweet wave, bringing supreme sovereignty further forward;’

5.9.10.b.s: amī ca ye maghavāno vayaṃ ceṣamūrjaṃ madhumatsaṃbharemeti sūdam /
5.9.10.b.d: अमी च ये मघवानो वयं चेषमूर्जं मधुमत्संभरेमेति सूदम् ।
5.9.10.b.m: ‘may we and those generous patrons gather sweet food and strength’—with this [he deposits] mud from a dried pool.

5.9.10.c.m: With ‘So large you were at first…’ [he scatters] earth dug up by a boar.

5.9.11.a.s: ado devī prathamānā pṛthagyaddevairnyuptā vyasarpo mahitvā /
5.9.11.a.d: अदो देवी प्रथमाना पृथग्यद्देवैर्न्युप्ता व्यसर्पो महित्वा ।
5.9.11.a.m: ‘Yonder goddess, spreading afar, which, scattered by the gods, spread out in greatness,’

5.9.11.b.m: ‘you grew firm with gravel; conquering the three worlds, you won the realms and four quarters’—with this [he scatters] gravel.

5.9.11.c.m: And he meditates in mind on the one he hates.

5.10.1.a.s: ṛtaṃ stṛṇāmi purīṣaṃ pṛthivyāmṛte 'dhyagnimādadhe satye 'dhyagnimādadha ity āyataneṣu saṃbhārānanuvyūhati
5.10.1.a.d: ऋतं स्तृणामि पुरीषं पृथिव्यामृते ऽध्यग्निमादधे सत्ये ऽध्यग्निमादध इत्य् आयतनेषु संभाराननुव्यूहति
5.10.1.a.m: ‘I strew order, the filling, on earth; upon order I place Agni, upon truth I place Agni’—with this he spreads out the materials in the hearths.

5.10.2.a.s: saṃ yā vaḥ priyāstanuva ity eṣā //
5.10.2.a.d: सं या वः प्रियास्तनुव इत्य् एषा ॥
5.10.2.a.m: This [verse]: ‘Those dear forms of yours that are together…’

5.10.2.b.s: saṃ vaḥ sṛjāmi hṛdayāni saṃsṛṣṭaṃ mano astu vaḥ /
5.10.2.b.d: सं वः सृजामि हृदयानि संसृष्टं मनो अस्तु वः ।
5.10.2.b.m: ‘I unite your hearts; united let your mind be;’

5.10.2.c.s: saṃsṛṣṭaḥ prāṇo astu va iti vānaspatyānsaṃsṛjya sikatāvannivapatītaḥ prathamaṃ jajñe agnir ity etayā
5.10.2.c.d: संसृष्टः प्राणो अस्तु व इति वानस्पत्यान्संसृज्य सिकतावन्निवपतीतः प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निर् इत्य् एतया
5.10.2.c.m: ‘united let your breath be’—having mixed together the wooden materials [with this formula], he scatters them like the sand, with this [verse]: ‘From here first Agni was born…’

5.10.3.a.s: yāste śivāstanuvo jātavedo yā antarikṣe divi yāḥ pṛthivyām /
5.10.3.a.d: यास्ते शिवास्तनुवो जातवेदो या अन्तरिक्षे दिवि याः पृथिव्याम् ।
5.10.3.a.m: ‘Those auspicious forms of yours, O Jātavedas, which are in the midspace, which in heaven, which on earth—’

5.10.3.b.s: tābhiḥ saṃbhūya sagaṇaḥ sajoṣā hiraṇyayonirvaha havyamagna iti gārhapatyāyatane sauvarṇaṃ hiraṇyaśakalamuttarataḥ saṃbhāreṣūpāsyati
5.10.3.b.d: ताभिः संभूय सगणः सजोषा हिरण्ययोनिर्वह हव्यमग्न इति गार्हपत्यायतने सौवर्णं हिरण्यशकलमुत्तरतः संभारेषूपास्यति
5.10.3.b.m: ‘uniting with them, along with your troop, being gracious, of golden womb, carry the oblation, O Agni!’ With this, he casts a piece of gold onto the materials on the north side in the gārhapatya hearth.

5.10.4.a.m: ‘The shining Agni, with shining chariot, golden-skinned, belonging to all men, seated in the waters, finding the sun,’

5.10.4.b.s: vigāhaṃ tūrṇiṃ taviṣībhirāvṛtaṃ bhūrṇiṃ devāsa iha suśriyaṃ dadhur ity upāstam abhimantrayate /
5.10.4.b.d: विगाहं तूर्णिं तविषीभिरावृतं भूर्णिं देवास इह सुश्रियं दधुर् इत्य् उपास्तम् अभिमन्त्रयते ।
5.10.4.b.m: ‘penetrating, swift, clothed in strengths, eager, the gods have set here of good fortune’—with this he addresses what was cast down.

5.10.4.c.m: He gives silver to the person he hates.

5.10.5.a.s: yadi dveṣyaṃ nādhigacchedyāṃ diśaṃ dveṣyaḥ syāttena nirasyet
5.10.5.a.d: यदि द्वेष्यं नाधिगच्छेद्यां दिशं द्वेष्यः स्यात्तेन निरस्येत्
5.10.5.a.m: If he should not find anyone he hates, he should cast it away in the direction in which someone he hates might be.

5.10.6.a.m: Thus he does, casting [gold] into all [the hearths].

5.10.7.a.m: Having removed the ashes from the brāhmaudana fire, in it he churns out the fire from [the churning-sticks made of] śamī-wood holding an aśvattha tree within.

5.10.8.a.m: When the sun's rays are rising, he puts the two churning-sticks together with the daśahotṛ formula.

5.10.9.a.s: sahāgne 'gninā jāyasva saha rayyā saha puṣṭyā saha prajayā saha paśubhiḥ saha brahmavarcasenetyupatiṣṭhatyaśve 'gniṃ manthati
5.10.9.a.d: सहाग्ने ऽग्निना जायस्व सह रय्या सह पुष्ट्या सह प्रजया सह पशुभिः सह ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेत्युपतिष्ठत्यश्वे ऽग्निं मन्थति
5.10.9.a.m: With ‘O Agni, be born along with the fire, along with wealth, along with nourishment, along with offspring, along with cattle, along with spiritual luster!’, he attends [it]; he churns the fire on a horse.

5.10.10.a.s: śveto 'śvo 'viklinnākṣo bhavati rohito vāsitajānurapi vā ya eva kaścitsāṇḍaḥ
5.10.10.a.d: श्वेतो ऽश्वो ऽविक्लिन्नाक्षो भवति रोहितो वासितजानुरपि वा य एव कश्चित्साण्डः
5.10.10.a.m: The horse is white with clear eyes, or reddish with black knees, or indeed any uncastrated horse whatsoever.

5.10.11.a.m: While it is being churned, he sings the Sāman of Śakti, the son of Saṅkṛti.

5.10.11.b.m: When smoke has arisen, [the Sāman] of Gāthin, the son of Kuśika;

5.10.11.c.m: and [he recites]: ‘Jātavedas is laid down in the two churning-sticks…’

5.10.12.a.m: With ‘Come down, O Jātavedas!’, he addresses the [fire] being produced.

5.11.1.a.m: Here he causes the sacrificer to recite the caturhotṛ formulas.

5.11.2.a.s: ajannagniḥ pūrvaḥ pūrvebhyaḥ pavamānaḥ śuciḥ pāvaka īḍya iti jātamabhimantrayate
5.11.2.a.d: अजन्नग्निः पूर्वः पूर्वेभ्यः पवमानः शुचिः पावक ईड्य इति जातमभिमन्त्रयते
5.11.2.a.m: With ‘Agni was born, the former for the former ones, the purifying, pure, cleansing, to be praised’, he addresses [the fire] once it is born.

5.11.3.a.m: When it is born, the sacrificer gives a choice gift.

5.11.4.a.s: gaur vai varo 'tivaro 'nyo dhenurvaro 'tivaro 'nyo 'naḍvānvaro 'tivaro 'nyaḥ paṣṭhauhī varo 'tivaro 'nyaḥ
5.11.4.a.d: गौर् वै वरो ऽतिवरो ऽन्यो धेनुर्वरो ऽतिवरो ऽन्यो ऽनड्वान्वरो ऽतिवरो ऽन्यः पष्ठौही वरो ऽतिवरो ऽन्यः
5.11.4.a.m: A cow is indeed a choice gift; another is an extra choice gift: a milch cow is a choice gift, another is an extra choice gift; an ox is a choice gift, another is an extra choice gift; a four-year-old cow is a choice gift, another is an extra choice gift.

5.11.5.a.s: jātaṃ yajamāno 'bhiprāṇiti prajāpatestvā prāṇenābhiprāṇimi pūṣṇaḥ poṣeṇa mahyaṃ dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya śataṃ śaradbhya āyuṣe varcase jīvātvai puṇyāyeti
5.11.5.a.d: जातं यजमानो ऽभिप्राणिति प्रजापतेस्त्वा प्राणेनाभिप्राणिमि पूष्णः पोषेण मह्यं दीर्घायुत्वाय शतशारदाय शतं शरद्भ्य आयुषे वर्चसे जीवात्वै पुण्यायेति
5.11.5.a.m: The sacrificer breathes upon [the fire] once born: ‘I breathe upon you with the breath of Prajāpati, with the nourishment of Pūṣan, for my long life, for a hundred autumns, for a life of a hundred autumns, for luster, for living, for holy merit.’

5.11.6.a.m: ‘Mortals have generated the immortal, the unfailing, the swift, with strong jaws;’

5.11.6.b.s: daśa svasāro agruvaḥ samīcīḥ pumāṃsaṃ jātamabhisaṃrabhantāmiti jātamañjalinābhigṛhya samrāḍasi virāḍasi sārasvatau tvotsau samindhātāmannādaṃ tvānnapatyāyetyupasamidhyāthainaṃ prāñcamuddhṛtyāsīnaḥ sarveṣāṃ mantrāṇāmantena rathaṃtare gīyamāne yajñāyajñīye ca yatharṣyādhānena prathamayā vyāhṛtyā dvābhyāṃ vā prathamābhyāṃ ca sarparājñībhyāṃ prathamena ca gharmaśirasā
5.11.6.b.d: दश स्वसारो अग्रुवः समीचीः पुमांसं जातमभिसंरभन्तामिति जातमञ्जलिनाभिगृह्य सम्राडसि विराडसि सारस्वतौ त्वोत्सौ समिन्धातामन्नादं त्वान्नपत्यायेत्युपसमिध्याथैनं प्राञ्चमुद्धृत्यासीनः सर्वेषां मन्त्राणामन्तेन रथंतरे गीयमाने यज्ञायज्ञीये च यथर्ष्याधानेन प्रथमया व्याहृत्या द्वाभ्यां वा प्रथमाभ्यां च सर्पराज्ञीभ्यां प्रथमेन च घर्मशिरसा
5.11.6.b.m: ‘may the ten unwedded sisters together take hold of the male born’—having taken up the born [fire] with cupped hands with this, having kindled it with ‘You are an emperor, you are a sovereign ruler, may the two Sarasvatī springs kindle you; you, the consumer of food, for food-lordship’, then lifting it eastward while seated, at the end of all the formulas, while the Rathaṃtara and Yajñāyajñīya [sāmans] are being sung, with the formula of establishment according to the ṛṣi lineage, with the first vyāhṛti or with the two first ones, and with the two first sarparājñī verses, and with the first gharmaśiras formula—

5.11.7.a.s: bhṛgūṇāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmīti bhārgavasyādadhyāt /
5.11.7.a.d: भृगूणां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामीति भार्गवस्यादध्यात् ।
5.11.7.a.m: for a descendant of Bhṛgu he should establish it with: ‘By the vow of the Bhṛgus, the gods, O lord of vows, I establish you’;

5.11.7.b.s: aṅgirasāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmīti yo brāhmaṇa āṅgirasaḥ syāt /
5.11.7.b.d: अङ्गिरसां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामीति यो ब्राह्मण आङ्गिरसः स्यात् ।
5.11.7.b.m: for a brāhmaṇa who is an Āṅgirasa, with: ‘By the vow of the Aṅgirases, the gods, O lord of vows, I establish you’;

5.11.7.c.s: ādityānāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmītyanyāsāṃ brāhmaṇīnāṃ prajānām /
5.11.7.c.d: आदित्यानां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामीत्यन्यासां ब्राह्मणीनां प्रजानाम् ।
5.11.7.c.m: for other brāhmaṇa descendants, with: ‘By the vow of the Ādityas, the gods, O lord of vows, I establish you’;

5.11.7.d.s: varuṇasya tvā rājño vratapate vratenādadhāmīti rājñaḥ /
5.11.7.d.d: वरुणस्य त्वा राज्ञो व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामीति राज्ञः ।
5.11.7.d.m: for a king, with: ‘By the vow of King Varuṇa, O lord of vows, I establish you’;

5.11.7.e.m: for a rājanya, with: ‘By the power of Indra, O lord of vows, I establish you’;

5.11.7.f.m: for a vaiśya, with: ‘By the vow of Manu, the village headman, O lord of vows, I establish you’;

5.11.7.g.s: ṛbhūṇāṃ tvā devānāṃ vratapate vratenādadhāmīti rathakārasyeti yatharṣyādhānāni
5.11.7.g.d: ऋभूणां त्वा देवानां व्रतपते व्रतेनादधामीति रथकारस्येति यथर्ष्याधानानि
5.11.7.g.m: for a chariot-maker, with: ‘By the vow of the Ṛbhus, the gods, O lord of vows, I establish you’—these are the establishments according to the ṛṣi lineage.

5.12.1.a.m: The vyāhṛtis are bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ.

5.12.1.b.m: With ‘The earth by broadness…’ [he recites] the Sarparājñī verses.

5.12.1.c.m: ‘The head is the gharma; may this Agni here become dear to the cattle!’

5.12.1.d.m: ‘Grant shelter to our offspring, to our children.’

5.12.1.e.m: ‘The out-breath is the wind; may this Agni here become dear to the cattle!’

5.12.1.f.m: ‘Cook food tasty for our offspring, for our children.’

5.12.1.g.m: ‘The eye is the sun; that is the sun yonder; may this Agni here become dear to the cattle!’

5.12.1.h.s: yatte śukra śaukraṃ varcaḥ śukrā tanūḥ śukraṃ jyotirajasraṃ tena me dīdihi tena tvādadhe 'gnināgne brahmaṇeti gharmaśirāṃsi
5.12.1.h.d: यत्ते शुक्र शौक्रं वर्चः शुक्रा तनूः शुक्रं ज्योतिरजस्रं तेन मे दीदिहि तेन त्वादधे ऽग्निनाग्ने ब्रह्मणेति घर्मशिरांसि
5.12.1.h.m: ‘Whatever bright radiance of thine is brilliant, O bright one, whatever body is bright, whatever light is bright and unceasing, shine with that for me; with that I set thee down, with Agni, O Agni, with Brahman’—these are the Gharma-heads.

5.12.2.a.s: yāste śivāstanuvo jātavedo yā antarikṣa uta pārthivīryāḥ /
5.12.2.a.d: यास्ते शिवास्तनुवो जातवेदो या अन्तरिक्ष उत पार्थिवीर्याः ।
5.12.2.a.m: ‘Whatever auspicious bodies of thine [there are], O Jātavedas, which are in the intermediate space, and which are of the earth—

5.12.2.b.s: tābhiḥ saṃbhūya sagaṇaḥ sajoṣā hiraṇyayonirvaha havyamagne //
5.12.2.b.d: ताभिः संभूय सगणः सजोषा हिरण्ययोनिर्वह हव्यमग्ने ॥
5.12.2.b.m: uniting with these, having thy troop, being in agreement, possessing a golden womb, carry the oblation, O Agni!’

5.12.2.c.m: ‘I establish thee as out-breath in the immortal, food-eater for eating food, protector for protection.’

5.12.2.d.s: divastvā vīryeṇa pṛthivyai mahimnāntarikṣasya poṣeṇa paśūnāṃ tejasā sarvapaśumādadhe //
5.12.2.d.d: दिवस्त्वा वीर्येण पृथिव्यै महिम्नान्तरिक्षस्य पोषेण पशूनां तेजसा सर्वपशुमादधे ॥
5.12.2.d.m: ‘By the virility of heaven, by the greatness of earth, by the nourishment of intermediate space, by the splendour of cattle, I establish thee, possessing all cattle.’

5.12.2.e.s: agne gṛhapate 'he budhnya pariṣadya divaḥ pṛthivyāḥ paryantarikṣāllokaṃ vinda yajamānāya /
5.12.2.e.d: अग्ने गृहपते ऽहे बुध्न्य परिषद्य दिवः पृथिव्याः पर्यन्तरिक्षाल्लोकं विन्द यजमानाय ।
5.12.2.e.m: ‘O Agni, lord of the house, Ahi Budhnya, attendant, from heaven, from earth, from intermediate space find a place for the sacrificer!’

5.12.2.f.m: ‘I seat thee on the head of earth in the sacrificial place.’

5.12.2.g.s: yo no agne niṣṭyo yo 'niṣṭyo 'bhidāsatīdamahaṃ taṃ tvayābhinidadhāmīti saṃbhāreṣu nidadhāti
5.12.2.g.d: यो नो अग्ने निष्ट्यो यो ऽनिष्ट्यो ऽभिदासतीदमहं तं त्वयाभिनिदधामीति संभारेषु निदधाति
5.12.2.g.m: ‘O Agni, whether related or unrelated, whoever attacks us, here I place him down with thee’—[saying this,] he places [the fire] down upon the ritual requisites.

5.12.3.a.m: ‘Being a good master of the household, burning down enemies, bringing ever better dawns,

5.12.3.b.s: agne sapatnām̐ apabādhamāno rāyaspoṣamiṣamūrjamasmāsu dhehītyādhīyamānamabhimantrayate yajamāno ghramaśirāṃsi cainamadhvaryurvācayati
5.12.3.b.d: अग्ने सपत्नाम्̐ अपबाधमानो रायस्पोषमिषमूर्जमस्मासु धेहीत्याधीयमानमभिमन्त्रयते यजमानो घ्रमशिरांसि चैनमध्वर्युर्वाचयति
5.12.3.b.m: O Agni, repelling rivals, place in us increase of wealth, food, and vigour’—with this the sacrificer addresses [the fire] being established, and the adhvaryu has him recite the Gharma-heads.

5.13.1.a.m: When the sun is half-risen, he establishes the āhavanīya.

5.13.2.a.m: When it has fully risen, for one who desires spiritual splendour.

5.13.3.a.m: He kindles on the gārhapatya the carrying firewood-bundle of aśvattha wood, and prepares the sand acting as underlayer.

5.13.4.a.s: tamudyacchatyojase balāya tvodyacche vṛṣaṇe śuṣmāyāyuṣe varcase /
5.13.4.a.d: तमुद्यच्छत्योजसे बलाय त्वोद्यच्छे वृषणे शुष्मायायुषे वर्चसे ।
5.13.4.a.m: He lifts it up with: ‘For vigor, for strength I lift thee up, for the bull, for energy, for life, for radiance.’

5.13.4.b.m: ‘Thou art the slayer of rivals, the slayer of Vṛtra.’

5.13.4.c.s: yaste deveṣu mahimā suvargo yasta ātmā paśuṣu praviṣṭaḥ /
5.13.4.c.d: यस्ते देवेषु महिमा सुवर्गो यस्त आत्मा पशुषु प्रविष्टः ।
5.13.4.c.m: ‘Whatever greatness of thine among the gods is heavenly, whatever self of thine has entered into cattle,

5.13.4.d.s: puṣṭiryā te manuṣyeṣu paprathe tayā no agne juṣamāṇa ehi //
5.13.4.d.d: पुष्टिर्या ते मनुष्येषु पप्रथे तया नो अग्ने जुषमाण एहि ॥
5.13.4.d.m: whatever nourishment of thine has extended among men, with that, O Agni, being pleased, come to us!’

5.13.4.e.m: ‘From heaven, from earth, from intermediate space, from the wind, from cattle, from the plants,

5.13.4.f.s: yatrayatra jātavedaḥ saṃbabhūtha tato no agne juṣamāṇa ehi //
5.13.4.f.d: यत्रयत्र जातवेदः संबभूथ ततो नो अग्ने जुषमाण एहि ॥
5.13.4.f.m: wherever, O Jātavedas, thou hast arisen, from there, O Agni, being pleased, come to us!’

5.13.4.g.s: udu tvā viśve devā ity etābhiścatasṛbhiḥ
5.13.4.g.d: उदु त्वा विश्वे देवा इत्य् एताभिश्चतसृभिः
5.13.4.g.m: [He lifts it up] with these four [verses] beginning with: ‘The All-gods [have lifted] thee up…’

5.13.5.a.m: He lifts the fire somewhat high.

5.13.6.a.m: He holds the sand acting as underlayer beneath the lifted fire.

5.13.7.a.s: athāśvasya dakṣiṇe karṇe yajamānamagnitanūrvācayati yā vājinnagneḥ paśuṣu pavamānā priyā tanūstāmāvaha yā vājinnagnerapsu pāvakā priyā tanūstāmāvaha yā vājinnagneḥ sūrye śuciḥ priyā tanūstāmāvaheti /
5.13.7.a.d: अथाश्वस्य दक्षिणे कर्णे यजमानमग्नितनूर्वाचयति या वाजिन्नग्नेः पशुषु पवमाना प्रिया तनूस्तामावह या वाजिन्नग्नेरप्सु पावका प्रिया तनूस्तामावह या वाजिन्नग्नेः सूर्ये शुचिः प्रिया तनूस्तामावहेति ।
5.13.7.a.m: Then he makes the sacrificer recite into the right ear of the horse the Agni-bodies: ‘O swift courser, bring that dear body of Agni which purifies among cattle; O swift courser, bring that dear body of Agni which is pure in the waters; O swift courser, bring that dear body of Agni which is radiant in the sun.’

5.13.8.a.s: athāgnīdhro laukikamagnimāhṛtya mathitvā vordhvajñurāsīno dakṣiṇāmagnimādadhāti yajñāyajñīye gīyamāne yatharṣyādhānena dvitīyayā vyāhṛtyā tiṣrbhiḥ sarparājñībhirdvitīyena ca gharmaśirasā //
5.13.8.a.d: अथाग्नीध्रो लौकिकमग्निमाहृत्य मथित्वा वोर्ध्वज्ञुरासीनो दक्षिणामग्निमादधाति यज्ञायज्ञीये गीयमाने यथर्ष्याधानेन द्वितीयया व्याहृत्या तिष्र्भिः सर्पराज्ञीभिर्द्वितीयेन च घर्मशिरसा ॥
5.13.8.a.m: Then the agnīdh, having fetched secular fire or having churned it, sitting with his right knee raised, establishes the dakṣiṇa fire while the Yajñāyajñīya is being sung, with the establishment formula according to his seer, with the second vyāhṛti, with three Sarparājñī verses, and with the second Gharma-head:

5.13.8.b.s: yāste śivāstanuvo jātavedo yā antarikṣa uta pārthivīryāḥ /
5.13.8.b.d: यास्ते शिवास्तनुवो जातवेदो या अन्तरिक्ष उत पार्थिवीर्याः ।
5.13.8.b.m: ‘Whatever auspicious bodies of thine [there are], O Jātavedas, which are in the intermediate space, and which are of the earth—

5.13.8.c.m: uniting with these, having thy troop, being in agreement, possessing a golden womb, carry the oblation, O Agni!’

5.13.8.d.m: ‘I establish thee as diffused breath in the immortal, food-eater for eating food, protector for protection.’

5.13.8.e.s: divastvā vīryeṇa pṛthivyai mahimnāntarikṣasya poṣeṇa paśūnāṃ tejasā sarvapaśumādadhe //
5.13.8.e.d: दिवस्त्वा वीर्येण पृथिव्यै महिम्नान्तरिक्षस्य पोषेण पशूनां तेजसा सर्वपशुमादधे ॥
5.13.8.e.m: ‘By the virility of heaven, by the greatness of earth, by the nourishment of intermediate space, by the splendour of cattle, I establish thee, possessing all cattle.’

5.13.8.f.s: agne 'nnapā mayobhuva suśevadivaḥ pṛthivyāḥ paryantarikṣāllokaṃ vinda yajamānāya /
5.13.8.f.d: अग्ने ऽन्नपा मयोभुव सुशेवदिवः पृथिव्याः पर्यन्तरिक्षाल्लोकं विन्द यजमानाय ।
5.13.8.f.m: ‘O Agni, guardian of food, bringing delight, gracious one, from heaven, from earth, from intermediate space find a place for the sacrificer!’

5.13.8.g.m: ‘I seat thee on the head of earth in the sacrificial place.’

5.13.8.h.s: yo no agne niṣṭyo yo 'niṣṭyo 'bhidāsatīdamahaṃ taṃ tvayābhinidadhāmīti saṃbhāreṣu nidadhāti
5.13.8.h.d: यो नो अग्ने निष्ट्यो यो ऽनिष्ट्यो ऽभिदासतीदमहं तं त्वयाभिनिदधामीति संभारेषु निदधाति
5.13.8.h.m: ‘O Agni, whether related or unrelated, whoever attacks us, here I place him down with thee’—[saying this,] he places [the fire] down upon the ritual requisites.

5.14.1.a.s: yo brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyaḥ śūdro vāsura iva bahupuṣṭaḥ syāttasya gṛhādāhṛtyādadhyātpuṣṭikāmasya
5.14.1.a.d: यो ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वैश्यः शूद्रो वासुर इव बहुपुष्टः स्यात्तस्य गृहादाहृत्यादध्यात्पुष्टिकामस्य
5.14.1.a.m: For one who desires prosperity, he should establish [the dakṣiṇa fire] having brought it from the house of a brāhmaṇa, a rājanya, a vaiśya, or a śūdra, who is very prosperous like an Asura.

5.14.2.a.m: However, he should not eat in his house afterwards.

5.14.3.a.m: For one who desires food, [it should be taken] from a frying pan; for one who desires spiritual splendour, from a blazing treetop.

5.14.4.a.m: They sing the Vāmadevya chant as the āhavanīya is being taken out.

5.14.5.b.m: ‘Stride forward; great art thou, a seat on the altar ground for humans;

5.14.5.c.s: triṣu lokeṣu jāgṛhi prajayā ca dhanena ca //
5.14.5.c.d: त्रिषु लोकेषु जागृहि प्रजया च धनेन च ॥
5.14.5.c.m: watch over the three worlds with offspring and with wealth!’

5.14.5.d.s: imā u māmupatiṣṭhantu rāya ābhiḥ prajābhiriha saṃvaseya /
5.14.5.d.d: इमा उ मामुपतिष्ठन्तु राय आभिः प्रजाभिरिह संवसेय ।
5.14.5.d.m: ‘May these riches approach me; may I dwell here together with these offspring;

5.14.5.e.s: iho iḍā tiṣṭhatu viśvarūpī madhye vasordīdihi jātaveda iti prāñco 'śvaprathamā abhipravrajanti
5.14.5.e.d: इहो इडा तिष्ठतु विश्वरूपी मध्ये वसोर्दीदिहि जातवेद इति प्राञ्चो ऽश्वप्रथमा अभिप्रव्रजन्ति
5.14.5.e.m: may all-formed Iḍā dwell here; shine in the midst of wealth, O Jātavedas!’—with these [verses] they march forward towards the east, preceded by the horse.

5.14.6.a.s: dakṣiṇato brahmā rathaṃ rathaṃ rathacakraṃ vā vartayati yāvaccakraṃ triḥ parivartate
5.14.6.a.d: दक्षिणतो ब्रह्मा रथं रथं रथचक्रं वा वर्तयति यावच्चक्रं त्रिः परिवर्तते
5.14.6.a.m: To the south the brahman rolls a chariot or a chariot wheel, so long as the wheel turns around three times.

5.14.8.a.s: jānudaghne dhārayamāṇastṛtīyamadhvano 'gniṃ harati nābhidaghne tṛtīyamāsyadaghne tṛtīyam /
5.14.8.a.d: जानुदघ्ने धारयमाणस्तृतीयमध्वनो ऽग्निं हरति नाभिदघ्ने तृतीयमास्यदघ्ने तृतीयम् ।
5.14.8.a.m: Holding it knee-high, he carries the fire for a third of the way; navel-high for a third; mouth-high for a third.

5.14.8.b.m: He does not lift it higher than ear-height.

5.14.9.a.m: If, having raised it, he should lower it, he should establish it after measuring it with his mouth.

5.14.10.a.m: He should not step between the fire and the sun.

5.14.11.a.m: Grasping it from the south, he carries it.

5.14.12.a.m: Halfway along the path, the sacrificer gives a boon.

5.14.13.a.s: ardhādhve hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya nāko 'si bradhnaḥ pratiṣṭhā saṃkramaṇa ityatikrāmati
5.14.13.a.d: अर्धाध्वे हिरण्यं निधाय नाको ऽसि ब्रध्नः प्रतिष्ठा संक्रमण इत्यतिक्रामति
5.14.13.a.m: Having placed gold halfway along the path, he steps over it with: ‘Thou art heaven, the sun, the firm foundation, the crossing.’

5.14.14.a.s: prāñcamaśvamabhyasthādviśvā iti dakṣiṇena padottarataḥ saṃbhārānākramayati yathāhitasyāgneraṅgārāḥ padamabhyavavarteranniti
5.14.14.a.d: प्राञ्चमश्वमभ्यस्थाद्विश्वा इति दक्षिणेन पदोत्तरतः संभारानाक्रमयति यथाहितस्याग्नेरङ्गाराः पदमभ्यववर्तेरन्निति
5.14.14.a.m: With ‘He has stepped upon all…’, he makes the horse step upon the ritual requisites northwards with its right foot, facing east, so that the coals of the established fire might roll towards the footprint.

5.14.15.a.m: Having turned it clockwise, he makes it step again with: ‘When thou didst neigh…’

5.14.16.a.m: He holds the horse in front, facing west.

5.14.18.a.d: तदभावे ऽनड्वान्पूर्ववाडेतानि कर्माणि करोतीति पैङ्गायनिब्राह्मणं भवति
5.14.18.a.m: In its absence, a previously harnessed ox performs these duties—so states a Paiṅgāyani-brāhmaṇa.

5.15.1.a.m: 'One should establish [the fire] in the footprint of a water-jar'—thus [says] the Bahvṛca-brāhmaṇa.

5.15.1.b.m: 'One should establish [it] in the footprint of a goat'—thus the Vājasaneyaka.

5.15.2.a.s: atha yajamānaḥ śivā japati ye te agne śive tanuvau virāṭca svarāṭca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām /
5.15.2.a.d: अथ यजमानः शिवा जपति ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ विराट्च स्वराट्च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् ।
5.15.2.a.m: Then the sacrificer mutters the auspicious [formulas]: 'Those two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, Virāj and Svarāj, let them enter me, let them invigorate me!

5.15.2.b.s: ye te agne śive tanuvau samrāṭcābhibhūśca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām /
5.15.2.b.d: ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ सम्राट्चाभिभूश्च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् ।
5.15.2.b.m: Those two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, Samrāj and Abhibhū, let them enter me, let them invigorate me!

5.15.2.c.s: ye te agne śive tanuvau vibhūśca paribhūśca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām /
5.15.2.c.d: ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ विभूश्च परिभूश्च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् ।
5.15.2.c.m: Those two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, Vibhū and Paribhū, let them enter me, let them invigorate me!

5.15.2.d.s: ye te agne śive tanuvau prabhvī ca prabhūtiśca te mā viśatāṃ te mā jinvatām /
5.15.2.d.d: ये ते अग्ने शिवे तनुवौ प्रभ्वी च प्रभूतिश्च ते मा विशतां ते मा जिन्वताम् ।
5.15.2.d.m: Those two auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, Prabhvī and Prabhūti, let them enter me, let them invigorate me!

5.15.2.e.m: With those auspicious bodies of yours, O Agni, with them I establish you.'

5.15.3.a.s: yāste agne ghorāstanuvastābhiramuṃ gaccheti yajamāno dveṣyāya prahiṇoti tābhirenaṃ parābhāvayati
5.15.3.a.d: यास्ते अग्ने घोरास्तनुवस्ताभिरमुं गच्छेति यजमानो द्वेष्याय प्रहिणोति ताभिरेनं पराभावयति
5.15.3.a.m: With: 'Those terrifying bodies of yours, O Agni, with them go to so-and-so,' the sacrificer dispatches [them] against one who is hated; with them he causes him to perish.

5.15.4.a.m: They are to be recited in the wilderness.

5.15.5.a.s: yadidaṃ divo yadadaḥ pṛthivyāḥ saṃvidāne rodasī saṃbabhūvatuḥ /
5.15.5.a.d: यदिदं दिवो यददः पृथिव्याः संविदाने रोदसी संबभूवतुः ।
5.15.5.a.m: 'What was here of the sky, what was there of the earth—the two consenting firmaments came together:

5.15.5.b.s: tayoḥ pṛṣṭhe sīdatu jātavedāḥ śaṃbhūḥ prajābhyastanuve syona ity abhimantrya purastātpratyaṅ tiṣṭhannāhavanīyamādadhāti
5.15.5.b.d: तयोः पृष्ठे सीदतु जातवेदाः शंभूः प्रजाभ्यस्तनुवे स्योन इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य पुरस्तात्प्रत्यङ् तिष्ठन्नाहवनीयमादधाति
5.15.5.b.m: on the back of them both let Jātavedas sit, bringing welfare to offspring, gentle to the self'—having addressed [the fire] with this [verse], standing facing west to the east [of the hearth], he establishes the āhavanīya.

5.15.6.a.s: bṛhati gīyamāne śyaitavāravantīyayoryajñāyajñīye ca yatharṣyādhānena sarvābhirvyāhṛtībhiḥ sarvābhiḥ sarparājñībhistṛtīyena ca gharmaśirasā yāste śivāstanuvo jātavedo yā antarikṣa uta pārthivīryāḥ /
5.15.6.a.d: बृहति गीयमाने श्यैतवारवन्तीययोर्यज्ञायज्ञीये च यथर्ष्याधानेन सर्वाभिर्व्याहृतीभिः सर्वाभिः सर्पराज्ञीभिस्तृतीयेन च घर्मशिरसा यास्ते शिवास्तनुवो जातवेदो या अन्तरिक्ष उत पार्थिवीर्याः ।
5.15.6.a.m: While the Bṛhat [sāman] is being sung, or the Śyaita and Vāravantīya, or the Yajñāyajñīya, with the establishment according to the ṛṣis, with all the vyāhṛtis, with all the Sarparājñī verses, and with the third Gharmaśiras verse: 'Those auspicious bodies of yours, O Jātavedas, which are in the intermediate space and which are of the earth—

5.15.6.b.s: tābhiḥ saṃbhūya sagaṇaḥ sajoṣā hiraṇyayonir vaha havyamagne //
5.15.6.b.d: ताभिः संभूय सगणः सजोषा हिरण्ययोनिर् वह हव्यमग्ने ॥
5.15.6.b.m: uniting with them, accompanied by your troop, harmonious, having a golden womb, convey the offering, O Agni!

5.15.6.c.m: I establish you, the out-breath, in the immortal, the eater of food for food-eating, the protector for protection!

5.15.6.d.s: divastvā vīryeṇa pṛthivyai mahimnāntarikṣasya poṣeṇa paśūnāṃ tejasā sarvapaśumādadhe //
5.15.6.d.d: दिवस्त्वा वीर्येण पृथिव्यै महिम्नान्तरिक्षस्य पोषेण पशूनां तेजसा सर्वपशुमादधे ॥
5.15.6.d.m: By the vigor of the sky, by the greatness of the earth, by the nourishment of the intermediate space, by the splendor of cattle, I establish [you], possessing all cattle!

5.15.6.e.s: agne samrāḍajaikapādāhavanīya divaḥ pṛthivyāḥ paryantarikṣāllokaṃ vinda yajamānāya /
5.15.6.e.d: अग्ने सम्राडजैकपादाहवनीय दिवः पृथिव्याः पर्यन्तरिक्षाल्लोकं विन्द यजमानाय ।
5.15.6.e.m: O Agni, sovereign, Aja Ekapād, āhavanīya, find a realm for the sacrificer from the sky, from the earth, and around from the intermediate space!

5.15.6.f.m: I seat you on the head of the earth, in the sacrificial place!

5.15.6.g.s: yo no agne niṣṭyo yo 'niṣṭyo 'bhidāsatīdamahaṃ taṃ tvayābhinidadhāmīti saṃbhāreṣu nidadhāti
5.15.6.g.d: यो नो अग्ने निष्ट्यो यो ऽनिष्ट्यो ऽभिदासतीदमहं तं त्वयाभिनिदधामीति संभारेषु निदधाति
5.15.6.g.m: Whoever, O Agni, whether an insider or an outsider, assails us, here with you I press him down'—with these words he places [the fire] upon the materials.

5.16.1.a.m: 'I have attained, I have pervaded, I have attained all lifespan!

5.16.1.b.s: ahaṃ tvadasmi madasi tvametanmamāsi yonistava yonirasmi /
5.16.1.b.d: अहं त्वदस्मि मदसि त्वमेतन्ममासि योनिस्तव योनिरस्मि ।
5.16.1.b.m: I am from you, you are from me, thus: you are my womb, I am your womb!

5.16.1.c.s: mamaiva sanvaha havyānyagne putraḥ pitre lokakṛjjātaveda ity ādhīyamānamabhimantrayate yajamānaḥ
5.16.1.c.d: ममैव सन्वह हव्यान्यग्ने पुत्रः पित्रे लोककृज्जातवेद इत्य् आधीयमानमभिमन्त्रयते यजमानः
5.16.1.c.m: Being indeed my own, convey the offerings, O Agni, like a son for a father making a place, O Jātavedas'—with these words the sacrificer addresses [the fire] being established.

5.16.2.a.d: व्याहृतीः सर्पराज्ञीर्घर्मशिरांसीति सर्वेष्वाधानेषु यजमानो ऽनुवर्तयते येनयेनादधाति
5.16.2.a.m: In all establishments, with whichever [formula] he establishes [the fire], the sacrificer repeats along with it the vyāhṛtis, the Sarparājñī verses, and the Gharmaśiras verses.

5.16.3.a.m: One does not touch a fire that has been established but not offered into.

5.16.3.b.m: It is to be appeased with clarified butter and herbs.

5.16.4.a.s: yā te agne paśuṣu pavamānā priyā tanūryā pṛthivyāṃ yāgnau yā rathantare yā gāyatre chandasi tāṃ ta etenāvayaje svāhā /
5.16.4.a.d: या ते अग्ने पशुषु पवमाना प्रिया तनूर्या पृथिव्यां याग्नौ या रथन्तरे या गायत्रे छन्दसि तां त एतेनावयजे स्वाहा ।
5.16.4.a.m: 'That purifying, dear body of yours, O Agni, which is in cattle, which is on earth, which is in fire, which is in the Rathantara, which is in the Gāyatrī metre—that [body] of yours I propitiate with this, svāhā!

5.16.4.b.s: yā te agne 'psu pāvakā priyā tanūryāntarikṣe yā vāyau yā vāmadevye yā traiṣṭubhe chandasi tāṃ ta etenāvayaje svāhā /
5.16.4.b.d: या ते अग्ने ऽप्सु पावका प्रिया तनूर्यान्तरिक्षे या वायौ या वामदेव्ये या त्रैष्टुभे छन्दसि तां त एतेनावयजे स्वाहा ।
5.16.4.b.m: That cleansing, dear body of yours, O Agni, which is in the waters, which is in the intermediate space, which is in the wind, which is in the Vāmadevya, which is in the Triṣṭubh metre—that [body] of yours I propitiate with this, svāhā!

5.16.4.c.s: yā te agne sūrye śuciḥ priyā tanūryā divi yāditye yā bṛhati yā jāgate chandasi tāṃ ta etenāvayaje svāhetyetaiḥ pratimantramājyamoṣadhīśca juhoti
5.16.4.c.d: या ते अग्ने सूर्ये शुचिः प्रिया तनूर्या दिवि यादित्ये या बृहति या जागते छन्दसि तां त एतेनावयजे स्वाहेत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रमाज्यमोषधीश्च जुहोति
5.16.4.c.m: That bright, dear body of yours, O Agni, which is in the sun, which is in the sky, which is in Āditya, which is in the Bṛhat, which is in the Jagatī metre—that [body] of yours I propitiate with this, svāhā!' With these formulas, verse by verse, he offers clarified butter and herbs.

5.16.5.a.m: Some say: 'He places firesticks [on the fire].'

5.16.6.a.m: At the setting up of the fires, the brahman sings sāmans.

5.16.8.a.m: 'The udgītha is performed solely with the vyāhṛtis'—thus the Vājasaneyaka.

5.17.1.a.m: Then he establishes the sabhya and the āvasathya [fires], having fetched worldly fire or having churned [it], or from the āhavanīya, with the establishment according to the ṛṣis.

5.17.2.a.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवसे ऽग्ने पवस्व स्वपाः ।
5.17.2.a.m: 'O Agni, you purify lifespans; O Agni, purify [us], doing good work!

5.17.2.b.m: Agni, the purifying seer, belonging to the five peoples, the domestic priest:

5.17.2.c.s: tamīmahe mahāgayamiti tisra āśvatthyaḥ samidha ekaikasminnādadhāti
5.17.2.c.d: तमीमहे महागयमिति तिस्र आश्वत्थ्यः समिध एकैकस्मिन्नादधाति
5.17.2.c.m: him we beseech for a great household'—with these [verses] he places three aśvattha firesticks on each one.

5.17.4.a.m: 'From the ocean the sweet wave has arisen; along with Upāṃśu it reached immortality.

5.17.4.b.s: ghṛtasya nāma guhyaṃ yadasti jihvā devānāmamṛtasya nābhiḥ //
5.17.4.b.d: घृतस्य नाम गुह्यं यदस्ति जिह्वा देवानाममृतस्य नाभिः ॥
5.17.4.b.m: The secret name of clarified butter that exists—the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality—

5.17.4.c.s: vayaṃ nāma prabravāmā ghṛtenāsminyajñe dhārayāmā namobhiḥ /
5.17.4.c.d: वयं नाम प्रब्रवामा घृतेनास्मिन्यज्ञे धारयामा नमोभिः ।
5.17.4.c.m: let us proclaim the name with clarified butter; in this sacrifice let us support [it] with homages.

5.17.4.d.d: उप ब्रह्मा शृणवच्छस्यमानं चतुःशृङ्गो ऽवमीद्गौर एतत् ॥
5.17.4.d.m: Let the brahman hear what is being recited; the four-horned ox bellowed this.

5.17.4.e.s: catvāri śṛṅgā trayo asya pādā dve śīrṣe sapta hastāso asya /
5.17.4.e.d: चत्वारि शृङ्गा त्रयो अस्य पादा द्वे शीर्षे सप्त हस्तासो अस्य ।
5.17.4.e.m: Four are his horns, three are his feet, two his heads, seven his hands;

5.17.4.f.s: tridhā baddho vṛṣabho roravīti maho devo martyām̐ āviveśeti śamīmayyo ghṛtānvaktāstisṛbhistisra ekaikasminnādadhāti /
5.17.4.f.d: त्रिधा बद्धो वृषभो रोरवीति महो देवो मर्त्याम्̐ आविवेशेति शमीमय्यो घृतान्वक्तास्तिसृभिस्तिस्र एकैकस्मिन्नादधाति ।
5.17.4.f.m: bound in three places, the bull roars loudly; the great god has entered mortals'—with these three [verses] he places three [firesticks] made of śamī wood and smeared with clarified butter on each one.

5.17.5.b.s: preddho agne dīdihi puro na ityaudumbarīṃ samidhamādadhāti /
5.17.5.b.d: प्रेद्धो अग्ने दीदिहि पुरो न इत्यौदुम्बरीं समिधमादधाति ।
5.17.5.b.m: 'Enkindled forward, O Agni, shine forth before us'—with this he places a firestick of udumbara wood;

5.17.5.c.s: vidhema te parame janmannagna iti vaikaṅkatīm /
5.17.5.c.d: विधेम ते परमे जन्मन्नग्न इति वैकङ्कतीम् ।
5.17.5.c.m: 'Let us pay worship to you at your highest birth, O Agni'—[with this, one] of vikaṅkata wood;

5.17.5.d.m: 'That wondrous [splendor] of the choice Savitṛ'—[with this, one] of śamī wood.

5.17.6.a.m: Then he performs the agnihotra silently.

5.17.7.a.s: api vā dvādaśagṛhītena srucaṃ pūrayitvā prajāpatiṃ manasā dhyāyañjuhoti /
5.17.7.a.d: अपि वा द्वादशगृहीतेन स्रुचं पूरयित्वा प्रजापतिं मनसा ध्यायञ्जुहोति ।
5.17.7.a.m: Or, having filled the ladle with a twelvefold scoop, meditating upon Prajāpati in thought, he offers.

5.17.7.b.m: This takes the place of the agnihotra.

5.17.8.a.s: yaste agne ghorāstanuvastābhiramuṃ gaccheti yajamāno dveṣyāya prahiṇoti tābhirenaṃ nitamayati /
5.17.8.a.d: यस्ते अग्ने घोरास्तनुवस्ताभिरमुं गच्छेति यजमानो द्वेष्याय प्रहिणोति ताभिरेनं नितमयति ।
5.17.8.a.m: With: 'Those terrifying bodies of yours, O Agni, with them go to so-and-so,' the sacrificer dispatches [them] against one who is hated; with them he brings him down.

5.17.8.b.m: They are to be recited in the wilderness.

5.18.1.a.s: dvādaśagṛhītena srucaṃ pūrayitvā sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvā iti saptavatyā pūrṇāhutiṃ juhoti /
5.18.1.a.d: द्वादशगृहीतेन स्रुचं पूरयित्वा सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वा इति सप्तवत्या पूर्णाहुतिं जुहोति ।
5.18.1.a.m: Having filled the ladle with a twelvefold scoop, he offers the full oblation with the seven-part verse: 'Seven are your firesticks, O Agni, seven your tongues.'

5.18.1.b.s: hutāyāṃ yajamāno varaṃ dattvā śivā japati /
5.18.1.b.d: हुतायां यजमानो वरं दत्त्वा शिवा जपति ।
5.18.1.b.m: When it has been offered, the sacrificer, having given a boon, mutters the auspicious [formulas].

5.18.1.c.s: ye agnayo divo ye pṛthivyāḥ samāgacchantīṣamūrjaṃ duhānāḥ /
5.18.1.c.d: ये अग्नयो दिवो ये पृथिव्याः समागच्छन्तीषमूर्जं दुहानाः ।
5.18.1.c.m: 'Whichsoever fires of the sky, whichsoever of the earth, come together, yielding refreshment and strength:

5.18.1.d.s: te asmā agnayo draviṇaṃ dattveṣṭāḥ prītā āhutibhājo bhūtvā yathālokaṃ punarastaṃ pareta svāheti juhoti
5.18.1.d.d: ते अस्मा अग्नयो द्रविणं दत्त्वेष्टाः प्रीता आहुतिभाजो भूत्वा यथालोकं पुनरस्तं परेत स्वाहेति जुहोति
5.18.1.d.m: let those fires, having given wealth to us, worshipped, gratified, having received oblations, depart back home according to their proper place, svāhā'—with this he offers.

5.18.2.a.s: atha virāṭkramairyajamāna upatiṣṭhate 'tharva pituṃ me gopāyānnaṃ prānena saṃmitam /
5.18.2.a.d: अथ विराट्क्रमैर्यजमान उपतिष्ठते ऽथर्व पितुं मे गोपायान्नं प्रानेन संमितम् ।
5.18.2.a.m: Then with the Virāj steps the sacrificer attends [upon the fires]: 'O Atharvan, protect my food, nourishment commensurate with breath;

5.18.2.b.s: tvayā guptā iṣamūrjaṃ madanto rāyaspoṣeṇa samiṣā mademetyanvāhāryapacanam //
5.18.2.b.d: त्वया गुप्ता इषमूर्जं मदन्तो रायस्पोषेण समिषा मदेमेत्यन्वाहार्यपचनम् ॥
5.18.2.b.m: protected by you, rejoicing in refreshment and strength, let us rejoice with abundance of wealth, with nourishment'—[thus he attends upon] the anvāhāryapacana.

5.18.2.c.s: narya prajāṃ me gopāya mūlaṃ lokasya saṃtatim /
5.18.2.c.d: नर्य प्रजां मे गोपाय मूलं लोकस्य संततिम् ।
5.18.2.c.m: 'O Narya, protect my offspring, the root of the world, the lineage!'

5.18.2.d.s: ātmano hṛdayānnirmitāṃ tāṃ te paridadāmyahamiti gārhapatyam //
5.18.2.d.d: आत्मनो हृदयान्निर्मितां तां ते परिददाम्यहमिति गार्हपत्यम् ॥
5.18.2.d.m: [With the words:] 'fashioned from my own heart, that I entrust to you,' [he worships] the gārhapatya.

5.18.2.e.s: śaṃsya paśūnme gopāya viśvarūpaṃ dhanaṃ vasu /
5.18.2.e.d: शंस्य पशून्मे गोपाय विश्वरूपं धनं वसु ।
5.18.2.e.m: 'O Praiseworthy one, protect my livestock, all-formed wealth and treasure;

5.18.2.f.m: the nourishment and joy of our homes, these I entrust to you,' [with these words he worships] the āhavanīya.

5.18.2.g.m: 'O Far-reaching one, protect my assembly, vital power that increases prosperity;

5.18.2.h.s: viśvajanasya chāyāṃ tāṃ te paridadāmyahamiti sabhyam //
5.18.2.h.d: विश्वजनस्य छायां तां ते परिददाम्यहमिति सभ्यम् ॥
5.18.2.h.m: the shelter of all people, that I entrust to you,' [with these words he worships] the sabhya.

5.18.2.i.s: ahe budhniya mantraṃ me gopāya śriyaṃ ca yaśasā saha /
5.18.2.i.d: अहे बुध्निय मन्त्रं मे गोपाय श्रियं च यशसा सह ।
5.18.2.i.m: 'O Serpent of the Deep, protect my sacred prayer, and fortune along with fame;

5.18.2.j.s: ahaye budhniyāya mantraṃ śriyaṃ yaśaḥ paridadāmyahamityāvasathyam //
5.18.2.j.d: अहये बुध्नियाय मन्त्रं श्रियं यशः परिददाम्यहमित्यावसथ्यम् ॥
5.18.2.j.m: to the Serpent of the Deep I entrust prayer, fortune, and fame,' [with these words he worships] the āvasathya.

5.18.2.k.m: 'Fivefold the Virāj strode across the fires, created from Prajāpati;

5.18.2.l.m: the red dawn ascended upward, the womb of Agni, the foundation,' with these words [he worships] all [the fires].

5.19.1.a.m: He sets in motion the procedure of the eight-potsherd [cake] for Agni.

5.19.2.a.m: The oblation is ladled out and brought forward, but not [yet] sprinkled.

5.19.2.b.s: atha sabhāyā madhye 'dhidevanamuddhatyāvokṣyākṣānnyupyākṣeṣu hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya samūhya vyūhya prathayitvā niṣasāda dhṛtavrata iti madhye 'dhidevane rājanyasya juhoti
5.19.2.b.d: अथ सभाया मध्ये ऽधिदेवनमुद्धत्यावोक्ष्याक्षान्न्युप्याक्षेषु हिरण्यं निधाय समूह्य व्यूह्य प्रथयित्वा निषसाद धृतव्रत इति मध्ये ऽधिदेवने राजन्यस्य जुहोति
5.19.2.b.m: Then, in the middle of the assembly hall, having raised the gaming ground, sprinkled it, cast down the dice, placed gold upon the dice, gathered them together, spread them out, and extended them, he makes an offering for a kṣatriya on the middle of the gaming ground with [the verse]: 'He sat down, he whose ordinances are firm...'

5.19.3.a.s: āvasathe pariṣado madhye hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya mantravatyā hiraṇye juhoti pra nūnaṃ brahmaṇaspatirmantraṃ vadatyukthyam /
5.19.3.a.d: आवसथे परिषदो मध्ये हिरण्यं निधाय मन्त्रवत्या हिरण्ये जुहोति प्र नूनं ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मन्त्रं वदत्युक्थ्यम् ।
5.19.3.a.m: In the āvasatha hall, having placed gold in the middle of the gathered assembly, he makes an offering upon the gold with the verse containing the word 'mantra': 'Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati speaks the mantra worthy of laudation,

5.19.3.b.s: yasminnindro varuṇo mitro aryamā devā okāṃsi cakrira iti
5.19.3.b.d: यस्मिन्निन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा देवा ओकांसि चक्रिर इति
5.19.3.b.m: in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the gods have made their abodes.'

5.19.4.a.d: उत नो ऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोत्वज एकपात्पृथिवी समुद्रः ।
5.19.4.a.m: 'And may the Serpent of the Deep hear us, Aja Ekapād, the earth, the ocean;

5.19.4.b.s: viśve devā ṛtāvṛdho huvānāḥ stutā mantrāḥ kaviśastā avantu na ity uktvā śatamakṣānyajamānāya prayacchannāha vrīhibhyo gāṃ dīvyatāhiṃsantaḥ parūṃṣi viśasateti
5.19.4.b.d: विश्वे देवा ऋतावृधो हुवानाः स्तुता मन्त्राः कविशस्ता अवन्तु न इत्य् उक्त्वा शतमक्षान्यजमानाय प्रयच्छन्नाह व्रीहिभ्यो गां दीव्यताहिंसन्तः परूंषि विशसतेति
5.19.4.b.m: may all the gods, augmenters of truth, when invoked, and the recited mantras praised by sages, protect us'—having said this, handing a hundred dice to the sacrificer, he says: 'Play for the cow [as stakes] against rice; without harming it, butcher the joints.'

5.19.5.a.m: They act according to the ritual call.

5.20.1.a.m: The sacrificer wins the winning throw.

5.20.2.a.s: tayā yajjayanti tadannaṃ saṃskṛtya sabhāsadbhya upaharanti
5.20.2.a.d: तया यज्जयन्ति तदन्नं संस्कृत्य सभासद्भ्य उपहरन्ति
5.20.2.a.m: Preparing the food that they win by means of it [the cow], they serve it to the members of the assembly.

5.20.4.a.s: kḷptisāmanasībhyāmagnīnyajamāna upatiṣṭhate kalpetāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ye 'gnayaḥ samanasa iti
5.20.4.a.d: कॢप्तिसामनसीभ्यामग्नीन्यजमान उपतिष्ठते कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी ये ऽग्नयः समनस इति
5.20.4.a.m: The sacrificer worships the fires with the Kḷpti and Sāmanasī verses: 'May heaven and earth be fit...' and 'Those fires that are concordant...'

5.20.5.a.m: He undertakes the rite beginning with the sprinkling.

5.20.6.a.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts of the cake for Agni, he gives the sacrificial gifts.

5.20.7.a.m: A goat, a full vessel, a bolster, and an entire garment of wool [he gives] to the agnīdh.

5.20.8.a.m: A draft horse to the brahman or to the adhvaryu.

5.20.9.a.m: An ox in the place of the āhavanīya to the adhvaryu.

5.20.10.a.m: To the west of the gārhapatya, a milch cow to the hotṛ.

5.20.11.a.s: vāso mithunau gāvau navaṃ ca rathaṃ dadāti /
5.20.11.a.d: वासो मिथुनौ गावौ नवं च रथं ददाति ।
5.20.11.a.m: He gives a garment, a pair of cattle, and a new chariot;

5.20.11.b.m: these are shared among all [the priests].

5.20.12.a.s: ā dvādaśabhyo dadātītyuktvāha kāmamūrdhvaṃ deyamaparimitasyāvaruddhyā iti vijñāyate
5.20.12.a.d: आ द्वादशभ्यो ददातीत्युक्त्वाह काममूर्ध्वं देयमपरिमितस्यावरुद्ध्या इति विज्ञायते
5.20.12.a.m: 'He gives up to twelve,' having said this, [the scripture] says: 'He may give at will beyond that, for the attainment of the boundless,' so it is taught.

5.20.13.a.s: ūrdhvamādiṣṭadakṣiṇābhyo vadati ṣaḍ deyā dvādaśa deyāścaturviṃśatirdeyā iti
5.20.13.a.d: ऊर्ध्वमादिष्टदक्षिणाभ्यो वदति षड् देया द्वादश देयाश्चतुर्विंशतिर्देया इति
5.20.13.a.m: Beyond the prescribed sacrificial gifts, it says: 'Six should be given, twelve should be given, twenty-four should be given.'

5.20.15.a.s: yeṣāṃ paśūnāṃ puṣṭiṃ bhūyasīṃ kāmayeta teṣāṃ vayasām
5.20.15.a.d: येषां पशूनां पुष्टिं भूयसीं कामयेत तेषां वयसाम्
5.20.15.a.m: Of whichever animals he should desire greater thriving, [he gives beasts] of their ages:

5.20.16.a.m: he should give an eighteen-month-old heifer, and an uncastrated eighteen-month-old bull.

5.20.17.a.m: He gives an increasing sacrificial gift.

5.20.18.a.s: yadyanāḍhyo 'gnīnādadhīta kāmamevaikāṃ gāṃ dadyātsā gavāṃ pratyāmnāyo bhavatīti vijñāyate
5.20.18.a.d: यद्यनाढ्यो ऽग्नीनादधीत काममेवैकां गां दद्यात्सा गवां प्रत्याम्नायो भवतीति विज्ञायते
5.20.18.a.m: 'If an impoverished man should establish the fires, he may give only a single cow at will; that becomes the substitute for [all] the cows,' so it is taught.

5.20.19.a.m: The offering is concluded in the established manner.

5.21.1.a.m: He should offer the Pavamāna oblations immediately on the same day,

5.21.2.a.s: dvādaśāhe dvyahe tryahe caturahe 'rdhamāse māsyṛtau saṃvatsare vā
5.21.2.a.d: द्वादशाहे द्व्यहे त्र्यहे चतुरहे ऽर्धमासे मास्यृतौ संवत्सरे वा
5.21.2.a.m: or after twelve days, after two days, after three days, after four days, after half a month, after a month, after a season, or after a year.

5.21.3.a.m: One who does not intend to sacrifice with soma should not offer [them] before a year.

5.21.5.a.s: yadi nirvapedagnaye pavamānāyāgnaye pāvakāyāgnaye śucaya iti tisra ājyāhutīḥ somadevatābhyo vā hutvā nirvapet
5.21.5.a.d: यदि निर्वपेदग्नये पवमानायाग्नये पावकायाग्नये शुचय इति तिस्र आज्याहुतीः सोमदेवताभ्यो वा हुत्वा निर्वपेत्
5.21.5.a.m: If he should offer [them earlier], he should offer [them] after making three clarified-butter offerings with: 'To Agni Pavamāna,' 'To Agni Pāvaka,' 'To Agni Śuci,' or to the deities of soma.

5.21.6.a.m: They share a single framework, or have separate frameworks, or share the framework with the [offering] to Agni.

5.21.7.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyānsyāditi tasyaikamekam etāni havīṃṣi nirvapet /
5.21.7.a.d: यं कामयेत पापीयान्स्यादिति तस्यैकमेकम् एतानि हवींषि निर्वपेत् ।
5.21.7.a.m: For one whom he desires, 'May he become worse,' he should offer these oblations one by one;

5.21.7.b.s: na vasīyānna pāpīyāniti tasya sākaṃ sarvāṇi /
5.21.7.b.d: न वसीयान्न पापीयानिति तस्य साकं सर्वाणि ।
5.21.7.b.m: for one whom he desires, 'May he become neither better nor worse,' he should offer all of them together;

5.21.7.c.s: yaṃ kāmayetottaraṃ vasīyāñchreyān syād iti tasyāgnaye pavamānāya nirupya pāvakaśucibhyāṃ samānabarhiṣī nirvapet
5.21.7.c.d: यं कामयेतोत्तरं वसीयाञ्छ्रेयान् स्याद् इति तस्याग्नये पवमानाय निरुप्य पावकशुचिभ्यां समानबर्हिषी निर्वपेत्
5.21.7.c.m: for one whom he desires, 'May he become progressively better and superior,' having offered [the oblation] for Agni Pavamāna, he should offer those for Pāvaka and Śuci on the same sacrificial grass.

5.21.8.a.m: A hundred measures of gold is the sacrificial gift.

5.21.9.a.m: For the first two oblations, two pieces of thirty measures [each]; for the latter one, a piece of forty measures.

5.21.10.a.s: yena hiraṇyaṃ mimate tena mītvā dadāti
5.21.10.a.d: येन हिरण्यं मिमते तेन मीत्वा ददाति
5.21.10.a.m: Measuring with whatever [unit] they measure gold, he gives it.

5.21.11.a.m: The offering is concluded in the established manner.

5.22.1.a.m: He performs a subsequent offering of an eleven-potsherd [cake] to Indra and Agni, and a caru in clarified butter to the Ādityas.

5.22.3.a.m: At the time of the fourfold division, he hands the [caru] for the Ādityas to the brahman.

5.22.4.a.m: Four descendants of ṛṣis partake of it.

5.22.5.a.m: To those who have partaken of it he gives an identical choice gift;

5.22.5.b.m: some teach the gift of a cow and an ox.

5.22.5.c.m: The offering is concluded in the established manner.

5.22.6.a.m: He performs a subsequent offering of an eleven-potsherd [cake] to Agni and Viṣṇu, an eleven-potsherd [cake] to Agni and Soma, and a caru in clarified butter cooked with three portions of rice to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa.

5.22.7.a.m: The offering is concluded in the established manner.

5.22.8.a.s: ādityaṃ ghṛte caruṃ saptadaśasāmidhenīkaṃ dhenudakṣiṇaṃ sarveṣāmanunirvāpyāṇāṃ sthāne vājasneyinaḥ samāmananti
5.22.8.a.d: आदित्यं घृते चरुं सप्तदशसामिधेनीकं धेनुदक्षिणं सर्वेषामनुनिर्वाप्याणां स्थाने वाजस्नेयिनः समामनन्ति
5.22.8.a.m: The followers of the Vājasaneyaka teach a caru in clarified butter to the Ādityas, accompanied by seventeen kindling verses and with a cow as the sacrificial gift, in place of all the subsequent offerings.

5.22.9.a.m: The iṣṭi is concluded in the established manner.

5.22.10.a.s: agnihotramārapsyamāno daśahotāraṃ manasānudrutyāhavanīye sagrahaṃ hutvātha sāyamagnihotraṃ juhoti
5.22.10.a.d: अग्निहोत्रमारप्स्यमानो दशहोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्याहवनीये सग्रहं हुत्वाथ सायमग्निहोत्रं जुहोति
5.22.10.a.m: When about to begin the agnihotra, he recites the daśahotṛ formula mentally, offers it together with the graha into the āhavanīya fire, and then offers the evening agnihotra.

5.22.11.a.m: He should set down [the offering] with the vyāhṛtis.

5.22.12.a.m: When the year has elapsed, he should set down [the offering] with these very [vyāhṛtis].

5.22.13.a.s: dvādaśāhamajasreṣvagniṣu yajamānaḥ svayamagnihotraṃ juhuyādapravasannahataṃ vāso bibharti
5.22.13.a.d: द्वादशाहमजस्रेष्वग्निषु यजमानः स्वयमग्निहोत्रं जुहुयादप्रवसन्नहतं वासो बिभर्ति
5.22.13.a.m: For twelve days, in fires that are kept constantly burning, the sacrificer should himself offer the agnihotra; without travelling away from home, he wears an unwashed garment.

5.23.1.a.s: yāṃ prathamāmagnihotrāya dogdhi tāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti
5.23.1.a.d: यां प्रथमामग्निहोत्राय दोग्धि तां दक्षिणां ददाति
5.23.1.a.m: The cow that he milks first for the agnihotra, that one he gives as a sacrificial gift.

5.23.2.b.s: agnīnādhāya hastāvavanijya saṃvatsaramagnihotraṃ hutvātha darśapūrṇamāsāvārabhate tābhyāṃ saṃvatsaramiṣṭvā somena paśunā vā yajate tata ūrdhvamanyāni karmāṇi kurute
5.23.2.b.d: अग्नीनाधाय हस्ताववनिज्य संवत्सरमग्निहोत्रं हुत्वाथ दर्शपूर्णमासावारभते ताभ्यां संवत्सरमिष्ट्वा सोमेन पशुना वा यजते तत ऊर्ध्वमन्यानि कर्माणि कुरुते
5.23.2.b.m: Having established the fires and washed his hands, having offered the agnihotra for a year, he then begins the New and Full Moon sacrifices; having sacrificed with both of them for a year, he sacrifices with soma or with an animal; thereafter, he performs other rites.

5.23.3.a.s: trayodaśarātramahatavāsā yajamānaḥ svayamagnihotraṃ juhuyādapravasannatraiva somena paśunā veṣṭvāgnīnutsṛjati yathā suyavasānkṛtvā prājyāttādṛktaditi śāṭyāyanibrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati
5.23.3.a.d: त्रयोदशरात्रमहतवासा यजमानः स्वयमग्निहोत्रं जुहुयादप्रवसन्नत्रैव सोमेन पशुना वेष्ट्वाग्नीनुत्सृजति यथा सुयवसान्कृत्वा प्राज्यात्तादृक्तदिति शाट्यायनिब्राह्मणं भवति
5.23.3.a.m: For thirteen nights, wearing an unwashed garment, the sacrificer should himself offer the agnihotra without travelling away; right here, having sacrificed with soma or with an animal, he lets the fires go out; 'just as one having brought [cattle] to good pasture might drive them forth, such is that'—so says the Śāṭyāyani Brāhmaṇa.

5.23.4.a.s: pūrṇā paścādyatte devā adadhuriti sārasvatau homau hutvānvārambhaṇīyāmiṣṭiṃ nirvapati
5.23.4.a.d: पूर्णा पश्चाद्यत्ते देवा अदधुरिति सारस्वतौ होमौ हुत्वान्वारम्भणीयामिष्टिं निर्वपति
5.23.4.a.m: Having offered the two Sārasvata oblations with: 'Full behind...' and 'What the gods placed...', he prepares the Anvārambhaṇīyā iṣṭi.

5.23.5.a.m: [It consists of] a cake on eleven potsherds for Agni and Viṣṇu, a caru for Sarasvatī, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Sarasvat.

5.23.6.a.s: agnaye bhagine 'ṣṭākapālaṃ yaḥ kāmayeta bhagyannādaḥ syāmiti
5.23.6.a.d: अग्नये भगिने ऽष्टाकपालं यः कामयेत भग्यन्नादः स्यामिति
5.23.6.a.m: For Agni Bhagin, a cake on eight potsherds, if he desires: 'May I be fortunate and an eater of food.'

5.23.7.a.m: Some hand it down as obligatory.

5.23.9.a.s: tvadviśvā subhaga saubhagānyagne vi yanti vanino na vayāḥ /
5.23.9.a.d: त्वद्विश्वा सुभग सौभगान्यग्ने वि यन्ति वनिनो न वयाः ।
5.23.9.a.m: 'From you, fortunate Agni, all fortunes branch out like boughs from a tree,

5.23.9.b.s: śruṣṭī rayirvājo vṛtratūrye divo vṛṣṭirīḍyo rītirapām //
5.23.9.b.d: श्रुष्टी रयिर्वाजो वृत्रतूर्ये दिवो वृष्टिरीड्यो रीतिरपाम् ॥
5.23.9.b.m: Obedience, wealth, food in the contest with Vṛtra, praise-worthy rain of heaven, the flow of waters.

5.23.9.c.s: tvaṃ bhago na ā hi ratnamiṣe parijmeva kṣayasi dasmavarcāḥ /
5.23.9.c.d: त्वं भगो न आ हि रत्नमिषे परिज्मेव क्षयसि दस्मवर्चाः ।
5.23.9.c.m: Like Bhaga, you bring us treasure for refreshment; like one encircling, you rule, endowed with wondrous splendour.

5.23.9.d.s: agne mitro na bṛhata ṛtasyāsi kṣattā vāmasya deva bhūreriti yājyānuvākye
5.23.9.d.d: अग्ने मित्रो न बृहत ऋतस्यासि क्षत्ता वामस्य देव भूरेरिति याज्यानुवाक्ये
5.23.9.d.m: Agni, like Mitra of the great cosmic order, you are the dispenser of abundant loveliness, O god'—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses.

5.24.1.a.m: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt, he offers the Jaya oblations with: 'Thought and thinking...'

5.24.2.a.s: cittāya svāhā cittyai svāhety eke samāmananti
5.24.2.a.d: चित्ताय स्वाहा चित्त्यै स्वाहेत्य् एके समामनन्ति
5.24.2.a.m: 'To thought, svāhā! To thinking, svāhā!'—thus some hand it down.

5.24.3.a.m: With: 'Prajāpati [created] the Jayas...', he offers the thirteenth [oblation].

5.24.4.a.s: agne balada saha ojaḥ kramamāṇāya me dāḥ /
5.24.4.a.d: अग्ने बलद सह ओजः क्रममाणाय मे दाः ।
5.24.4.a.m: 'O Agni, giver of strength, bestow vigour and might upon me as I step forward,

5.24.4.b.s: abhiśastikṛte 'nabhiśastenyāyāsyai janatāyai śraiṣṭyāyeti caturdaśīṃ yaḥ kāmayeta citraṃ janatāyāṃ syāmiti /
5.24.4.b.d: अभिशस्तिकृते ऽनभिशस्तेन्यायास्यै जनतायै श्रैष्ट्यायेति चतुर्दशीं यः कामयेत चित्रं जनतायां स्यामिति ।
5.24.4.b.m: Upon the curser, upon the blameless, for the supremacy of this community'—with this fourteenth [mantra] one who desires: 'May I be distinguished among the community.'

5.24.4.c.s: citraṃ bhavati śabalaṃ tvasya mukhe jāyate
5.24.4.c.d: चित्रं भवति शबलं त्वस्य मुखे जायते
5.24.4.c.m: He becomes distinguished; but a speckled mark appears on his face.

5.24.5.a.m: A pair of cattle is the sacrificial gift.

5.24.6.a.m: The iṣṭi is concluded in the established manner.

5.24.7.a.m: When about to begin the New and Full Moon sacrifices, he recites the caturhotṛ formula mentally, offers it together with the graha into the āhavanīya fire, and then begins the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

5.24.8.a.m: He should place the oblations with the vyāhṛtis; when the year has elapsed, he should place them with these very [vyāhṛtis].

5.24.9.a.m: This is for one establishing the fires on a new moon day.

5.24.9.b.m: On a full moon day, however, having completed the establishment of the fires along with the iṣṭi and the Anvārambhaṇīyā on the preceding joint-day,

5.25.1.a.m: On the next day, he sacrifices with the Full Moon sacrifice.

5.25.2.a.m: Directly after the establishment of the fires are the vows of one who has established the fires:

5.25.4.a.m: A brāhmaṇa should not stay in his house without having eaten.

5.25.5.a.m: He should not turn away for lodging a guest brought by the setting sun.

5.25.6.a.m: He should not eat food cooked in an earthen oven.

5.25.7.a.m: He should not put wet wood on [the fire].

5.25.8.a.m: He should not eat from water that is navigable by boat.

5.25.9.a.m: He should not settle on a naturally barren tract.

5.25.11.a.m: Having uttered the hiṅ-sound, with restrained speech, he should approach his wife.

5.25.13.a.m: He should not eat in the evening when the evening oblation is not yet offered.

5.25.15.a.s: āhitāgnergṛhe na sāyamahute bhoktavyaṃ tathā prātarityanyeṣāṃ vratam
5.25.15.a.d: आहिताग्नेर्गृहे न सायमहुते भोक्तव्यं तथा प्रातरित्यन्येषां व्रतम्
5.25.15.a.m: 'In the house of one who has established the fires, one should not eat when the evening [oblation] is not offered; likewise in the morning'—this is the vow according to others.

5.25.16.a.m: At night he should give nothing other than food.

5.25.18.a.m: Giving food, however, he should eat.

5.25.19.a.m: During this year, he should not eat meat without having sacrificed with an animal.

5.25.20.a.s: manasāgnibhyaḥ prahiṇomi bhakṣaṃ mama vācā taṃ saha bhakṣayantu /
5.25.20.a.d: मनसाग्निभ्यः प्रहिणोमि भक्षं मम वाचा तं सह भक्षयन्तु ।
5.25.20.a.m: 'Mentally I dispatch the portion to the fires; with my speech let them eat it together;

5.25.20.b.s: apramādyannapramattaścarāmi śivena manasā saha bhakṣayateti yadyādiṣṭo bhakṣayed etaṃ mantramuktvā bhakṣayet
5.25.20.b.d: अप्रमाद्यन्नप्रमत्तश्चरामि शिवेन मनसा सह भक्षयतेति यद्यादिष्टो भक्षयेद् एतं मन्त्रमुक्त्वा भक्षयेत्
5.25.20.b.m: Not erring, vigilant, I walk; with an auspicious mind, do you eat together'—if, being prescribed [to do so], he should eat, he should eat having recited this mantra.

5.26.1.a.m: We shall explain the re-establishment of the fires.

5.26.2.a.m: Its procedure is like that of the establishment of the fires.

5.26.3.a.s: agnīnādhāyaitasminsaṃvatsare yo nardhnuyātsa punarādadhīta prajākāmaḥ paśukāmaḥ puṣṭikāmo jyānyāṃ putramartyāyāṃ sveṣvārudhyamāneṣu yadā vāṅgena vidhuratāṃ nīyāt
5.26.3.a.d: अग्नीनाधायैतस्मिन्संवत्सरे यो नर्ध्नुयात्स पुनरादधीत प्रजाकामः पशुकामः पुष्टिकामो ज्यान्यां पुत्रमर्त्यायां स्वेष्वारुध्यमानेषु यदा वाङ्गेन विधुरतां नीयात्
5.26.3.a.m: He who, having established the fires, does not prosper during this year, should re-establish them, if desiring offspring, desiring cattle, desiring prosperity, or upon suffering loss, upon the death of a son, when his own people are kept in distress, or when he is reduced to infirmity in a limb.

5.26.4.a.s: āgneyamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapedvaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ vāruṇaṃ daśakapālamagnaye 'psumate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ maitraṃ carumagnimudvāsayiṣyan
5.26.4.a.d: आग्नेयमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद्वैश्वानरं द्वादशकपालं वारुणं दशकपालमग्नये ऽप्सुमते ऽष्टाकपालं मैत्रं चरुमग्निमुद्वासयिष्यन्
5.26.4.a.m: When about to extinguish the fire, he should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, a cake on twelve potsherds to Vaiśvānara, a cake on ten potsherds to Varuṇa, a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Apsumat, and a caru to Mitra.

5.26.5.a.s: yā te agna utsīdataḥ pavamānā priyā tanūḥ /
5.26.5.a.d: या ते अग्न उत्सीदतः पवमाना प्रिया तनूः ।
5.26.5.a.m: 'O Agni, that dear purifying form of yours which rises up,

5.26.5.b.s: tayā saha pṛthivīmāviśa rathaṃtareṇa sāmnā gāyatreṇa ca chandasā //
5.26.5.b.d: तया सह पृथिवीमाविश रथंतरेण साम्ना गायत्रेण च छन्दसा ॥
5.26.5.b.m: With that enter into the earth, together with the Rathaṃtara Sāman and the Gāyatrī metre.

5.26.5.c.s: yā te agne pāvakā yā manasā preyasī priyā tanūḥ /
5.26.5.c.d: या ते अग्ने पावका या मनसा प्रेयसी प्रिया तनूः ।
5.26.5.c.m: O Agni, that purifying, that dear form of yours which is dearer than the mind,

5.26.5.d.s: tayā sahāntarikṣamāviśa vāmadevyena sāmnā traiṣṭubhena ca chandasā /
5.26.5.d.d: तया सहान्तरिक्षमाविश वामदेव्येन साम्ना त्रैष्टुभेन च छन्दसा ।
5.26.5.d.m: With that enter into the atmosphere, together with the Vāmadevya Sāman and the Traiṣṭubha metre;

5.26.5.e.s: tato na ūrjamā kṛdhi gṛhamedhaṃ ca vardhaya //
5.26.5.e.d: ततो न ऊर्जमा कृधि गृहमेधं च वर्धय ॥
5.26.5.e.m: Thence make us vigour and increase the domestic sacrifice.'

5.26.5.f.s: yā te agne sūrye śuciḥ priyā tanūḥ śukre 'dhyadhi saṃbhṛtā /
5.26.5.f.d: या ते अग्ने सूर्ये शुचिः प्रिया तनूः शुक्रे ऽध्यधि संभृता ।
5.26.5.f.m: "O Agni, that pure, beloved form of yours, which is brought together over the bright [sun],

5.26.5.g.s: tayā saha divamāviśa bṛhatā sāmnā jāgatena ca chandasā tato no vṛṣṭyāvata //
5.26.5.g.d: तया सह दिवमाविश बृहता साम्ना जागतेन च छन्दसा ततो नो वृष्ट्यावत ॥
5.26.5.g.m: together with it enter heaven with the Bṛhat chant and the Jāgatī metre; thence protect us with rain."

5.26.5.h.m: "O Agni, those wish-granting distributed forms of yours that have been gathered together:

5.26.5.i.m: with them milk for us wishes here: offspring, prosperity, and wealth."

5.26.5.j.m: "O Agni, the materials which Indra, as a boar, brought for you:

5.26.5.k.s: tāsu śociṣu sīdeha bhasma vaiśvānarasya yat
5.26.5.k.d: तासु शोचिषु सीदेह भस्म वैश्वानरस्य यत्
5.26.5.k.m: in those flames sit here, what is the ash of Vaiśvānara."

5.27.1.a.s: ye te agne vānaspatyāḥ saṃbhārāḥ saṃbhṛtāḥ saha /
5.27.1.a.d: ये ते अग्ने वानस्पत्याः संभाराः संभृताः सह ।
5.27.1.a.m: "O Agni, those materials belonging to trees that have been gathered together:

5.27.1.b.m: with them go each to the trees, to your own womb."

5.27.1.c.m: "Agni has gone according to his realm; he has sat in his own seat.

5.27.1.d.s: avīrahatyaṃ deveṣūpāgāṃ manasā saheti purastātsviṣṭakṛtaḥ saptāhutīrjuhoti
5.27.1.d.d: अवीरहत्यं देवेषूपागां मनसा सहेति पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतः सप्ताहुतीर्जुहोति
5.27.1.d.m: With my mind I have approached non-destruction of heroes among the gods"—with [these mantras] he offers seven oblations before the Sviṣṭakṛt [offering].

5.27.2.a.m: The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.

5.27.3.a.m: Having performed the Full Moon sacrifice, he discards the burning fires.

5.27.4.a.m: He remains one who has discarded his fires for a year at most.

5.27.5.a.m: Rohiṇī, Punarvasū, [or] Anurādhā are the asterisms [for re-establishing them].

5.27.6.a.m: He should establish them in the rainy season or in autumn.

5.27.7.a.m: The ritual materials and the yajus mantras are optional.

5.27.8.a.m: Or rather, he brings five earthen materials;
