5.27.9.a.m: Having strewn old darbha grass on the hearths, he establishes the gārhapatya fire with the Sarparājñī verses, [beginning with] "Earth with fullness".

5.27.11.a.m: With scorched darbha grass from last year, withered by the wind for a year, he takes out the burning āhavanīya fire.

5.27.12.a.m: With "Since an angry one discarded you" [he takes out] the southern fire;

5.27.12.b.m: with "What of you discarded through fury" [he takes out] the other [fires].

5.27.13.a.m: He reveres [the fire] with the verse containing [the name of] Bṛhaspati: "May Mind delight in the light".

5.27.14.a.s: sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvā ityagnihotraṃ juhoti
5.27.14.a.d: सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वा इत्यग्निहोत्रं जुहोति
5.27.14.a.m: He offers the agnihotra with: "Seven are your kindling sticks, O Agni; seven your tongues".

5.28.1.a.m: He measures out [a cake] on five potsherds or on eight potsherds for Agni.

5.28.2.a.m: If it is on five potsherds, the two consecratory-and-invitatory verses are in the Gāyatrī metre;

5.28.2.b.m: if it is on eight potsherds, they are in the Paṅkti metre.

5.28.4.a.m: The kindling verses are fifteen or seventeen.

5.28.5.a.m: Beginning with the kindling verses, he sacrifices in a low voice until the final after-offering, [and] loud for the Sviṣṭakṛt.

5.28.6.a.s: agnāgne 'gnāvagne 'gnināgne 'gnimagna iti caturṣu prayājeṣu catasro vibhaktīrdadhāti
5.28.6.a.d: अग्नाग्ने ऽग्नावग्ने ऽग्निनाग्ने ऽग्निमग्न इति चतुर्षु प्रयाजेषु चतस्रो विभक्तीर्दधाति
5.28.6.a.m: In four fore-offerings he inserts four case-forms: "agnā agne", "agnāv agne", "agninā agne", [and] "agnim agne".

5.28.8.a.m: Having uttered the case-form, he utters the vaṣaṭ-call with the fore-offering [formula].

5.28.9.a.s: yaṃ kāmayetardhnuyāditi tasyopariṣṭādyeyajāmahādvibhaktiṃ dadhyātpurā vā vaṣaṭkārāt
5.28.9.a.d: यं कामयेतर्ध्नुयादिति तस्योपरिष्टाद्येयजामहाद्विभक्तिं दध्यात्पुरा वा वषट्कारात्
5.28.9.a.m: For one whom he wishes should thrive, he should insert the case-form after "ye yajāmahe" or before the vaṣaṭ-call.

5.28.10.a.d: अग्निं स्तोमेन बोधयेत्याग्नेयस्याज्यभागस्य पुरो ऽनुवाक्या भवति ।
5.28.10.a.m: "Awaken Agni with praise" is the invitatory verse of the butter portion for Agni;

5.28.10.b.m: "O Agni, [give] life spans from marrow" [is the invitatory verse] of that for Soma.

5.28.11.a.m: Or he may make "Agni is the head" [the invitatory verse] of that for Soma

5.28.12.a.m: for one desirous of offspring, desirous of cattle, or deprived of offspring or deprived of cattle.

5.28.13.a.m: The verses of the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings are marked by [the name] Agni.

5.28.14.a.m: Or rather, just as the two butter portions are according to the original model, so are the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.

5.28.15.a.m: The invitatory and consecratory verses are in the Akṣarapaṅkti metre: "O Agni, that horse today";

5.28.15.b.m: two for the [offering] to Agni, two for the Sviṣṭakṛt.

5.28.16.a.s: punarūrjā saha rayyetyabhitaḥ puroḍāśam āhutīr juhoti
5.28.16.a.d: पुनरूर्जा सह रय्येत्यभितः पुरोडाशम् आहुतीर् जुहोति
5.28.16.a.m: With "Again with strength" [and] "Together with wealth" he offers oblations on both sides of the sacrificial cake.

5.28.17.a.m: Or with "Again with strength" before the fore-offerings, and with "Together with wealth" after the after-offerings.

5.28.19.a.m: He gives both kinds of sacrificial gifts:

5.29.1.a.s: āgnyādheyikīḥ paunarādheyikīśca punarniṣkṛto ratha ity etāḥ śatamānaṃ ca hiraṇyam
5.29.1.a.d: आग्न्याधेयिकीः पौनराधेयिकीश्च पुनर्निष्कृतो रथ इत्य् एताः शतमानं च हिरण्यम्
5.29.1.a.m: those belonging to the fire-establishment and those belonging to the re-establishment: "a renovated chariot" and these, and gold weighing a hundred mānas.

5.29.3.a.s: punarabhihito rathaḥ punarutsyūtaṃ syāmūlaṃ punaḥkāmasyāptyā ity ekeṣām
5.29.3.a.d: पुनरभिहितो रथः पुनरुत्स्यूतं स्यामूलं पुनःकामस्याप्त्या इत्य् एकेषाम्
5.29.3.a.m: "A chariot harnessed anew, a garment made of coarse cloth stitched anew, for the attainment of renewed desire"—according to some.

5.29.4.a.m: If the others are not found, he should give even an ox alone;

5.29.4.b.s: anaḍuhi ha vā ete ca kāmā ataśca bhūyāṃsa iti paiṅgāyanibrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati
5.29.4.b.d: अनडुहि ह वा एते च कामा अतश्च भूयांस इति पैङ्गायनिब्राह्मणं भवति
5.29.4.b.m: "In an ox, indeed, are these desires, and even more than this"—so is the Paiṅgāyani Brāhmaṇa.

5.29.5.a.s: deve agnau devo agniriti dvayoranūyājayorvibhaktī dadhāti
5.29.5.a.d: देवे अग्नौ देवो अग्निरिति द्वयोरनूयाजयोर्विभक्ती दधाति
5.29.5.a.m: In two after-offerings he inserts case-forms: "deve agnau", "devo agniḥ".

5.29.7.a.m: He issues the ritual call for the last one loudly.

5.29.8.a.m: The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.

5.29.9.a.m: He pours out an offering on eleven potsherds to Agni and Varuṇa following it, in place of all the subsequent offerings, or for those [gods] sharing two deities.

5.29.10.a.m: The sacrifice concludes in the established manner;

5.29.11.a.s: yastṛtīyamādadhīta sa etānhomāñjuhuyāllekaḥ salekaḥ suleka iti
5.29.11.a.d: यस्तृतीयमादधीत स एतान्होमाञ्जुहुयाल्लेकः सलेकः सुलेक इति
5.29.11.a.m: He who would establish [the fires] a third time should offer these oblations: "Leka, Saleka, Suleka".

5.29.12.a.m: If [the fire] taken up into the two churning sticks is lost,

5.29.13.a.m: or if the sun should set or rise when both his fires have gone out, the punarādheya is the expiation for it.

5.29.14.a.m: “The punarādheya,” says Āśmarathya; “the agnyādheya,” says Ālekhana, Ālekhana.

6.1.2.a.s: adhivṛkṣasūrya āviḥsūrye vā dhṛṣṭirasi brahma yacchetyupaveṣamādāya gārhapatyamabhimantrayate sugārhapatya iti
6.1.2.a.d: अधिवृक्षसूर्य आविःसूर्ये वा धृष्टिरसि ब्रह्म यच्छेत्युपवेषमादाय गार्हपत्यमभिमन्त्रयते सुगार्हपत्य इति
6.1.2.a.m: When the sun is above the trees or when the sun is visible, taking the fire-poker with: “You are the fire-stirrer; grant sacred power,” he addresses the gārhapatya with: “Good gārhapatya…”

6.1.3.a.s: athainaṃ bodhayaty udbudhyasvāgne prati jāgṛhyenam iṣṭāpūrte saṃsṛjethāmayaṃ ca /
6.1.3.a.d: अथैनं बोधयत्य् उद्बुध्यस्वाग्ने प्रति जागृह्येनम् इष्टापूर्ते संसृजेथामयं च ।
6.1.3.a.m: Then he awakens it with: “Awake, O Agni, be vigilant towards him; let this man and his sacrificial and charitable deeds unite

6.1.3.b.s: asmin sadhasthe adhyuttarasmin viśve devā yajamānaś ca sīdateti
6.1.3.b.d: अस्मिन् सधस्थे अध्युत्तरस्मिन् विश्वे देवा यजमानश् च सीदतेति
6.1.3.b.m: in this higher seat; O all gods and sacrificer, sit down!”

6.1.4.a.m: “Bring out [the fire]!” is indeed what the sacrificer says in the evening;

6.1.5.a.m: By this he secures a thousand wish-granting cows.

6.1.6.a.s: vācā tvā hotrā prāṇenodgātrā cakṣuṣādhvaryuṇā manasā brahmaṇā śrotreṇāgnīdhaitaistvā pañcabhirdaivyair ṛtvigbhir uddharāmīti gārhapatyādāhavanīyaṃ jvalantamuddharati
6.1.6.a.d: वाचा त्वा होत्रा प्राणेनोद्गात्रा चक्षुषाध्वर्युणा मनसा ब्रह्मणा श्रोत्रेणाग्नीधैतैस्त्वा पञ्चभिर्दैव्यैर् ऋत्विग्भिर् उद्धरामीति गार्हपत्यादाहवनीयं ज्वलन्तमुद्धरति
6.1.6.a.m: With: “With speech as hotṛ, with breath as udgātṛ, with sight as adhvaryu, with mind as brahman, with hearing as agnīdh—with these five divine officiants I bring you out,” he brings out the blazing āhavanīya from the gārhapatya.

6.1.7.a.s: bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaruddhriyamāṇa uddhara pāpmano mā yadavidvānyacca vidvāṃścakāra /
6.1.7.a.d: भूर्भुवः सुवरुद्ध्रियमाण उद्धर पाप्मनो मा यदविद्वान्यच्च विद्वांश्चकार ।
6.1.7.a.m: “Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ! Being brought out, bring me out from evil, whatever I have done knowingly and whatever unknowingly;

6.1.7.b.s: ahnā yadenaḥ kṛtamasti pāpaṃ sarvasmānmoddhṛto muñca tasmādityuddhriyamāṇamabhimantrayate yajamānaḥ sāyam /
6.1.7.b.d: अह्ना यदेनः कृतमस्ति पापं सर्वस्मान्मोद्धृतो मुञ्च तस्मादित्युद्ध्रियमाणमभिमन्त्रयते यजमानः सायम् ।
6.1.7.b.m: whatever sinful deed has been done by day, from all that, being brought out, release me!”—with this [formula] the sacrificer addresses [the fire] while it is being brought out in the evening;

6.1.7.c.s: rātryā yadenaḥ kṛtamasti pāpaṃ sarvasmānmoddhṛto muñca tasmāditi prātaḥ
6.1.7.c.d: रात्र्या यदेनः कृतमस्ति पापं सर्वस्मान्मोद्धृतो मुञ्च तस्मादिति प्रातः
6.1.7.c.m: with: “Whatever sinful deed has been done by night, from all that, being brought out, release me!” in the morning.

6.1.8.a.d: अग्निपतये ऽग्नये मे विद्ध्यग्निपतये ऽग्नये मे मृड ।
6.1.8.a.m: “Know me, O Agni, lord of fire; be gracious to me, O Agni, lord of fire!

6.1.8.b.m: I offer the immortal oblation into the immortal Agni on the earth for the conquest of immortality;

6.1.8.c.s: tayānantaṃ kāmamahaṃ jayāni prajāpatiryaṃ prathamo jigāyāgnimagnau svāhā
6.1.8.c.d: तयानन्तं काममहं जयानि प्रजापतिर्यं प्रथमो जिगायाग्निमग्नौ स्वाहा
6.1.8.c.m: by it may I conquer endless desire, which Prajāpati first conquered; to Agni in Agni, svāhā!”

6.2.1.a.s: agne samrāḍajaikapādāhavanīya divaḥ pṛthivyāḥ paryantarikṣāllokaṃ vinda yajamānāya /
6.2.1.a.d: अग्ने सम्राडजैकपादाहवनीय दिवः पृथिव्याः पर्यन्तरिक्षाल्लोकं विन्द यजमानाय ।
6.2.1.a.m: “O Agni, sovereign, Aja Ekapād, āhavanīya! From sky, from earth, from the intermediate space find a world for the sacrificer!

6.2.1.b.m: I set you down on the head of the earth, in the sacred realm.

6.2.1.c.s: yo no agne niṣṭyo yo 'niṣṭyo 'bhidāsatīdamahaṃ taṃ tvayābhinidadhāmīti purastātparikramyodaṅmukhaḥ pratyaṅmukho vā sāyamāyatane 'gniṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati /
6.2.1.c.d: यो नो अग्ने निष्ट्यो यो ऽनिष्ट्यो ऽभिदासतीदमहं तं त्वयाभिनिदधामीति पुरस्तात्परिक्रम्योदङ्मुखः प्रत्यङ्मुखो वा सायमायतने ऽग्निं प्रतिष्ठापयति ।
6.2.1.c.m: He who, kin to us, O Agni, or not kin to us, attacks us, him do I here set down by means of you!”—having walked around from the east, facing north or facing west, he establishes the fire in its seat in the evening;

6.2.2.a.s: svayaṃ yajamāna idhmānāharati viśvadānīmābharanto nātureṇa manasā /
6.2.2.a.d: स्वयं यजमान इध्मानाहरति विश्वदानीमाभरन्तो नातुरेण मनसा ।
6.2.2.a.m: The sacrificer himself brings pieces of firewood with: “Bringing [them] at all times with an untroubled mind,

6.2.2.b.m: O Agni, may we, your neighbours, not be harmed.”

6.2.3.a.s: yadagne yāni kāni cetyetābhiḥ pañcabhiḥ pratimantramagniṣu mhata idhmānādadhāti
6.2.3.a.d: यदग्ने यानि कानि चेत्येताभिः पञ्चभिः प्रतिमन्त्रमग्निषु म्हत इध्मानादधाति
6.2.3.a.m: With these five [verses], “Whatever [fuel], O Agni…”, he places fuel sticks on the fires, one verse to each stick.

6.2.5.a.m: In the order in which they were established, or starting from the āhavanīya.

6.2.6.a.m: The fire should be laid so that the oblation does not go astray.

6.2.8.a.m: If the eastern [fire] has gone out, one may pass through,

6.2.9.a.m: for it has then gone back to the west.

6.2.10.a.m: “At will one may pass through after the offering has been made,” say some.

6.2.11.a.m: He maintains the āhavanīya during the night.

6.2.12.a.m: For one who has attained prosperity, it is maintained constantly.

6.2.14.a.m: Likewise the anvāhāryapacana, if it has been established by churning.

6.2.15.a.m: If it is to be brought, they bring it every day from the south.

6.2.16.a.m: “They should bring it only on the fast day, or they should bring it only on entering a new residence,” states the Vājasaneyaka.

6.3.1.a.m: They adorn the fires by sweeping around them.

6.3.2.a.m: Adornment is done beforehand in the evening, afterward in the morning.

6.3.3.b.s: ubhayato 'laṃkārāḥ sāyaṃ tathā prātar ity eke
6.3.3.b.d: उभयतो ऽलंकाराः सायं तथा प्रातर् इत्य् एके
6.3.3.b.m: “Adornment on both sides in the evening, likewise in the morning,” say some.

6.3.4.a.s: agne gṛhapate śundhasveti gārhapatyamagne vahne śundhasveti dakṣiṇāgnimange samrāṭ śundhasvetyāhavanīyamagne sabhya śundhasveti sabhyamagne pariṣadya śundhasvetyāvasathyam
6.3.4.a.d: अग्ने गृहपते शुन्धस्वेति गार्हपत्यमग्ने वह्ने शुन्धस्वेति दक्षिणाग्निमन्गे सम्राट् शुन्धस्वेत्याहवनीयमग्ने सभ्य शुन्धस्वेति सभ्यमग्ने परिषद्य शुन्धस्वेत्यावसथ्यम्
6.3.4.a.m: With: “O Agni, lord of the house, purify yourself,” [he sweeps around] the gārhapatya; with: “O Agni, bearer [of oblations], purify yourself,” the dakṣiṇāgni; with: “O Agni, sovereign, purify yourself,” the āhavanīya; with: “O Agni of the hall, purify yourself,” the sabhya; with: “O Agni of the assembly, purify yourself,” the āvasathya.

6.3.5.a.m: With darbha grass or other grass pointing north and pointing east, he strews around the fires, or fire by fire.

6.3.6.a.m: The sruva is made of khadira wood; the agnihotra-ladle is made of vikankata wood, measuring an arm’s length or a cubit.

6.3.7.a.m: The agnihotra pot is broad-shaped, made by an Ārya, with an upright rim, and formed without a potter’s wheel.

6.3.8.a.s: dakṣiṇena vihāramagnihotrī tiṣṭhati tāṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrayata iḍāsi vratabhṛdahaṃ nāvubhayorvrataṃ cariṣyāmi surohiṇyahaṃ nāvubhayorvrataṃ cariṣyāmīḍa ehi mayi śrayasvera ehyadita ehi gaurehi śraddha ehi satyena tvāhvayāmīti
6.3.8.a.d: दक्षिणेन विहारमग्निहोत्री तिष्ठति तां यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्रयत इडासि व्रतभृदहं नावुभयोर्व्रतं चरिष्यामि सुरोहिण्यहं नावुभयोर्व्रतं चरिष्यामीड एहि मयि श्रयस्वेर एह्यदित एहि गौरेहि श्रद्ध एहि सत्येन त्वाह्वयामीति
6.3.8.a.m: To the south of the sacred ground stands the agnihotra cow; the sacrificer addresses her with: “You are Iḍā, observer of vows; I will observe the vow of both of us. O good Rohiṇī, I will observe the vow of both of us. O Iḍā, come; stay in me. O food, come; O Aditi, come; O cow, come; O faith, come; with truth I summon you!”

6.3.9.a.s: atha vedideśamabhimṛśatīyamasi tasyāste 'gnirvatsaḥ sā me svargaṃ ca lokamamṛtaṃ ca dhukṣveti
6.3.9.a.d: अथ वेदिदेशमभिमृशतीयमसि तस्यास्ते ऽग्निर्वत्सः सा मे स्वर्गं च लोकममृतं च धुक्ष्वेति
6.3.9.a.m: Then he touches the place of the altar ground with: “You are this [earth]; Agni is your calf. As such, milk for me the heavenly world and immortality!”

6.3.10.a.s: pūṣāsīti dakṣiṇato vatsamupasṛjya prācīmāvṛtya dogdhyudīcīṃ prācīmudīcīṃ vā
6.3.10.a.d: पूषासीति दक्षिणतो वत्समुपसृज्य प्राचीमावृत्य दोग्ध्युदीचीं प्राचीमुदीचीं वा
6.3.10.a.m: Having let loose the calf from the south with: “You are Pūṣan,” turning [her] eastward, he milks her facing north, or facing northeast.

6.3.12.a.m: For what the Śūdra is, is born of non-existence.

6.3.14.a.m: Because he puts it over the gārhapatya, he thereby purifies it.

6.3.15.a.m: He milks using the agnihotra pot and the milking pail.

6.4.1.a.s: pūrvau duhyājjyeṣṭhasya jyaiṣṭhineyasya yo vā gataśrīḥ syāt /
6.4.1.a.d: पूर्वौ दुह्याज्ज्येष्ठस्य ज्यैष्ठिनेयस्य यो वा गतश्रीः स्यात् ।
6.4.1.a.m: He should milk the two front [teats] for the eldest son, for the son of the eldest wife, or for one who has attained prosperity;

6.4.1.b.s: aparau duhyātkaniṣṭhasya kāniṣṭhaneyasya yo vānujāvaro yo vā bubhūṣet
6.4.1.b.d: अपरौ दुह्यात्कनिष्ठस्य कानिष्ठनेयस्य यो वानुजावरो यो वा बुभूषेत्
6.4.1.b.m: he should milk the two hind [teats] for the youngest son, for the son of the youngest wife, for a younger brother, or for one who desires to prosper.

6.4.3.a.m: In the regular ritual form, he milks according to how they are grasped.

6.4.4.a.d: पूर्ववदुपसृष्टां दुह्यमानां धाराघोषं च यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
6.4.4.a.m: The sacrificer follows [with formulas] the cow let loose, being milked, and the sound of the milk-stream, as before.

6.4.6.a.m: The offering should be made immediately after sunset.

6.4.7.a.s: samudro vā eṣa yadahorātrastasyaite gādhe tīrthe yatsaṃdhī tasmātsamdhau hotavyamiti śailālibrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati
6.4.7.a.d: समुद्रो वा एष यदहोरात्रस्तस्यैते गाधे तीर्थे यत्संधी तस्मात्सम्धौ होतव्यमिति शैलालिब्राह्मणं भवति
6.4.7.a.m: "Day and night are indeed an ocean; its shallow fords are the twilights. Therefore one should offer at twilight"—so says the Śailāli-Brāhmaṇa.

6.4.8.a.s: nakṣatraṃ dṛṣṭvā pradoṣe niśāyāṃ vā sāyam
6.4.8.a.d: नक्षत्रं दृष्ट्वा प्रदोषे निशायां वा सायम्
6.4.8.a.m: In the evening, [one offers] having seen a star, at nightfall, or at night.

6.4.9.a.m: In the morning, [one offers] at dawn, near sunrise, when the sun is halfway risen, or when it has risen.

6.4.10.a.s: yadudite juhotyagniṣṭomaṃ tenāvarunddhe yanmadhyaṃdine juhotyukthyaṃ tenāvarunddhe yadaparāhṇe juhoti ṣoḍaśinaṃ tenāvarunddhe yatpūrvarātre juhoti prathamaṃ tena rātriparyāyamapnoti yanmadhyarātre juhoti madhyamaṃ tena rātriparyāyamāpnoti yadapararātre juhoti jaghanyaṃ tena rātriparyāyamāpnoti
6.4.10.a.d: यदुदिते जुहोत्यग्निष्टोमं तेनावरुन्द्धे यन्मध्यंदिने जुहोत्युक्थ्यं तेनावरुन्द्धे यदपराह्णे जुहोति षोडशिनं तेनावरुन्द्धे यत्पूर्वरात्रे जुहोति प्रथमं तेन रात्रिपर्यायमप्नोति यन्मध्यरात्रे जुहोति मध्यमं तेन रात्रिपर्यायमाप्नोति यदपररात्रे जुहोति जघन्यं तेन रात्रिपर्यायमाप्नोति
6.4.10.a.m: "When one offers after sunrise, thereby one secures the Agniṣṭoma; when one offers at midday, thereby one secures the Ukthya; when one offers in the afternoon, thereby one secures the Ṣoḍaśin; when one offers in the first part of the night, thereby one obtains the first night round; when one offers at midnight, thereby one obtains the middle night round; when one offers in the latter part of the night, thereby one obtains the last night round.

6.4.11.a.s: sa na manyeta sarveṣveteṣu kāleṣu hotavyamāpadi hutamityeva pratīyāditi vijñāyate
6.4.11.a.d: स न मन्येत सर्वेष्वेतेषु कालेषु होतव्यमापदि हुतमित्येव प्रतीयादिति विज्ञायते
6.4.11.a.m: He should not think that one ought to offer at all these times; one should understand that it is offered [at those times only] in case of emergency"—so it is known [from sacred tradition].

6.5.1.a.m: His agnihotra is accompanied by his wife.

6.5.2.a.m: The wife sits down in her own place.

6.5.3.a.s: apareṇāhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśya yajamāno vidyudasi vidya me pāpmānamṛtātsatyamupaimi mayi śraddhetyapa ācāmati
6.5.3.a.d: अपरेणाहवनीयं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविश्य यजमानो विद्युदसि विद्य मे पाप्मानमृतात्सत्यमुपैमि मयि श्रद्धेत्यप आचामति
6.5.3.a.m: Having stepped beyond [the space] to the west of the āhavanīya toward the south and sat down, the sacrificer sips water, saying: "You are lightning; dispel my evil. From the cosmic order I approach truth; faith [be] in me."

6.5.4.a.s: ṛtaṃ tvā satyena pariṣiñcāmīti sāyaṃ pariṣiñcati /
6.5.4.a.d: ऋतं त्वा सत्येन परिषिञ्चामीति सायं परिषिञ्चति ।
6.5.4.a.m: In the evening he sprinkles [the fires with water] with: "I sprinkle around you, cosmic order, with truth."

6.5.4.b.m: In the morning with: "I sprinkle around you, truth, with cosmic order."

6.5.4.c.s: āhavanīyamagre 'tha gārhapatyamatha dakṣiṇāgnimapi vā gārhapatyamāhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇāgniṃ yathā vāhitāḥ
6.5.4.c.d: आहवनीयमग्रे ऽथ गार्हपत्यमथ दक्षिणाग्निमपि वा गार्हपत्यमाहवनीयं दक्षिणाग्निं यथा वाहिताः
6.5.4.c.m: First the āhavanīya, then the gārhapatya, then the anvāhāryapacana; or the gārhapatya, the āhavanīya, and the anvāhāryapacana; or in the order in which they were established.

6.5.5.a.s: yajñasya saṃtatirasi yajñasya tvā saṃtatimanusaṃtanomīti gārhaptayātprakramya saṃtatāmudakadhārāṃ srāvayatyāhavanīyāt
6.5.5.a.d: यज्ञस्य संततिरसि यज्ञस्य त्वा संततिमनुसंतनोमीति गार्हप्तयात्प्रक्रम्य संततामुदकधारां स्रावयत्याहवनीयात्
6.5.5.a.m: Starting from the gārhapatya, he pours an unbroken stream of water up to the āhavanīya, saying: "You are the continuity of the sacrifice; I extend you continuously along the continuity of the sacrifice."

6.5.6.a.s: dhṛṣṭirasi brahma yacchetyupaveṣamādāya bhūtakṛta sthāpoḍhaṃ janyaṃ bhayamapoḍhāḥ senā abhītvarīriti gārhapatyādudīco 'ṅgārānnirūhya vyantāngārhapatyena kṛtvā sagrā sthetyabhimantrya japatyagnaya ādityaṃ gṛhṇāmyahne rātrimiti sāyam /
6.5.6.a.d: धृष्टिरसि ब्रह्म यच्छेत्युपवेषमादाय भूतकृत स्थापोढं जन्यं भयमपोढाः सेना अभीत्वरीरिति गार्हपत्यादुदीचो ऽङ्गारान्निरूह्य व्यन्तान्गार्हपत्येन कृत्वा सग्रा स्थेत्यभिमन्त्र्य जपत्यग्नय आदित्यं गृह्णाम्यह्ने रात्रिमिति सायम् ।
6.5.6.a.m: Taking the fire-shovel with: "You are the poker; bestow sacred power," having drawn out glowing coals toward the north from the gārhapatya with: "You are the performers of good deeds; pushed away is the peril caused by strangers; pushed away are the attacking armies," having placed them separate from the gārhapatya, and having addressed them with: "You are of the community," he mutters in the evening: "For Agni I take the sun, for the day the night."

6.5.6.b.m: In the morning: "For the sun I take Agni, for the night the day."

6.5.7.a.s: iḍāyāḥ padaṃ ghṛtavaccarācaraṃ jātavedo haviridaṃ juṣasva /
6.5.7.a.d: इडायाः पदं घृतवच्चराचरं जातवेदो हविरिदं जुषस्व ।
6.5.7.a.m: "The step of Iḍā, rich in ghee, moving and unmoving, O Jātavedas, enjoy this oblation

6.5.7.b.s: ye grāmyāḥ paśavo viśvarūpā virūpāsteṣāṃ saptānāmiha rantirastu /
6.5.7.b.d: ये ग्राम्याः पशवो विश्वरूपा विरूपास्तेषां सप्तानामिह रन्तिरस्तु ।
6.5.7.b.m: Whichever domestic animals of all kinds and diverse forms there are, may those seven find pleasure here

6.5.7.c.m: For increase of wealth, for good offspring, for good valour"—with these words he sets the agnihotra [milk] on those [coals].

6.6.1.b.d: न सुशृतं कुर्याद्रेतः कूलयेन्नो ऽशृतमन्तरेवैव स्यात्
6.6.1.b.m: He should not make it fully cooked, [lest] he burn the semen; nor should it be uncooked; it should be just in between.

6.6.3.a.m: Having caused the bubbles to cease, [water] is to be poured in.

6.6.4.a.s: apratiṣekyaṃ syāt tejaskāmasya brahmavarcasakāmasya pāpmānaṃ tustūrṣamāṇasyātho sarvebhyaḥ kāmebhyo 'tho yaḥ kāmayeta vīro ma ājāyeteti
6.6.4.a.d: अप्रतिषेक्यं स्यात् तेजस्कामस्य ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य पाप्मानं तुस्तूर्षमाणस्याथो सर्वेभ्यः कामेभ्यो ऽथो यः कामयेत वीरो म आजायेतेति
6.6.4.a.m: It should not have [water] poured into it for one who desires lustre, for one who desires sacred splendour, for one wishing to overcome evil, as well as for all [other] desires, and for one who desires: "May a heroic son be born to me."

6.6.6.a.s: adabdhena tvā cakṣuṣāvekṣa iti tṛṇena jvalatāvekṣate
6.6.6.a.d: अदब्धेन त्वा चक्षुषावेक्ष इति तृणेन ज्वलतावेक्षते
6.6.6.a.m: He inspects it with a burning grass blade, saying: "I inspect you with an undeceiving eye."

6.6.7.a.s: dohanasaṃkṣālanaṃ sruva ānīya haraste mā vinaiṣamiti tena pratiṣiñcaty apāṃ vā stokena
6.6.7.a.d: दोहनसंक्षालनं स्रुव आनीय हरस्ते मा विनैषमिति तेन प्रतिषिञ्चत्य् अपां वा स्तोकेन
6.6.7.a.m: Having poured the wash-water of the milking vessel into the sruva, he pours it in with: "May I not take away your heat," or with a drop of water.

6.6.8.a.s: udbhava sthodahaṃ prajayā pra paśubhirbhūyāsaṃ haraste mā vigādudyansuvargo lokastriṣu lokeṣu rocayeti punarevāvekṣyāntaritaṃ rakṣo 'ntaritā arātayo 'pahatā vyṛddhirapahataṃ pāpaṃ karmāpahataṃ pāpasya pāpakṛtaḥ pāpaṃ karma yo naḥ pāpaṃ karma cikīrṣati pratyagenamṛccheti triḥ paryagnikṛtvā gharmo 'si rāyaspoṣavanirihorjaṃ dṛṃheti vartma kruvan prāgudvāsayatyudak prāgudagvā
6.6.8.a.d: उद्भव स्थोदहं प्रजया प्र पशुभिर्भूयासं हरस्ते मा विगादुद्यन्सुवर्गो लोकस्त्रिषु लोकेषु रोचयेति पुनरेवावेक्ष्यान्तरितं रक्षो ऽन्तरिता अरातयो ऽपहता व्यृद्धिरपहतं पापं कर्मापहतं पापस्य पापकृतः पापं कर्म यो नः पापं कर्म चिकीर्षति प्रत्यगेनमृच्छेति त्रिः पर्यग्निकृत्वा घर्मो ऽसि रायस्पोषवनिरिहोर्जं दृंहेति वर्त्म क्रुवन् प्रागुद्वासयत्युदक् प्रागुदग्वा
6.6.8.a.m: Saying: "You are originators; may I increase in offspring and cattle; may your heat not depart; rising, shine in the heavenly world, in the three worlds," having inspected it again, and having moved a firebrand three times around it with: "Warded off is the demon, warded off are the foes, smitten is failure, smitten is the evil deed, smitten is the evil deed of the evil evildoer; whoever wishes to do an evil deed to us, may he meet it head-on," he moves it off [the coals] toward the east, north-east, or north, making a path [in the ashes] with: "You are the hot drink, possessing increase of wealth; strengthen refreshment here."

6.6.10.a.s: iha prajāṃ paśūndṛṃheti trirbhūmau pratiṣṭhāpya subhūtakṛta stha pratyūḍhaṃ janyaṃ bhayaṃ pratyūḍhāḥ senā abhītvarīriti gārhapatye 'ṅgārān pratyūhya
6.6.10.a.d: इह प्रजां पशून्दृंहेति त्रिर्भूमौ प्रतिष्ठाप्य सुभूतकृत स्थ प्रत्यूढं जन्यं भयं प्रत्यूढाः सेना अभीत्वरीरिति गार्हपत्ये ऽङ्गारान् प्रत्यूह्य
6.6.10.a.m: Having set it down three times on the ground with: "Strengthen offspring and cattle here," and having pushed back the coals into the gārhapatya with: "You are the performers of good deeds; driven back is the peril caused by strangers; driven back are the attacking armies,"

6.7.1.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti sruksruvam ādāya pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātaya ityāhavanīye gārhapatye vā pratitapyāriṣṭo yajamānaḥ patnī ceti saṃmṛśya hiraṇyayaṣṭirasyamṛtapalāśā sroto yajñānāmityagnihotrahavaṇīmabhimantryomunneṣyāmi havyaṃ devebhyaḥ pāpmano yajamānamiti sāyamāha /
6.7.1.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति स्रुक्स्रुवम् आदाय प्रत्युष्टं रक्षः प्रत्युष्टा अरातय इत्याहवनीये गार्हपत्ये वा प्रतितप्यारिष्टो यजमानः पत्नी चेति संमृश्य हिरण्ययष्टिरस्यमृतपलाशा स्रोतो यज्ञानामित्यग्निहोत्रहवणीमभिमन्त्र्योमुन्नेष्यामि हव्यं देवेभ्यः पाप्मनो यजमानमिति सायमाह ।
6.7.1.a.m: having taken the sruc and sruva with: "At the impulse of divine Savitṛ," having heated them at the āhavanīya or at the gārhapatya with: "Scorched is the demon, scorched are the foes," having touched them with: "Uninjured be the sacrificer and his wife," and having addressed the agnihotra ladle with: "You are a golden staff, with leaves of immortality, the stream of sacrifices," he says in the evening: "Om, I shall draw out the oblation for the gods, [and] the sacrificer from evil."

6.7.2.a.s: havirdevānāmasi mṛtyorme 'bhayaṃ svasti me 'stvabhayaṃ me astvityupāṃśūktvomunnayetyuccairanujānāti /
6.7.2.a.d: हविर्देवानामसि मृत्योर्मे ऽभयं स्वस्ति मे ऽस्त्वभयं मे अस्त्वित्युपांशूक्त्वोमुन्नयेत्युच्चैरनुजानाति ।
6.7.2.a.m: Having said in a low voice: "You are the oblation of the gods; my fearlessness from death; may well-being be mine, may fearlessness be mine," he permits aloud with: "Om, draw it out."

6.7.2.b.m: In the absence of the sacrificer, [the adhvaryu] himself should give permission to himself.

6.7.3.a.s: unnīyamāna ubau vācaṃ yacchata ā homāt
6.7.3.a.d: उन्नीयमान उबौ वाचं यच्छत आ होमात्
6.7.3.a.m: While it is being drawn out, both restrain their speech until the oblation.

6.7.4.a.m: And the sacrificer does not close his eyes and stands.

6.7.7.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta putrāṇāmayamṛdhnuyāditi taṃ prati pūrṇamunnayet
6.7.7.a.d: यं कामयेत पुत्राणामयमृध्नुयादिति तं प्रति पूर्णमुन्नयेत्
6.7.7.a.m: Whichever of his sons he wishes: "May this one prosper," for him he should draw out a full ladleful.

6.7.8.a.s: yadi kāmayeta jyeṣṭhato 'sya prajārdhukā syāditi pūrṇaṃ prathamamunnayettata ūnataramūnataram /
6.7.8.a.d: यदि कामयेत ज्येष्ठतो ऽस्य प्रजार्धुका स्यादिति पूर्णं प्रथममुन्नयेत्तत ऊनतरमूनतरम् ।
6.7.8.a.m: If he wishes that his offspring should prosper starting from the eldest, he should draw out the first ladleful full, and then each subsequent one less and less.

6.7.8.b.m: Starting from the youngest, this is reversed.

6.7.8.c.m: If all [are to be] of equal vigour, [he draws out] equal amounts.

6.7.9.a.m: In the regular ritual, he draws it out as it comes to hand.

6.8.1.a.s: agnaye ca tvā pṛthivyai connayāmīti prathamaṃ vāyave ca tvāntarikṣāya ceti dvitīyaṃ sūryāya ca tvā dive ceti tṛtīyaṃ candramase ca tvā nakṣatrebhyaśceti caturtham
6.8.1.a.d: अग्नये च त्वा पृथिव्यै चोन्नयामीति प्रथमं वायवे च त्वान्तरिक्षाय चेति द्वितीयं सूर्याय च त्वा दिवे चेति तृतीयं चन्द्रमसे च त्वा नक्षत्रेभ्यश्चेति चतुर्थम्
6.8.1.a.m: [He draws out] the first with: "I draw you out for Agni and the earth," the second with: "For Vāyu and the atmosphere," the third with: "For Sūrya and the sky," and the fourth with: "For Candramas and the constellations."

6.8.2.a.m: For descendants of Jamadagni, a fifth with: "And for the waters and the plants."

6.8.3.a.s: bhūriḍā bhuva iḍā suvariḍā karadiḍā pṛthigiḍeti vā pratimantram
6.8.3.a.d: भूरिडा भुव इडा सुवरिडा करदिडा पृथिगिडेति वा प्रतिमन्त्रम्
6.8.3.a.m: Or [he draws it out] with the respective formulas: "Bhūḥ-iḍā, Bhuvaḥ-iḍā, Suvar-iḍā, Kara-iḍā, Pṛthak-iḍā."

6.8.4.a.s: paśūnme yacchetyapareṇa gārhapatyamunnayanadeśe 'bhitarāṃ vā sādayitvā gārhapatye hastaṃ pratāpya saṃmṛśati sajūrdevaiḥ sāyaṃyāvabhiḥ sāyaṃyāvāno devāḥ svasti saṃpārayantu paśubhiḥ saṃpṛcīya prajāṃ dṛṃheti sāyam /
6.8.4.a.d: पशून्मे यच्छेत्यपरेण गार्हपत्यमुन्नयनदेशे ऽभितरां वा सादयित्वा गार्हपत्ये हस्तं प्रताप्य संमृशति सजूर्देवैः सायंयावभिः सायंयावानो देवाः स्वस्ति संपारयन्तु पशुभिः संपृचीय प्रजां दृंहेति सायम् ।
6.8.4.a.m: Having placed [the ladle] to the west of the gārhapatya at the drawing place or further inward with: "Bestow cattle upon me," and having warmed his hand at the gārhapatya, he touches [the ladle] in the evening with: "Together with the gods who go in the evening; may the gods who go in the evening bring about well-being; may I be united with cattle; strengthen the offspring."

6.8.4.b.s: sajūrdevaiḥ prātaryāvabhiḥ prātaryāvāṇo devāḥ svasti saṃpārayantu paśubhiḥ saṃpṛcīya prajāṃ dṛṃheti prātaḥ
6.8.4.b.d: सजूर्देवैः प्रातर्यावभिः प्रातर्यावाणो देवाः स्वस्ति संपारयन्तु पशुभिः संपृचीय प्रजां दृंहेति प्रातः
6.8.4.b.m: In the morning with: "Together with the gods who go in the morning; may the gods who go in the morning bring about well-being; may I be united with cattle; strengthen the offspring."

6.8.5.a.s: daśahotrā cābhimṛśya pālāśīṃ samidhaṃ prādeśamātrīmupari dhārayangārhapatyasya samayārcirharati
6.8.5.a.d: दशहोत्रा चाभिमृश्य पालाशीं समिधं प्रादेशमात्रीमुपरि धारयन्गार्हपत्यस्य समयार्चिर्हरति
6.8.5.a.m: And having touched it with the daśahotṛ formula, holding a palāśa kindling-stick a span long over it, he carries it past the flame of the gārhapatya.

6.8.6.a.m: He steps forward with: "Traverse the wide intermediate space."

6.8.7.a.m: While stepping forward, he recites the daśahotṛ formula.

6.8.9.a.m: At the middle region, he lowers it with: "Svāhā to Agni Vaiśvānara."

6.8.11.a.s: upapreta saṃyatadhvaṃ māntargāta bhaginaṃ bhāgadheyātsaptarṣīṇāṃ sukṛtāṃ yatra lokastatremaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ ca dhehy upapratnamupa bhūrbhuvaḥ suvarāyurme yacchetyapareṇāhavanīyaṃ darbheṣu sādayati
6.8.11.a.d: उपप्रेत संयतध्वं मान्तर्गात भगिनं भागधेयात्सप्तर्षीणां सुकृतां यत्र लोकस्तत्रेमं यज्ञं यजमानं च धेह्य् उपप्रत्नमुप भूर्भुवः सुवरायुर्मे यच्छेत्यपरेणाहवनीयं दर्भेषु सादयति
6.8.11.a.m: With: "Approach, unite yourselves; do not exclude him who has a portion from his share; where the world of the seven sages, the performers of good deeds, is, there place this sacrifice and the sacrificer; approach the ancient one, approach; bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar; bestow life upon me," he sets it down on darbha grass to the west of the āhavanīya.

6.9.1.a.m: "When it is offered while the fire is being carried forward, it is offered to the Vasus

6.9.1.b.m: When it lies smoking, [it is offered] to the Rudras

6.9.1.c.m: When the flame reaches the first firewood stick, [it is offered] to the Ādityas

6.9.1.d.s: sarva eva sarvaśa idhma ādīpto bhavati viśveṣu deveṣu /
6.9.1.d.d: सर्व एव सर्वश इध्म आदीप्तो भवति विश्वेषु देवेषु ।
6.9.1.d.m: When the firewood is completely ablaze on all sides, [it is offered] to the Viśve Devas /"

6.9.1.e.m: When the flame goes down and becomes reddish, as it were, it is offered to Indra.

6.9.1.f.d: अङ्गारा भवन्ति तेभ्यो ऽङ्गारेभ्यो ऽर्चिरुदेति प्रजापतावेव ।
6.9.1.f.m: When there are coals and from those coals a flame rises up, it is [offered] to Prajāpati himself.

6.9.1.g.s: śro 'ṅgārā adhyūhante tato nīlopakāśo 'rcirudeti brahmaṇi hutaṃ bhavati
6.9.1.g.d: श्रो ऽङ्गारा अध्यूहन्ते ततो नीलोपकाशो ऽर्चिरुदेति ब्रह्मणि हुतं भवति
6.9.1.g.m: When coals are heaped up and then a flame with a bluish sheen rises up, it is offered to Brahman.

6.9.2.a.s: yadaṅgāreṣu vyavaśānteṣu lelāyadvīva bhāti taddevānāmāsyaṃ tasmāt tathā hotavyaṃ yathāsye 'pidadhātyevaṃ taditi vijñāyate
6.9.2.a.d: यदङ्गारेषु व्यवशान्तेषु लेलायद्वीव भाति तद्देवानामास्यं तस्मात् तथा होतव्यं यथास्ये ऽपिदधात्येवं तदिति विज्ञायते
6.9.2.a.m: “When the coals have died down and it shines, flickering as it were, that is the mouth of the gods; therefore one should offer in such a way, just as one places [food] into a mouth, like that it is,” thus it is known from the tradition.

6.9.3.a.s: vidyudasi vidya me pāpmānamṛtātsatyamupaimīti hoṣyannapa upaspṛśya pālāśīṃ samidhamādadhātyekāṃ dve tisro vā
6.9.3.a.d: विद्युदसि विद्य मे पाप्मानमृतात्सत्यमुपैमीति होष्यन्नप उपस्पृश्य पालाशीं समिधमादधात्येकां द्वे तिस्रो वा
6.9.3.a.m: About to offer, he touches water with the words: “You are lightning; strike away my evil; from non-truth I approach truth,” and puts on a firewood stick of palāśa wood: one, two, or three.

6.9.4.b.s: hiraṇyayaṃ tvā vaṃśaṃ svargasya lokasya saṃkramaṇaṃ dadhāmīti dvitīyām /
6.9.4.b.d: हिरण्ययं त्वा वंशं स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य संक्रमणं दधामीति द्वितीयाम् ।
6.9.4.b.m: With: “I place you as a golden beam, a stepping-stone to the heavenly world,” the second.

6.9.4.c.s: rajatāṃ tvā haritagarbhāmagnijyotiṣamakṣitiṃ kāmadughāṃ svargyāṃ svargāya lokāya rātrimiṣṭakāmupadadhe tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdeti sāyaṃ tṛtīyām /
6.9.4.c.d: रजतां त्वा हरितगर्भामग्निज्योतिषमक्षितिं कामदुघां स्वर्ग्यां स्वर्गाय लोकाय रात्रिमिष्टकामुपदधे तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेति सायं तृतीयाम् ।
6.9.4.c.m: In the evening, the third with: “You of silver, with a golden womb, whose light is fire, imperishable, milking desires, leading to heaven, I place as the night-brick for the heavenly world; through that deity, in the manner of the Aṅgirases, sit firm.”

6.9.4.d.s: hariṇīṃ tvā rajatagarbhāṃ sūryajyotiṣamakṣitiṃ kāmadughāṃ svargyāṃ svargāya lokāyāhariṣṭakāmupadadha iti prātaḥ
6.9.4.d.d: हरिणीं त्वा रजतगर्भां सूर्यज्योतिषमक्षितिं कामदुघां स्वर्ग्यां स्वर्गाय लोकायाहरिष्टकामुपदध इति प्रातः
6.9.4.d.m: In the morning with: “You of gold, with a silver womb, whose light is the sun, imperishable, milking desires, leading to heaven, I place as the day-brick for the heavenly world.”

6.10.1.a.s: samidhamādhāya prāṇyāpānya nimīlya vīkṣya hutvā dhyāyedyatkāmaḥ syāt
6.10.1.a.d: समिधमाधाय प्राण्यापान्य निमील्य वीक्ष्य हुत्वा ध्यायेद्यत्कामः स्यात्
6.10.1.a.m: Having put on the firewood stick, breathing in and out, closing his eyes and opening them, having offered, he should meditate on whatever he may desire.

6.10.2.a.m: Having offered, he looks intently at the great [fire].

6.10.3.a.s: ādīptāyāṃ juhoti śyāvāyāṃ vā yadā vā samatītārcirlelāyatīva /
6.10.3.a.d: आदीप्तायां जुहोति श्यावायां वा यदा वा समतीतार्चिर्लेलायतीव ।
6.10.3.a.m: He offers when it is blazing, or when it has turned dark brown, or when the flame, having passed away, flickers as it were.

6.10.3.b.m: When it is smoking, for one who desires a village; when it is flaming, for one who desires spiritual luster; upon coals, for one who desires splendor.

6.10.4.a.m: He offers on the firewood stick two angulas from the base.

6.10.5.a.m: He offers stepping forward in the evening, stepping backward in the morning;

6.10.6.a.m: or stepping forward in both cases.

6.10.7.a.m: About to offer, he whispers: “Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ.”

6.10.8.a.m: In the evening he offers the agnihotra with: “Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā.”

6.10.8.b.m: In the morning with: “Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā.”

6.10.9.a.m: Or the combined offering: in the evening with: “Agni is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā;”

6.10.9.b.m: in the morning with: “Sūrya is light, light is Agni, svāhā.”

6.10.10.a.s: iṣe tveti sruṅmukhādavācīnaṃ sāyaṃ lepamavamārṣṭyūrje tveti /
6.10.10.a.d: इषे त्वेति स्रुङ्मुखादवाचीनं सायं लेपमवमार्ष्ट्यूर्जे त्वेति ।
6.10.10.a.m: With: “For vigor, you,” in the evening he wipes off the smear downwards from the tip of the ladle; with: “For strength, you,”

6.10.11.a.s: oṣadhībhyastvauṣadhīrjinveti barhiṣi lepaṃ nimṛjya varco me yaccheti srucaṃ sādayitvāgne gṛhapate mā mā saṃtāpsīrātmannamṛtamadhiṣi prajā jyotiradbdhena tvā cakṣuṣā pratīkṣa iti gārhapatyaṃ pratīkṣya bhūrbhuvaḥ suvarityuttarāmāhutiṃ purvārdhe samidhi juhoti tūṣṇīṃ vā
6.10.11.a.d: ओषधीभ्यस्त्वौषधीर्जिन्वेति बर्हिषि लेपं निमृज्य वर्चो मे यच्छेति स्रुचं सादयित्वाग्ने गृहपते मा मा संताप्सीरात्मन्नमृतमधिषि प्रजा ज्योतिरद्ब्धेन त्वा चक्षुषा प्रतीक्ष इति गार्हपत्यं प्रतीक्ष्य भूर्भुवः सुवरित्युत्तरामाहुतिं पुर्वार्धे समिधि जुहोति तूष्णीं वा
6.10.11.a.m: Having wiped the smear on the sacrificial grass with: “To the plants, you; enliven the plants,” having placed down the ladle with: “Grant me luster,” having looked toward the gārhapatya with: “O Agni, lord of the house, do not burn me up; I place immortality in myself, offspring, light; with uninjured eye I gaze upon you,” he offers the second oblation on the firewood stick in the eastern half with: “Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ,” or silently.

6.10.12.a.m: “One should not offer upon the firewood stick,” say some.

6.11.1.a.m: Having offered the larger second oblation, he leaves behind more for eating.

6.11.2.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyānsyāditi bhūyastasya pūrvaṃ hutvottaraṃ kanīyo juhuyāt
6.11.2.a.d: यं कामयेत पापीयान्स्यादिति भूयस्तस्य पूर्वं हुत्वोत्तरं कनीयो जुहुयात्
6.11.2.a.m: For whomsoever he might wish that he should become worse off, he should offer more of his first oblation and offer less as the second.

6.11.3.a.s: hutvā srucamudgṛhya rudra mṛḍānārbhava mṛḍa dhūrta namaste astu paśupate trāyasvainamiti triḥ srucāgnimudañcamativalgayati
6.11.3.a.d: हुत्वा स्रुचमुद्गृह्य रुद्र मृडानार्भव मृड धूर्त नमस्ते अस्तु पशुपते त्रायस्वैनमिति त्रिः स्रुचाग्निमुदञ्चमतिवल्गयति
6.11.3.a.m: Having offered, having lifted up the ladle, with: “O Rudra, be gracious; O son of Ṛbhu, be gracious; O Dhūrta, reverence be to you; O lord of animals, protect him,” he moves the ladle thrice northwards across the fire with a waving motion.

6.11.4.a.s: pūrvavallepamavamṛjya prācīnāvītī svadhā pitṛbhyaḥ pitṝñjinveti dakṣiṇena vediṃ bhumyāṃ lepaṃ nimṛjya prajāṃ me yaccheti srucaṃ sādayitvā vṛṣṭirasi vṛśca me pāpmānamṛtātsatyamupāgāmiti hutvāpa upaspṛśyāntarvedi sruk /
6.11.4.a.d: पूर्ववल्लेपमवमृज्य प्राचीनावीती स्वधा पितृभ्यः पितॄञ्जिन्वेति दक्षिणेन वेदिं भुम्यां लेपं निमृज्य प्रजां मे यच्छेति स्रुचं सादयित्वा वृष्टिरसि वृश्च मे पाप्मानमृतात्सत्यमुपागामिति हुत्वाप उपस्पृश्यान्तर्वेदि स्रुक् ।
6.11.4.a.m: Having wiped off the smear as before, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, having wiped the smear on the ground south of the altar ground with: “Svadhā to the ancestors; enliven the ancestors,” having placed down the ladle with: “Grant me offspring,” having offered, having touched water with: “You are rain; cut off my evil; from non-truth I have approached truth,” the ladle [remains] inside the altar ground.

6.11.4.b.s: athāṅgulyāpādāya pūṣāsīti lepaṃ praśnātyaśabdaṃ kurvannatihāya dataḥ
6.11.4.b.d: अथाङ्गुल्यापादाय पूषासीति लेपं प्रश्नात्यशब्दं कुर्वन्नतिहाय दतः
6.11.4.b.m: Then, taking [the smear] with his finger, he eats the smear with: “You are Pūṣan,” making no sound, bypassing his teeth.

6.11.5.a.s: apa ācamyaivaṃ punaḥ pāśyācamya barhiṣopayamyodaṅṅāvṛtyotsṛpya garbhebhyastvā garbhānprīṇīhyāgneyaṃ haviḥ prajānanaṃ me astu daśavīraṃ sarvagaṇaṃ svastaye /
6.11.5.a.d: अप आचम्यैवं पुनः पाश्याचम्य बर्हिषोपयम्योदङ्ङावृत्योत्सृप्य गर्भेभ्यस्त्वा गर्भान्प्रीणीह्याग्नेयं हविः प्रजाननं मे अस्तु दशवीरं सर्वगणं स्वस्तये ।
6.11.5.a.m: Having sipped water, having eaten again in this same manner, having sipped water, supporting [the ladle] with sacrificial grass, turning to the north, creeping forward: “To the embryos, you; satisfy the embryos; let the offering to Agni be generative for me, with ten heroes, with a whole troop, for well-being;”

6.11.5.b.m: “winning self, winning offspring, winning cattle, winning security, winning the world, winning rain;”

6.11.5.c.s: agniḥ prajāṃ bahulāṃ me karotvannaṃ payo reto asmāsu dhehi /
6.11.5.c.d: अग्निः प्रजां बहुलां मे करोत्वन्नं पयो रेतो अस्मासु धेहि ।
6.11.5.c.m: “may Agni make my offspring abundant; place food, milk, seed in us;”

6.11.5.d.m: “may he uphold increase of wealth, vigor, strength in us, svāhā” — with [these mantras] he sips from the ladle whose handle points north or points east.

6.12.1.a.m: In the morning he modifies the mantra to: “the offering to Sūrya.”

6.12.2.a.s: dviḥ srucaṃ nirlihyādbhiḥ pūrayitvocchiṣṭabhājo jinveti parācīnaṃ ninīyācamyāgreṇāhavanīyaṃ darbhairagnihotrahavaṇīṃ prakṣālayati
6.12.2.a.d: द्विः स्रुचं निर्लिह्याद्भिः पूरयित्वोच्छिष्टभाजो जिन्वेति पराचीनं निनीयाचम्याग्रेणाहवनीयं दर्भैरग्निहोत्रहवणीं प्रक्षालयति
6.12.2.a.m: Having licked the ladle twice, having filled it with water, having poured it out backwards with: “Enliven those who share in the remnants,” having sipped water, he washes the agnihotra-ladle in front of the āhavanīya with darbha grass.

6.12.3.a.s: na māmsadhautasya devā bhuñjata iti vijñāyate
6.12.3.a.d: न माम्सधौतस्य देवा भुञ्जत इति विज्ञायते
6.12.3.a.m: “The gods do not consume what has been washed with flesh [of the hand],” thus it is known from the tradition.

6.12.4.a.s: adbhiḥ srucaṃ pūrayitvā sarpebhyastvā sarpāñjinveti pratidiśaṃ vyutsicya sarpānpipīlikā jinva sarpetarajanāñjinva sarpadevajanāñjinveti tisraḥ sruca utsicya caturthīṃ pūrayitvā pṛthivyāmamṛtaṃ juhomi svāhetyapareṇāhavanīyaṃ ninīya śeṣaṃ patnyā añjalau gṛhebhyastvā gṛhāñjinveti
6.12.4.a.d: अद्भिः स्रुचं पूरयित्वा सर्पेभ्यस्त्वा सर्पाञ्जिन्वेति प्रतिदिशं व्युत्सिच्य सर्पान्पिपीलिका जिन्व सर्पेतरजनाञ्जिन्व सर्पदेवजनाञ्जिन्वेति तिस्रः स्रुच उत्सिच्य चतुर्थीं पूरयित्वा पृथिव्याममृतं जुहोमि स्वाहेत्यपरेणाहवनीयं निनीय शेषं पत्न्या अञ्जलौ गृहेभ्यस्त्वा गृहाञ्जिन्वेति
6.12.4.a.m: Having filled the ladle with water, having poured it out in each direction with: “To the serpents, you; enliven the serpents,” having poured out three ladlefuls with: “Enliven the ants, enliven the serpents and other folk, enliven the serpent-godfolk,” having filled a fourth, having poured it out to the west of the āhavanīya with: “I offer immortality upon the earth, svāhā,” he [pours] the remainder into the folded hands of the wife with: “To the houses, you; enliven the houses.”

6.12.5.a.s: yadi patnī nānuṣyāddevānāṃ patnībhyo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi svāheti patnyāyatane ninayet
6.12.5.a.d: यदि पत्नी नानुष्याद्देवानां पत्नीभ्यो ऽमृतं जुहोमि स्वाहेति पत्न्यायतने निनयेत्
6.12.5.a.m: If the wife should not be present, he should pour it out in the place of the wife with: “I offer immortality to the wives of the gods, svāhā.”

6.12.6.a.s: aparaṃ srucyānīya vipruṣāṃ śāntirasītyunnayanadeśe ninīyāhavanīye srucaṃ pratāpya hasto 'vadheyo hasto vā pratāpya srucyavadheyaḥ
6.12.6.a.d: अपरं स्रुच्यानीय विप्रुषां शान्तिरसीत्युन्नयनदेशे निनीयाहवनीये स्रुचं प्रताप्य हस्तो ऽवधेयो हस्तो वा प्रताप्य स्रुच्यवधेयः
6.12.6.a.m: Having brought more [water] into the ladle, having poured it out at the spot of the drawing out with: “You are the appeasement of drops,” having heated the ladle at the āhavanīya, the hand is to be inserted, or having heated the hand, it is to be inserted into the ladle.

6.12.7.a.m: With it he points northward with: “To the Seven Ṛṣis, you; enliven the Seven Ṛṣis.”

6.13.1.a.s: agne gṛhapate pariṣadya juṣasva svāheti sruveṇa gārhapatye juhotyekāṃ dve tisraśacatasro vā
6.13.1.a.d: अग्ने गृहपते परिषद्य जुषस्व स्वाहेति स्रुवेण गार्हपत्ये जुहोत्येकां द्वे तिस्रशचतस्रो वा
6.13.1.a.m: With the dipping spoon he offers into the gārhapatya with: “O Agni, lord of the house, being seated around, enjoy, svāhā”: one, two, three, or four [oblations].

6.13.2.a.s: agnaye gṛhapataye rayipataye puṣṭipataye kāmāyānnādyāya svāhetyetāmeke samāmananti
6.13.2.a.d: अग्नये गृहपतये रयिपतये पुष्टिपतये कामायान्नाद्याय स्वाहेत्येतामेके समामनन्ति
6.13.2.a.m: Some teach this [mantra]: “To Agni, lord of the house, lord of wealth, lord of nourishment, to desire, to the eating of food, svāhā.”

6.13.4.a.s: agne 'dābhya pariṣadya juṣasva svāheti sruveṇānvāhāryapacane juhotyekāṃ dve tisraścatasro vā
6.13.4.a.d: अग्ने ऽदाभ्य परिषद्य जुषस्व स्वाहेति स्रुवेणान्वाहार्यपचने जुहोत्येकां द्वे तिस्रश्चतस्रो वा
6.13.4.a.m: With the dipping spoon he offers into the anvāhāryapacana with: “O Agni, undeceived, being seated around, enjoy, svāhā”: one, two, three, or four [oblations].

6.13.5.a.m: The second with: “O lord of food, give us food.”

6.13.6.a.m: Or, without having consumed [the remnant], he should offer in the other two [fires].

6.13.7.a.m: The offering is in the āhavanīya, not in the other two.

6.13.8.a.m: “If, having offered in the āhavanīya, he were to offer in the other two, it would be just as if one were to descend from the heavenly world,” thus it is known from the tradition.

6.13.9.a.m: Or all these [fires] are established for the sake of offerings.

6.13.9.b.s: catasro gārhapatye juhoti catasro 'nvāhāryapacane dve āhavanīye /
6.13.9.b.d: चतस्रो गार्हपत्ये जुहोति चतस्रो ऽन्वाहार्यपचने द्वे आहवनीये ।
6.13.9.b.m: He offers four in the gārhapatya, four in the anvāhāryapacana, two in the āhavanīya.

6.13.9.d.s: daśākṣarā virāḍvirājā yajñaḥ saṃmita iti bahvṛcabrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati
6.13.9.d.d: दशाक्षरा विराड्विराजा यज्ञः संमित इति बह्वृचब्राह्मणं भवति
6.13.9.d.m: “The virāj has ten syllables; the sacrifice is commensurate with the virāj,” thus says a Rigvedic Brāhmaṇa.

6.13.10.a.m: “Shine, you shine, he has shone” — this is handed down as the kindling up of the fire.

6.13.11.a.s: dīdihi dīdidāsi dīdāya dīdyāsaṃ dīdyasveti vā pratimantram
6.13.11.a.d: दीदिहि दीदिदासि दीदाय दीद्यासं दीद्यस्वेति वा प्रतिमन्त्रम्
6.13.11.a.m: Or with each mantra: “Shine, you shine, he has shone, may I shine, do shine!”

6.13.12.a.m: According to the order in which they were established, or proceeding from the āhavanīya.

6.14.1.a.m: he sprinkles around the fires as before;

6.14.2.a.s: apipreragne svāṃ tanvamayāḍ dyāvāpṛthivī ūrjamasmāsu dhehītyagnihotrasthālyāṃ tṛṇamaṅktvānupraharati
6.14.2.a.d: अपिप्रेरग्ने स्वां तन्वमयाड् द्यावापृथिवी ऊर्जमस्मासु धेहीत्यग्निहोत्रस्थाल्यां तृणमङ्क्त्वानुप्रहरति
6.14.2.a.m: Having anointed a blade of grass in the agnihotra pot, he throws it into the fire with: “You have pleased your own self, O Agni; you have sacrificed to Heaven and Earth; place strength in us.”

6.14.3.a.m: for that is the completion of the agnihotra.

6.14.4.b.m: for it is stated: 'This sacrifice, namely the agnihotra, is uncompleted.'

6.14.5.a.m: Having rinsed the agnihotra vessel, he pours [the wash-water] out at the place of ladling with: 'The inexhaustible I sacrifice for inexhaustibility, svāhā.'

6.14.6.a.s: vṛṣṭirasi vṛśca me pāpmānamṛtātsatyamupāgāmapsu śraddhetyapa ācamya yajamāno 'ntarvedi mārjayate 'nnādāḥ sthānnādo bhūyāsaṃ yaśaḥ stha yaśasvī bhūyāsaṃ śraddhā stha śraddhiṣīyeti
6.14.6.a.d: वृष्टिरसि वृश्च मे पाप्मानमृतात्सत्यमुपागामप्सु श्रद्धेत्यप आचम्य यजमानो ऽन्तर्वेदि मार्जयते ऽन्नादाः स्थान्नादो भूयासं यशः स्थ यशस्वी भूयासं श्रद्धा स्थ श्रद्धिषीयेति
6.14.6.a.m: Having sipped water with: 'You are rain; cut off my evil; from truth I have reached reality; in the waters is faith,' the sacrificer sprinkles himself inside the altar ground with: 'You are food-eaters, may I become a food-eater; you are fame, may I become famous; you are faith, may I have faith.'

6.14.7.a.s: āpo ha śleṣma prathamaṃ saṃbabhūva yena dhṛto varuṇo yena mitraḥ /
6.14.7.a.d: आपो ह श्लेष्म प्रथमं संबभूव येन धृतो वरुणो येन मित्रः ।
6.14.7.a.m: 'The waters indeed arose first as the fluid by which Varuṇa is sustained, by which Mitra,'

6.14.7.b.s: yenendraṃ devā abhyaṣiñcanta rājyāya tenāhaṃ māmabhiṣiñcāmi varcasa iti śirasyapa ānayate
6.14.7.b.d: येनेन्द्रं देवा अभ्यषिञ्चन्त राज्याय तेनाहं मामभिषिञ्चामि वर्चस इति शिरस्यप आनयते
6.14.7.b.m: 'by which the gods consecrated Indra for sovereignty; by that I consecrate myself with splendour'—with this he pours water upon his head.

6.14.8.a.m: For one desirous of cattle, he should sacrifice with the milk of two [cows].

6.14.9.a.m: He milks the first into the agnihotra pot;

6.14.10.a.m: Having put the first on the fire, he pours the second into it.

6.14.11.a.s: yasya rudraḥ paśūñchamāyetaitayaivāvṛtā dvayoḥ payasā sāyaṃprātarjuhuyāt
6.14.11.a.d: यस्य रुद्रः पशूञ्छमायेतैतयैवावृता द्वयोः पयसा सायंप्रातर्जुहुयात्
6.14.11.a.m: For one whose cattle Rudra strikes down, he should sacrifice evening and morning with the milk of two [cows] following this very procedure.

6.14.12.a.s: taccedatihanyātsajūrjātavedo diva ā pṛthivyā asya haviṣo ghṛtasya vīhi svāheti sāyaṃprātarājyena juhuyāt
6.14.12.a.d: तच्चेदतिहन्यात्सजूर्जातवेदो दिव आ पृथिव्या अस्य हविषो घृतस्य वीहि स्वाहेति सायंप्रातराज्येन जुहुयात्
6.14.12.a.m: If that should be too much, he should sacrifice with clarified butter evening and morning with: 'United, O Jātavedas, from heaven, from earth, partake of this offering of clarified butter, svāhā.'

6.14.13.a.s: anāramatyagne duḥśīrtatano juṣasva svāheti dvādaśāhamājyena hutvā tata ūrdhvaṃ na sūrkṣet
6.14.13.a.d: अनारमत्यग्ने दुःशीर्ततनो जुषस्व स्वाहेति द्वादशाहमाज्येन हुत्वा तत ऊर्ध्वं न सूर्क्षेत्
6.14.13.a.m: Having sacrificed with clarified butter for twelve days with: 'Unceasingly, O Agni of cold body, delight, svāhā,' beyond that he should take no further concern.

6.15.1.a.m: He should sacrifice with milk for one desirous of cattle, with curds for one desirous of sensory power, with barley gruel for one desirous of a village, with cooked rice for one desirous of food-sustenance, with rice-grains for one desirous of vigour;

6.15.1.c.m: with meat for one desirous of fame, with soma for one desirous of spiritual splendour, with clarified butter for one desirous of fiery energy.

6.15.2.a.m: He cooks the barley gruel with water to be poured in.

6.15.3.a.m: When it is cooked, he pours [water] in with a yajus formula.

6.15.5.a.m: He does not pour [water] into the clarified butter, [thinking]: 'Lest I take away your heat.'

6.15.5.b.m: He throws into it two tips of darbha grass, or one.

6.15.6.b.s: śṛtaṃ hi tanna pratiṣiñcati pratiṣiktaṃ hi tadātañcaneneti vijñāyate
6.15.6.b.d: शृतं हि तन्न प्रतिषिञ्चति प्रतिषिक्तं हि तदातञ्चनेनेति विज्ञायते
6.15.6.b.m: for it is [already] cooked; he does not pour [water] into it, for it is known [from scripture]: 'It is already poured into by means of the curdling agent.'

6.15.7.a.m: Likewise rice-grains, cooked rice, and soma.

6.15.8.a.s: ājyena taṇḍulair odanena somena vā juhuyād yasyāpratiṣekyaṃ syāt
6.15.8.a.d: आज्येन तण्डुलैर् ओदनेन सोमेन वा जुहुयाद् यस्याप्रतिषेक्यं स्यात्
6.15.8.a.m: He for whom the material does not require pouring-in should sacrifice with clarified butter, with rice-grains, with cooked rice, or with soma.

6.15.9.a.m: One desirous of fiery energy should sacrifice with clarified butter for a year, or for twelve days.

6.15.11.a.s: homakāle gṛhebhyo brāhmaṇāyānnaṃ prahiṇuyātteno haivāsya hutaṃ bhavati
6.15.11.a.d: होमकाले गृहेभ्यो ब्राह्मणायान्नं प्रहिणुयात्तेनो हैवास्य हुतं भवति
6.15.11.a.m: At the time of the oblation, [the kṣatriya] should send food from his house to a brahmin; through that indeed his oblation becomes offered.

6.15.12.a.m: He must regularly cause [him] to recite the veneration of the fires.

6.15.13.a.s: yo vā somayāji satyavādī tasya juhuyāt
6.15.13.a.d: यो वा सोमयाजि सत्यवादी तस्य जुहुयात्
6.15.13.a.m: Or he may sacrifice for one who is a soma-sacrificer and speaker of truth.

6.15.14.a.m: Day after day the sacrificer should himself offer the agnihotra,

6.15.16.a.s: brahmacārī vā juhuyādbrahmaṇā hi sa parikrīto bhavati /
6.15.16.a.d: ब्रह्मचारी वा जुहुयाद्ब्रह्मणा हि स परिक्रीतो भवति ।
6.15.16.a.m: Or a Vedic student may sacrifice, for he is bought with the sacred word;

6.15.16.b.s: kṣīrahotā vā juhuyāddhanena hi sa parikrīto bhavatīti bahvṛcabrāhmaṇam
6.15.16.b.d: क्षीरहोता वा जुहुयाद्धनेन हि स परिक्रीतो भवतीति बह्वृचब्राह्मणम्
6.15.16.b.m: or a milk-sacrificer may sacrifice, for he is bought with wealth—thus the Brāhmaṇa of the Ṛgveda states.

6.16.1.a.m: We shall explain the veneration of the fires.

6.16.2.a.m: When directed, 'he venerates', he should venerate the āhavanīya alone;

6.16.3.a.m: Having risen near the later oblation, he should venerate [the fire] standing somewhat obliquely,

6.16.4.a.m: with the six [verses beginning]: 'Advancing to the sacrifice.'

6.16.5.a.s: agnīṣomāvimaṃ su ma iti saptamyā pūrvapakṣe /
6.16.5.a.d: अग्नीषोमाविमं सु म इति सप्तम्या पूर्वपक्षे ।
6.16.5.a.m: In the bright fortnight, with the seventh [verse]: 'O Agni and Soma, this my [prayer]';
